## Mercedes-Benz G-Class (second generation) (2018–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/second-gen/
Codes: “W463A”, G 550, G 580

Verdict: Mercedes replaced almost everything except the silhouette and — astonishingly — the three locking differentials. Far better on the road, still serious off it, and now available with four electric motors that can spin it like a tank.

On 14 January 2018, at the Detroit auto show, Mercedes revealed a G-Class that looked almost exactly like the old one and was almost entirely new. It was 121 mm wider, 53 mm longer and about 170 kg lighter, with a modern cabin and electric rack-and-pinion steering. The headline change was underneath: the solid front axle the G had used since 1979 gave way to independent double wishbones. The ladder frame, the low range and all three locking differentials stayed.

### THE SAME SHAPE, A DIFFERENT TRUCK
The new front suspension bolts straight to the ladder frame with no subframe, and its lower wishbone mounts sit as high as possible to protect clearance. Out back, a rigid axle is located by four links per side and a Panhard rod. Mercedes quoted 9.5 inches of clearance between the axles, 27.6 inches of wading depth (up almost 4 inches), 31° approach, 30° departure and 26° breakover angles — better on every count than the solid-axle G 550 it replaced.
Low range got shorter, too: 2.93:1 against the old truck’s roughly 2.1:1, engaged at up to 25 mph. Engage it, or any locker, and the truck drops into G-Mode, which retunes the dampers, steering and throttle and holds gears. Development included the Schöckl, the mountain test course outside Graz with gradients up to 60%. The US G 550 kept the 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 — 416 hp and 450 lb-ft — now through a nine-speed automatic and a 40:60 torque split.

### SIX CYLINDERS AND HALF A MILLION Gs
The G kept selling as if nothing had changed. Graz built the 400,000th G-Class on 4 December 2020 and the 500,000th in April 2023 — a one-off in agave green with amber indicators, a tribute to a famous 1979 photo of a W460 240 GD in mid-air. The AMG G 63 carried on alongside with 577 hp.
For the 2025 model year the US G 550 traded its V8 for a turbocharged 3.0-litre inline-six with mild-hybrid assistance: 443 hp and 413 lb-ft. Aero tweaks cut the drag coefficient from 0.55 to 0.48, the cabin got twin 12.3-inch MBUX screens, and the Offroad Cockpit added a “transparent bonnet” camera view. The off-road hardware didn’t move: triple lockers, 9.5 inches of clearance and 27.6 inches of wading.

### THE ELECTRIC G
Then came the one nobody expected to work. The G 580 with EQ Technology, revealed in April 2024, keeps the ladder frame, independent front and rigid rear axle, but drives each wheel with its own motor — 579 hp in total, fed by a 116 kWh battery with 200 kW DC charging. There are no mechanical lockers; torque vectoring provides ‘virtual’ ones. Each axle has a 2:1 low range, and it wades 33.5 inches — 5.9 more than the gas truck.
It also does tricks no Land Cruiser or Defender can: G-Turn spins the truck on the spot by driving the wheels on each side in opposite directions, and G-Steering pivots it around the inside rear wheel. The price is weight — more than three tonnes (Wikipedia quotes 3,085 kg) — and range: up to 294 miles on the European WLTP cycle, 239 miles on the EPA cycle. For 2025 the US got it only as the loaded Edition One.

### Data plate
- Chassis: W463 (“W463A”)
- Years: 2018–present
- Engine (Us G 550): 4.0 TT V8 (to 2024) · 3.0 I6 mild hybrid (2025–)
- Output: 416 hp → 443 hp
- Transmission: 9G-TRONIC 9-speed
- Drive: Permanent 4WD, 40:60, low range 2.93:1
- Lockers: Centre, rear, front
- Suspension: Double-wishbone front · rigid rear
- Clearance: 9.5 in
- Wading: 27.6 in (G 580: 33.5 in)
- Angles: 31° / 30° / 26°
- Built In: Graz, Austria

### Engineering
The second-generation G keeps the old truck’s architecture where it matters off-road and modernizes everything else. The body still sits on a ladder frame, the rear axle is still rigid, and the transfer case still has a proper low range. The front, though, is now independent, the steering is electric rack-and-pinion instead of a recirculating-ball box, and the nine-speed automatic sends 40% of the torque forward and 60% rearward.
- Chassis: Ladder frame (Retained for the gas trucks and, remarkably, the electric G 580.)
- Front: Independent double wishbone (Bolted directly to the frame with no subframe; mounts set high for clearance.)
- Rear: Rigid axle (Four trailing links per side plus a Panhard rod.)
- Lockers: Centre, rear, front (Three 100% locks on gas models; the G 580 uses torque-vectoring ‘virtual’ locks instead.)
- Low Range: 2.93:1 (Engages at up to 25 mph; shift back to high up to 43 mph. Old truck: about 2.1:1.)
- Geometry: 31° / 30° / 26° (Approach, departure, breakover. 9.5 in between axles, 27.6 in wading.)

### Versions
- 2018–2024 · G 500 / G 550 (US) · M176 4.0 L twin-turbo V8 · 416 hp · 450 lb-ft · 9G-TRONIC; launched at Detroit, January 2018
- 2018– · AMG G 63 · AMG 4.0 L twin-turbo V8 · 577 hp · 627 lb-ft · Unveiled at Geneva, March 2018
- 2019– · G 350 d / G 400 d (not US) · OM656 2.9 L inline-six diesel · 282 hp / 326 hp · Diesel sold in other markets
- 2022– · G 63 4×4² · AMG 4.0 L twin-turbo V8 · 585 hp · Portal axles with independent front; $350,050
- 2025– · G 550 (US) · 3.0 L turbo inline-six, mild hybrid · 443 hp · 413 lb-ft · Cd 0.48; transparent-bonnet camera view
- 2025– · G 580 with EQ Technology · Four motors, 116 kWh battery · 579 hp · G-Turn, virtual lockers, 33.5 in wading

### Year-by-year
- 2018: New G unveiled at Detroit in January (G 550) and Geneva in March (AMG G 63). Independent front suspension, rack-and-pinion steering, 9G-TRONIC; about 170 kg lighter
- 2019: US launch; Mercedes-Benz USA's 2019 G 550 spec sheet lists $124,500 plus $995 destination. EPA 14 mpg combined for the V8 G 550
- 2019–2021: Early trucks carry several recalls, including the front-axle harness (23V097), diff-lock module (20V090) and rear door latch (21V353). Confirm by VIN that they were done
- 2022: AMG G 63 4×4² launched in June (MY2023 in the US, $350,050)
- 2023: Final Edition G 500 V8 announced: 1,500 built, 500 in each of three colours
- 2024: Updated G (media designation W465) revealed in March; the G 580 with EQ Technology follows in April
- 2025: US G 550 switches to a 3.0-litre mild-hybrid inline-six (443 hp, EPA 18 mpg combined); G 580 EV arrives with four motors and 33.5 in wading depth

### Capability
- Towing: 7,700 lb (3,493 kg) (2019 G 550, braked)
- GVWR: 6,614 lb (3,000 kg) (2019 G 550)
- Fuel tank: 26.4 US gal (100 L) (2019 G 550)
- Ground clearance: 9.5 in (241 mm) (maximum load; G 580: 9.8 in)
- Approach / departure / breakover: 30.9° / 29.9° / 23.5° (MBUSA 2019 spec sheet, breakover at maximum load; launch press quoted 31° / 30° / 26°)
- Wading depth: 27.6 in (700 mm) (G 580: 33.5 in)
- Low range: 2.93:1
- Fuel economy: EPA 13 city / 17 hwy / 14 comb (2019 V8); 17 / 19 / 18 (2025 inline-six); G 580: 62 MPGe combined, 239-mile range
- Curb weight: 5,551 lb (2,518 kg) (2019 G 550)
- Turning circle: 44.6 ft (13.6 m)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: 275/55R19 on 8.5x19 (2019 G 550), 275/50R20 (option), 265/60R18 all-terrain (optional 18-inch package)
- Bolt Pattern: 5x130
- Center Bore: 84.1 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5 bolts
- Lug Torque: 96 lb-ft (130 N·m)
- Offset: ET35–50 compatible range (2020 G 550)
- Biggest tire, 2.5 in lift: 33 in (Eurowise rates its W463A kit for 33-inch tires without rubbing, depending on wheel offset, and says it has tested 33.5 in. Bigger tires can set off driver-assist warnings (active brake assist, blind-spot, cruise))

### Buying checks
- Check recall 23V097: 26,116 US 2019–2021 G 550s and AMG G 63s were recalled because the front-axle wiring harness can chafe on the oil cooler, killing ABS and stability control. Confirm by VIN that the inspection and sleeve or harness were done.
- Test lockers and low range: Select low range and each lock on a loose surface. The ‘G’ icon should appear and every locker indicator should confirm. Most of these trucks have never been asked.
- Look under the middle: Owner reports point to transfer-case output-seal leaks on 2013–2023 trucks: oil spots under the centre, wet housing, whine. Check the driveshaft flanges for wear marks too.
- Open every door: The doors are heavy; owners report hinge sag. Check that each door closes cleanly with that famous bank-vault clack and lines up with its neighbors.
- Drive it through a full shift cycle: Harsh or jerky 9-speed shifts are often an adaptation issue fixable with a dealer tool — but get it documented before purchase.
- Exercise the screens and cameras: Infotainment freezes, reboots and blank camera feeds are reported; make sure software is current and the 360° camera works — you’ll want it on the trail.
- Check the wheels and badges: Many trucks wear 21- or 22-inch wheels and AMG bodywork. Factory G 550 sizes are 275/55R19 or 275/50R20; budget for an 18- or 20-inch all-terrain setup, and check the VIN before paying a G 63 premium.
- Rear door latches: Open and close both rear doors from inside and outside, and make sure each one latches fully. Then confirm that latch recalls 21V-353 and, for trucks that got a replacement latch, 24V-659 have been completed.

### Common repairs
#### Front-axle harness recall (23V097)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Dealer visit · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: ABS and stability-control warnings; on affected 2019–2021 trucks the front-axle wiring harness can rub through against the auxiliary oil cooler.
Fix: Run the VIN through NHTSA or Mercedes (MBUSA campaign 2023030005). The dealer inspects the harness, sleeves it or replaces it. If you’re underneath anyway, look at the harness routing near the cooler for chafe marks.
Tools: VIN · flashlight for inspection · dealer appointment

#### Transfer-case output seal leak
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Half a day · cost $500–1,200
Symptoms: Drips under the centre of the truck, a wet transfer-case housing, low fluid at service, whine from the transfer case.
Fix: Unbolt the affected driveshaft from the output flange (mark it for phasing), replace the output-shaft seal, inspect the flange for wear grooves and replace it if scored, then refill with Mercedes-approved transfer-case fluid. Clean the housing so you can spot any recurrence.
Tools: Output-shaft seal · seal puller and driver · flange holding tool · MB-approved transfer-case fluid · paint marker · torque wrench

#### Door hinge sag
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2 hours per door · cost $400–1,200
Symptoms: Doors dropping at the striker, needing a lift or a slam to latch, uneven gaps.
Fix: Lubricate hinges with Mercedes-approved grease at every service. If worn, replace the hinges and check the door straps; alignment is fussy, which is why many owners leave it to a dealer.
Tools: Hinge set · door strap · door support/jack with padding · Torx sockets · grease

#### Infotainment freeze or reboot
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 10 minutes · cost Free (software) to warranty
Symptoms: Black screen, reboots while driving, frozen navigation, missing camera image, audio dropouts.
Fix: Soft-reset by holding the power/volume control for about 10 seconds. Then get the latest software and map updates; persistent faults may need a head unit under warranty.
Tools: Your thumb · dealer software update

#### 9-speed shift adaptation
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour · cost Diagnosis-dependent
Symptoms: Harsh, jerky or delayed shifts.
Fix: Note the gear, temperature, drive mode and load when it happens. A Mercedes XENTRY session can reset and relearn the transmission adaptations; rule out the transfer case before condemning the gearbox.
Tools: XENTRY-capable diagnostic tool · notes or video of the symptom

#### Fitting a 2.5-inch lift and 33s
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time A day · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: Not a fault — the most common upgrade. Stock 20-inch tires are about 31 inches tall.
Fix: Install a lift kit (Eurowise's 2.5-inch kit for the 2019-on G, also sold by GwagenParts, works with AMG Ride Control or adaptive suspension) and fit up to 33-inch tires, depending on wheel offset. Above 33 inches Eurowise warns of wheel-speed-sensor faults and active brake assist, blind-spot and cruise-control warnings. Finish with an alignment that includes the adaptive cruise calibration.
Tools: Lift kit · spring compressor · jack and stands · torque wrench · alignment with ADAS calibration

#### Diff locks fail, ESP/ABS warnings (recall 20V-090)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Minutes to check. Dealer visit for the fix. · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: A locker that won't engage or report its status, often with ESP and ABS switching off and warnings on the dash. On affected trucks, a resistor in the differential-locking module can interrupt communication between the control unit and the lock actuator.
Fix: NHTSA recall 20V-090 covers about 6,300 2019–2020 G 550s and AMG G 63s. Dealers inspect the differential-locking modules and replace them as needed for free. Check the VIN, then test every lock on loose ground after the repair. If a lock still misbehaves on a truck that's had the recall done, have it diagnosed with XENTRY before replacing anything.
Tools: VIN · Mercedes-Benz dealer · loose surface to test the locks

#### Rear door won't latch or open (recalls 21V-353 and 24V-659)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Dealer visit · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: A rear door that looks shut but isn't fully latched, or one that won't open from inside.
Fix: Recall 21V-353 replaced the rear door latches on about 17,800 2019–2021 G 550s and G 63s. Recall 24V-659 then covered 2019–2023 trucks that had received a replacement latch, either in service or under the first recall, and replaced the right-rear latch again. A truck fixed under 21V-353 may still need the 24V-659 remedy. Check the VIN for both, and work every rear door from inside and outside on the test drive.
Tools: VIN · Mercedes-Benz dealer

### Baseline service
The second-generation G is still young enough that many have only had dealer A/B services — which skip most driveline fluids. This list covers the 2019–2024 V8 trucks; the 2025-on inline-six G 550 and the electric G 580 have different service needs, so check their manuals.
- Engine oil & filter: M176 4.0 twin-turbo · MB 229.52 or 229.61 · 10.0 US qt (9.5 L) with filter (2019 G 550 owner's manual) · Now, then when the ASSYST PLUS display calls for it. The manual says to service more often for arduous use, such as mountain driving and poor road surfaces. (FCP Euro lists its ≈10-litre M176 kit for the 2019–2024 G 550. Check that the oil carries MB 229.52 or 229.61. These figures are for the V8; check the manual for the 2025-on inline-six.)
- Air filters: M176 air filters · Now if undated
- Cabin air filter: 2019-on cabin filter · Now, then yearly
- Spark plugs & coils: M176 spark plugs (Mercedes-spec) · Now if no record [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
- Coolant: MB 325.6 (pink), FCP Euro lists it for the G 550 from 2015 on · 14.9 US qt (14.1 L) (2019 G 550 manual) · Now if undated (Mix 50/50 with distilled water.)
- Automatic transmission (9G-TRONIC 725.0): MB 236.17 (yellow) · Now if no record [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (On the 9G-TRONIC the filter is part of the pan. Ask for a shift-adaptation reset with XENTRY after the service.)
- Transfer case: Fluid type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Now if no record (Check the output-shaft seals for weeps — a known leak point.)
- Front & rear differentials: Gear oil type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Now if no record (Independent front, rigid rear, both locking. Engage low range and each lock on loose ground to confirm the ‘G’ icon and locker lights.)
- Steering: Electric rack-and-pinion — no power steering fluid · At purchase (Instead, check the tie-rod ends and boots, and the front-axle wiring harness routing near the oil cooler (recall 23V097).)
- Brake fluid: DOT 4 Plus (Genuine Mercedes) · MB approval 331.0 (owner's manual) · Now, then every 2 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
- Drive belts: M176 accessory belt + A/C belt · Inspect now; replace if cracked
- Door hinges: Mercedes-approved grease · Every service (Regular grease keeps the heavy doors from sagging at the striker.)
- Recalls & software: NHTSA 23V097 (2019–2021) · head-unit software · At purchase (Run the VIN through NHTSA and ask the dealer to load the latest software and maps.)
- 12-volt battery: AGM (absorbent glass mat). The manual says full function is only guaranteed with an AGM battery. · Load-test now (Load-test it, especially on a truck that has sat unused.)

### FAQ
Q: What’s the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: We couldn’t verify a firm owner consensus for the 2019-on truck. What is documented: factory G 550 sizes are 275/55R19 and 275/50R20 (about 31 in), Mercedes offered 18-inch all-terrain tires as an option, and a 2.5-inch lift kit is rated for up to 33-inch tires. On earlier Gs, about 32 inches is the commonly cited no-rub ceiling — treat it as a starting point and test-fit at full lock. [TO VERIFY FOR 2019+]

Q: Does it still have three locking differentials?
A: Yes — centre, rear and front, 100% locks, on every gas model. The electric G 580 drops mechanical lockers in favor of per-wheel torque vectoring.

Q: Is it still body-on-frame with a solid axle?
A: It’s still on a ladder frame — even the EV. The rear axle is rigid; the front is now independent double wishbones, the first time a G has had independent front suspension.

Q: What’s the low-range ratio?
A: 2.93:1, versus about 2.1:1 on the previous G. It engages at up to 25 mph with the transmission in neutral, and you can shift back to high range at up to 43 mph.

Q: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
A: 9.5 inches between the axles (10.6 inches to the front axle), 27.6 inches of wading depth, and 31° / 30° / 26° approach, departure and breakover angles. The G 580 EV has 9.8 inches and wades 33.5 inches.

Q: What fuel economy should I expect?
A: The V8 G 550 is EPA-rated 14 mpg combined for 2019–2020; the mild-hybrid inline-six G 550 is rated 18 mpg combined for 2025–2026.

Q: V8 or inline-six?
A: The 2019–2024 G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 makes 416 hp and 450 lb-ft; the 2025-on 3.0-litre mild-hybrid six makes 443 hp and 413 lb-ft and is rated about 4 mpg better combined. Same lockers, same clearance.

Q: What can the electric G 580 do off-road?
A: Climb 100% grades on suitable surfaces, wade 33.5 inches, crawl in three settings, and turn on the spot with G-Turn. It has a 2:1 low range in each axle’s transmission.

Q: What does “W463A” mean?
A: It’s an enthusiast label for the 2018-on truck. Mercedes-Benz doesn’t use it officially.

Q: Are there recalls I should know about?
A: Recall 23V097 covers 26,116 2019–2021 G 550s and AMG G 63s whose front-axle harness can chafe on the oil cooler and disable ABS/ESC. Check any VIN with NHTSA.

Q: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
A: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on high-grip surfaces. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

# Ineos Grenadier (2022–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/

When Land Rover ended classic Defender production at Solihull in January 2016 after 67 years, chemicals billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe tried to keep it alive. Jaguar Land Rover said no. So Ratcliffe did what billionaires do: he founded a car company, Ineos Automotive, and named its first product after his favourite pub, The Grenadier in Belgravia, where the idea was first kicked around. The result is a body-on-frame, beam-axle, permanent-4WD box built in a former Smart car factory in Hambach, France. BMW supplies the straight-six engines (B58 petrol, B57 diesel), ZF the eight-speed automatic, Tremec the two-speed transfer case and Italian tractor specialist Carraro the solid axles. Magna Steyr helped with the engineering. The Station Wagon arrived in late 2022, with US deliveries (petrol only) beginning for the 2024 model year. The Quartermaster double-cab pickup followed into production in late 2023 and reached US buyers for 2025. Both are new enough that the owner knowledge base is still being written, mostly on forums and in recall notices.

Verdict: A billionaire couldn't buy the old Defender, so he built his own from a pub table, a BMW engine and a pair of tractor axles. It is gloriously square, genuinely capable and steers like a canal boat (until 2026).

## Ineos Grenadier Station Wagon (2022–present (US: 2024–present))
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/station-wagon/
Codes: B58 petrol, B57 diesel (non-US), 2,922 mm WB

Verdict: The old Defender's spirit with a BMW heart and Italian tractor axles. Huge capability, real quirks, and steering that only got properly sorted for 2026.

In January 2016 Land Rover stopped building the classic Defender after 67 years, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the chemicals magnate behind Ineos, took it personally. He approached Jaguar Land Rover about buying the tooling to keep it in production, and JLR declined. So Ratcliffe built a replacement himself and named it after his favourite pub, The Grenadier in Belgravia, where the idea was hatched. Most pub ideas end with a hangover. This one ended with a factory.

### A PUB, A GRUDGE AND A CLEAN SHEET
Ineos announced Ineos Automotive in February 2017 to do the job, and the work ran under the codename Projekt Grenadier. Toby Ecuyer led design, and the brief was unapologetically utilitarian: a box-section steel ladder frame, solid axles at both ends and a shape that looks like it was drawn with a ruler because, functionally, it was. The finished exterior was shown online on 1 July 2020, and nobody needed the press release to see which old Land Rover it was mourning.
Land Rover had tried to trademark the old Defender's shape, and Ineos opposed the applications. The UK Intellectual Property Office refused registration for lack of distinctiveness, and in August 2020 the High Court dismissed JLR's appeal. That cleared the legal road for a square, upright, flat-glassed 4x4 built by somebody else. Ineos had argued the shape didn't work as a 'badge of origin' for JLR, and the courts agreed.

### BMW HEART, TRACTOR AXLES, FRENCH ADDRESS
Ineos wasn't going to design an engine from scratch. In March 2019 it signed BMW for powertrains: the 3.0-litre B58 turbo petrol six (282 hp, 332 lb-ft) and the B57 diesel six (245 hp, 406 lb-ft), both through a ZF eight-speed automatic and a Tremec two-speed transfer case with a 2.5:1 low range. Magna Steyr in Austria came on as engineering partner in December 2019, and the program logged a claimed 1.1 million miles of testing, including an outback hot-weather session in early 2022 that got interrupted by a flood.
The axles come from Carraro, an Italian tractor specialist, hung on five-link coil suspension with Eibach springs. Assembly was first planned for a new plant in Bridgend, Wales, announced in September 2019. Then Mercedes put its Smart factory in Hambach, France, up for sale, and in December 2020 Ineos bought it, along with a recently upgraded paint shop and a workforce that had been building Smarts since 1998. The steel floor and shell get 4,068 spot welds, and the body meets the frame in an eight-bolt drop.

### WHAT YOU ACTUALLY GET
Specs read like an overlander's wish list: 264 mm of ground clearance, 800 mm wading depth, 3,500 kg (about 7,700 lb) braked towing, permanent four-wheel drive with a lockable centre diff, and front and rear lockers via the Rough Pack, standard on the Trialmaster. Inside, the diff locks and off-road switches live in an aircraft-style overhead panel, there's a low-volume 'toot' horn for cyclists, and the rotary controller is BMW iDrive in work boots.
The catch is the steering. Up to the 2025 model year the Grenadier uses a Bosch hydraulically assisted recirculating-ball box with almost four turns lock to lock, and testers complained about vagueness and wander on the road. Ineos redid it for 2026 with a new variable-ratio worm gear, more assist as you turn, and a hydraulic stop at full lock. If the G 500 is the boxy 4x4 that went to the opera, the Grenadier is the one that stayed behind to fix the fence, and the 2026 truck finally does it without a workout.

### SO FAR, SO SQUARE
Series production began at Hambach in late 2022, with first deliveries that December. US buyers got the petrol B58 only, from $71,500, with US-spec trucks leaving France in September 2023. Then the growing pains. NHTSA recalls covered auxiliary-switch wiring that could short (a fire risk), steering ball-joint nuts that needed to be locking ones, and door buttons short on grease that could let a door open on the move. In September 2024 a parts shortage linked to the insolvency of supplier Recaro Automotive stopped the line until January 2025.
Production figures cited on Wikipedia put output at 4,553 Grenadiers in 2023 and about 8,000 in 2024, well short of the 25,000 a year Ineos said the plant could build at full capacity. The Quartermaster pickup joined in late 2023. Owners on the forums report software and electrical gremlins alongside real affection for the thing. It is the closest thing on sale to a new classic Defender with a warranty, and it has the quirks to prove it.

### Data plate
- Chassis: Box-section steel ladder frame
- Wheelbase: 2,922 mm (115.0 in)
- Length: 4,856 mm (191.2 in)
- Kerb Weight: 2,644–2,811 kg (5,829–6,197 lb)
- Engine (Us): BMW B58 3.0 turbo I6, 282 hp / 332 lb-ft
- Gearbox: ZF 8-speed automatic
- Transfer Case: Tremec 2-speed, 2.5:1 low, permanent 4WD
- Axles: Carraro beam axles, 5-link coil
- Ground Clearance: 264 mm (10.4 in)
- Wading: 800 mm (31.5 in)
- Towing: 3,500 kg (≈7,700 lb) braked
- Fuel Tank: 90 L (≈23.8 gal)

### Engineering
The Grenadier is old-school where it counts and bought-in where that's smarter. A box-section steel ladder frame carries Carraro beam axles on five-link coils, with permanent 4WD through a Tremec two-speed transfer case. The body is welded at Hambach and bolted to the frame in an eight-bolt drop. The engines and gearboxes are bought in from BMW and ZF. The frame, axles and body are Ineos' own.
- Chassis: Box-section steel ladder frame (Body bolted on in an eight-bolt drop at Hambach.)
- Axles: Carraro beam axles, front and rear (From the Italian tractor specialist; five-link coils, Eibach springs, anti-roll bars.)
- Engine: BMW B58 3.0 turbo I6 (B57 diesel ex-US) (282 hp / 332 lb-ft petrol; 245 hp / 406 lb-ft diesel.)
- Gearbox: ZF 8-speed automatic (8HP51 behind the petrol, 8HP76 behind the diesel.)
- Transfer: Tremec two-speed, 2.5:1 low range (Permanent 4WD with a centre lock; front and rear lockers optional or standard on Trialmaster.)
- Steering: Recirculating ball, hydraulic assist (Bosch box, nearly four turns lock to lock; new variable-ratio worm gear for MY2026.)

### Versions
- 2022–present · Station Wagon, 2,922 mm WB · BMW B58 3.0 turbo I6 petrol · 282 hp / 332 lb-ft · The only engine sold in the US (from MY2024).
- 2022–present · Station Wagon, 2,922 mm WB · BMW B57 3.0 turbo I6 diesel · 245 hp / 406 lb-ft · Europe, Australia and other markets; not sold in the US.
- 2022–present · Utility Wagon (2- or 5-seat) · B58 or B57 · As above · Commercial version with a full-height cargo barrier on the two-seater; sold in markets including Australia.
- 2022–present · Trialmaster Edition · B58 (US) / B58 or B57 · As above · Rough Pack standard (front and rear lockers, BFG KO2s), plus raised air intake, auxiliary battery and switch panel.
- 2022–present · Fieldmaster Edition · B58 (US) / B58 or B57 · As above · Safari windows, leather, heated front seats; Rough Pack optional.
- MY2026 · Station Wagon update · B58 (US) · 282 hp / 332 lb-ft · Variable-ratio steering, revised HVAC, quieter driver assists, Black Edition.

### Year-by-year
- 2020: Exterior revealed online on 1 July; INEOS buys the Smart plant at Hambach, France, in December
- 2022: Production starts at Hambach; first deliveries in December
- 2023: First US-bound trucks leave the factory in September for MY2024; B58 petrol only
- MY2024: Early US trucks covered by recalls 23V903, 23V828 and 25V147; check they're closed
- 2024–25: Factory stops from September 2024 to January 2025 over a parts-supply problem
- MY2026: Variable-ratio steering box with more assist, revised HVAC, quieter driver assists, Black Edition [buy]

### Capability
- Towing: 7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked
- Payload: About 1,680 lb (US figure)
- Roof load: 150 kg (330 lb) dynamic, 420 kg (925 lb) static
- Fuel tank: 90 L (23.8 gal)
- Ground clearance: 264 mm (10.4 in)
- Approach / departure / breakover: 35.5° / 36.1° / 28.2°
- Wading depth: 800 mm (31.5 in)
- Fuel economy: EPA 15 city / 15 hwy (Trialmaster 14 / 14; premium fuel)
- Curb weight: 2,644–2,811 kg (5,829–6,197 lb)
- Turning circle: About 13.5 m (44 ft) (pre-2026 steering)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: LT265/70R17, LT255/70R18
- Bolt Pattern: 6x130
- Offset: +55 mm (stock 17x7.5)
- Center Bore: 84.1 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 285/75R17 (≈34 in) (INEOS Forum consensus sweet spot with no rub, but you'll probably need washers under the spare carrier to clear the small rear door. 285/70R17 fits without fuss; DVA Mechanics lists 295/70R17 as 'stock or 40 mm lift'.)
- Biggest tire, 2 in lift: 315/70R17 (35 in) (DVA Mechanics lists 35s as needing at least 2 in of lift. Expect an aftermarket or offset spare carrier, and match the spare to the road tyres because the permanent 4WD centre diff doesn't like mismatched diameters.)

### Buying checks
- Run the VIN for all three US recalls: 23V828 (auxiliary switch relay wire trapped under a fastener, fire risk), 23V903 (non-locking nuts on the steering rod ball joint) and 25V147 (door button assemblies short on grease; 7,022 trucks built July 6, 2023 to April 19, 2024). All are free dealer fixes. Ask for proof they were done.
- Ask about software and module history: Forum owners report fuel 'implausibility' warnings that took more than one reflash, false steering warnings, failed modules and unexplained messages. A truck with documented updates and a quiet dash is worth more than one with a thin service file.
- Drive it on a real road: Pre-2026 trucks use the slow Bosch recirculating-ball box that reviewers called vague and wandering. Some owners love it, some fit aftermarket stabilizers or pump kits. MY2026 got a new variable-ratio steering gear. Know which one you're buying.
- Check for water in the doors and cabin: Owners have reported rear doors holding water after a wash, condensation, door seals coming off and a kickplate whose adhesive let go. Look at door bottoms, carpets and seals.
- Check the oil level and the break-in service: One owner got a low-oil message at 12,000 miles. Many owners did an early break-in oil change (500–1,000 miles was the dealer advice quoted on the forum). Ask whether it was done and check the dipstick reading in the menu.
- Confirm the Rough Pack if you want lockers: The centre diff lock is standard, but front and rear lockers come with the Rough Pack ($2,850 on base and Fieldmaster at launch; standard on Trialmaster). Look for the locker switches in the overhead panel.
- Inspect any lift and big-tire install: Agile Offroad warns that lift height changes can damage the factory driveshaft. On trucks with 285/75s or bigger, check that the spare clears the small rear door, and look for tire rub caused by a body sitting off-center on the frame.
- Understand the parts and dealer network: Ineos is a young brand with a small dealer network, and the factory stopped from September 2024 to January 2025 over a parts shortage. Powertrain parts are BMW and ZF, but body and chassis parts come through Ineos. Ask the local dealer about parts lead times.

### Common repairs
#### Engine oil and filter change (B58)
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour · cost About $150 dealer oil service quoted by a US owner; a US first service including transfer case and diff fluids was quoted at about $1,700
Symptoms: Service due, or an 'Engine Oil Low' message. Many owners do an early break-in change, then shorter intervals than the factory schedule.
Fix: Put the hood in its maintenance position and remove the plastic engine cover. The canister filter housing is on top of the engine; an owner used an impact-rated 32 mm socket on it and needed no U-joint. Swap the element and its O-ring, drain the sump, fit a new drain plug washer, refill and check the level in the menu. Tall owners still report standing on a crate to reach the housing.
Tools: 32 mm socket · drain pan · BMW-type oil filter with O-ring and crush washer · oil: an owner quoted the manual as 6.5 L of 0W-20, ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE (check your own manual)

#### Engine air filter
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 15 minutes · cost Filter only
Symptoms: Service interval, or after dusty trail use. One owner changes it every second oil change (about 5,000 miles).
Fix: Loosen the captive screws around the airbox (they don't come out), lift the upper half, remove the old filter and drop in the new one. Note how the white felt pre-filter is fitted: on some it's glued to the filter, on others it clips into the bottom of the box. Reassemble.
Tools: PZ3 (Pozidriv #3) screwdriver · filter (a member says Mahle LX3985/1 matches OEM; not officially confirmed)

#### Cabin air filter
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 5–10 minutes once you know the trick · cost About $18 for an aftermarket filter
Symptoms: Weak airflow or musty smell. Note: one owner found almost no cabin heat in 15°F weather with the filter removed.
Fix: On a left-hand-drive truck, slide the passenger seat back and recline it, then lie on your back in the footwell with a headlamp. Unsnap the two side clips under the filter frame, let the hinged plate swing down, pull the filter out (a curved pick helps), and fit the new one with the airflow arrow toward the cabin. Snap it shut. The glovebox stays in place.
Tools: Headlamp · curved pick · cardboard to lie on · OEM INEOS #100326881, or Microguard 3692 reported to fit (no charcoal layer); Mann CUK25001 reported not to fit

#### Spare carrier clearance after upsizing tires
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour · cost Washers, or $239 for a relocation bracket
Symptoms: With 285/75R17 or 255/85R17 tires, the spare hits or barely clears the small rear door.
Fix: Owners running 285/75s and 255/85s added a couple of washers under the spare carrier bolts (one used the top and lower-left bolts) to tilt the spare clear of the small door. For bigger tires or a cleaner fix, Leitner Designs sells a bolt-on bracket that moves the spare 1¾ in. up, right and outboard. Leitner rates it for up to 37 in. tires, but not for wheels with more than 25 mm offset.
Tools: Socket set · washers · or Leitner Designs Grenadier tire relocation bracket

#### Tire rub on one side only: re-center the body on the frame
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Shop job; time not documented · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: Bigger tires rub on one side but clear on the other, with the same wheels and offset on both sides.
Fix: On the INEOS Forum, a shop found one truck's body sitting off-center on the chassis. Slackening the body mount bolts, re-centering the body and re-tightening fixed the rub. Measure fender-to-tire gaps on both sides before you blame the tire, and torque the body mounts to factory spec.
Tools: Floor jack · large sockets · torque wrench · factory torque specs

#### Door doesn't latch / door button sticks (recall 25V147)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Dealer visit · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: Exterior door button stays pressed in, door doesn't fully latch, or the head unit shows a door-open warning that turns red with chimes once you're moving.
Fix: Ineos found the door button mechanisms on 7,022 US 2024 Grenadiers (built July 6, 2023 to April 19, 2024) may lack grease. Dealers replace the door button assemblies. Until then, check every door is fully shut before driving and take the head unit warning seriously.
Tools: VIN check at nhtsa.gov/recalls · dealer appointment

#### Steering ball-joint nut check (recall 23V903)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 15 minutes to look; dealer fix · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: Usually none until it's serious. A loose or missing nut can let the steering rod ball joint come apart, and you lose steering.
Fix: Affected 2023–2024 trucks may have non-locking nuts on the steering rod ball joint. Dealers install locking nuts. If you've bought used, confirm the campaign is closed, and check the steering linkage joints after hard trail use as a habit.
Tools: Flashlight · VIN check · dealer appointment

#### Auxiliary switch panel wiring (recall 23V828)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Dealer visit · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: Electrical faults on accessories wired through the auxiliary switch panel relay, or none at all.
Fix: On 2024 trucks with the auxiliary switch package, the relay control wire may be trapped under a fastener, damaging its insulation and risking a short and fire. Dealers inspect and secure the wire, repairing or replacing damaged wiring. Do this before adding lights or fridges to the auxiliary circuits.
Tools: VIN check · dealer appointment

### Baseline service
Assume nothing was done early: the factory schedule is long (12 months / 12,000 miles in the US), the full service manual isn't sold to owners, and only dealers can reset the service counter. Baseline every fluid once, keep receipts with OEM-spec fluids to protect the 5-year warranty, and note that much of the drivetrain is shared with BMW (B58/B57 engines, ZF 8-speed), so FCP Euro and other BMW specialists carry many of the consumables.
- Engine oil & filter: B58 petrol: 0W-20, ACEA C2 (dealers also cite C5 / API SP), BMW Longlife-17 FE+ · 6.5 L per the manual as quoted by owners; buy 7 L. B57 diesel: 0W-30 (the diesel manual lists Petronas Syntium 7000 E 0W-30) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Factory 12 months / 12,000 mi (US); owners and some dealers recommend 5,000–6,000 mi, or 6,000 mi for heavy use (Hood in maintenance position, engine cover off. 32 mm socket on the canister cap on top of the engine, 17 mm drain plug with a new copper washer, 25 Nm. Owners report the BMW B58 filter fits. Check the level in the menu, not by dipstick.)
- Engine air filter: Panel filter with white felt pre-filter (glued on some, clipped into the box on others) · Every 2 years / 24,000 mi; much sooner after dusty trails (Captive PZ3 screws on the airbox. If the history is unknown, just replace it, because it's cheap.)
- Cabin air filter: OEM INEOS #100326881 · Every annual service (Behind a hinged plate under the passenger footwell (LHD). The glovebox stays in. Arrow toward the cabin.)
- Spark plugs (B58 petrol): BMW B58 plugs · gap/spec [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Dealer schedules list 48,000 mi (or 4 years) (If the truck is near 48k and there's no record, do them now. Plug fitment below is listed for the BMW 340i B58; confirm against the INEOS parts catalogue.)
- Fuel filter (B57 diesel only): [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Every 2 years per dealer schedule (Non-US diesels only. Replace if there's no record, and more often on questionable fuel.)
- Coolant: BMW LC-18 coolant (BMW 83195A42DF3 = Frostox HT-12), 50/50 with distilled water · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Every 4 years per dealer schedule (Don't top up with generic green or older BMW GS 94000 coolant. Owners note many aftermarket brands don't list LC-18.)
- Automatic transmission (ZF 8HP: 8HP51 petrol, 8HP76 diesel): ZF Lifeguard 8 ATF · ≈10.6 L reported by an owner [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Dealer schedule: check every 2 years, replace at 6 years. Owners plan a pan/filter at 40–50k mi. (Do a drain and pan/filter change (the filter is built into the pan), not a flush. The Grenadier pan has a second, smaller pickup port, so aftermarket aluminium pans may not match. Fill level at the right temperature: use the Offroad › Temperatures screen and keep the truck level.)
- Transfer case (Tremec 2-speed): Fuchs Titan Sintopoid 75W-90 (75W-85 also acceptable) · 1.8 L, or 2.64 L if the oil cooler and lines are drained too · Dealer schedule: check every 2 years, replace at 6 years. Owners change it much earlier: one found metal flakes at 800 mi, and some trucks had it changed under recall at ~5,000 km. (O-ring-sealed drain and fill plugs, 15 Nm (owner-reported). Owners quoting the workshop manual say it calls for fill to spill; because the cooler lines drain back, some owners also measure what comes out so they know how much to put back.)
- Front & rear differentials (Carraro axles): SAE 80W-90 GL-5 · 2.1 L per axle (workshop-manual figure quoted on the INEOS Forum). Note: Agile Offroad's diff-cover instructions call for 75W-140. · First change at 12 months / 12,000 mi, then 60,000 mi per the US schedule as quoted by owners. Owners who wade or tow do it every 10,000 mi. (Remove the FILL plug first, because owners have snapped fill plugs after draining. 12 mm hex plugs (M22×1.5), 31 Nm; INEOS plug part GRA-5000-021220 (the O-ring isn't sold separately). The fill plug is magnetic. Same fluid with or without the lockers.)
- Brake fluid: DOT 4 (SAE J1703) · Every 2 years (If the date is unknown, flush it, especially after water crossings.)
- Power steering fluid (hydraulic Bosch box): Penrite LDAS, as cited from an INEOS support document by an Australian owner on the INEOS Forum · [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Check level and condition at every service (The recirculating-ball steering is hydraulic. Owners with big tires and heavy steering look at Owl's upgraded pump. Check for leaks at the box and pump.)
- Suspension retorque, body drains & recalls: Retorque suspension and body mounts; clear the body and safari-hatch drains · At purchase, then every annual service (Dealer first-service packages include a suspension retorque and drain clearing. Run the VIN for open recalls (door button 25V147, steering ball-joint nut 23V903, aux switch panel 23V828) before anything else.)
- Battery & charging: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Test at purchase and every service (Dealers include a battery health test in the annual service. Trucks that sat on a lot often have a tired battery, which causes odd electrical warnings.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: From the factory the Grenadier rides on LT265/70R17 or LT255/70R18 (about 32 in.). INEOS Forum owners report 285/70R17 fits with no problem. 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) is the popular sweet spot: owners report no rub on stock suspension, but you'll probably need a couple of washers under the spare carrier to clear the small rear door. DVA Mechanics' fitment guide lists 295/70R17 as 'stock or 40 mm lift' and treats 35-inch tires (315/70R17) as a 2-inch-lift job. A few forum owners report squeezing 35s onto aftermarket wheels without a lift, but treat 285/75R17 as the practical stock limit.

Q: How much can it tow?
A: 3,500 kg braked, about 7,700 lb (GearJunkie lists 7,716 lb). That's well above a Wrangler's 2,495 kg in Australian spec. Payload is about 1,680 lb in US figures, so a heavy trailer plus a fully loaded overland build will run into the GVWR before the hitch rating.

Q: What fuel economy does it get?
A: Not much. The EPA rates the 2024 petrol Grenadier at 15 mpg city, highway and combined, and the Trialmaster at 14 mpg on premium fuel. The tank holds 90 litres (about 23.8 gal), which gives a range of roughly 350 miles in mixed use at the EPA figure, less with a roof tent and big tires.

Q: How much weight can go on the roof?
A: 150 kg (330 lb) dynamic, meaning while driving, and 420 kg (925 lb) static, meaning parked. That's enough for a rooftop tent with people in it. Front Runner's Slimline II kit installs with no drilling and weighs about 57 kg (126 lb) itself, so count it against the dynamic limit.

Q: Can I get the diesel in the US?
A: No. In the US and Canada the Grenadier and Quartermaster come only with the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six, 282 hp and 332 lb-ft. The B57 diesel (245 hp, 406 lb-ft) is sold in Europe, Australia and other markets.

Q: Does it have lockers, and how does the 4WD work?
A: It has permanent four-wheel drive through a Tremec two-speed transfer case (2.5:1 low), with a centre diff lock on a lever. Front and rear lockers come with the Rough Pack, which also adds BFG KO2 tires. It's standard on the Trialmaster and was a $2,850 option on base and Fieldmaster trucks at US launch. The locker switches are in the overhead panel.

Q: What oil does the B58 take and how often should I change it?
A: An owner quoting the manual on the INEOS Forum lists 6.5 L of 0W-20 meeting ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE. Check your own manual, since the oil forums note the US manual is vague. One owner reports the manufacturer schedule as every 12,000 miles. Many owners do an early break-in change (500–1,000 miles on dealer advice) and then change it every 5,000–7,500 miles, especially if they tow.

Q: Is the steering really that bad?
A: Before 2026, it's slow: a Bosch hydraulic recirculating-ball box with almost four turns lock to lock, which The Drive found wandered on the highway and was heavy when parked. Some owners like it off-road, and Owl sells a $2,150 pump kit and a Fox stabilizer. For MY2026 Ineos fitted a variable-ratio worm gear with more assist and a tighter on-center feel. GearJunkie called it 'a big leap forward'.

Q: Which years should I buy or avoid?
A: There's no bad engine to avoid, since every US truck has the B58. The early US trucks (MY2024) carry all three recalls, so get proof they're closed. MY2026 brings the revised steering, HVAC and driver-assist tweaks plus more than 40 smaller changes. If you plan to drive a lot of highway miles, 2026 is the one to buy. Cars.com calls the 2026 steering 'a tremendous improvement'; Parkers is cooler and calls it 'marginally better on-road'.

Q: Is it reliable?
A: It's too new for a long-term verdict. The BMW six and ZF eight-speed are widely used and well proven elsewhere. Owner reports focus on electronics: modules, false warnings, software reflashes, sticky door buttons and water ingress, plus three US recalls. Most owners on the forums still sound happy, but a good dealer matters more than usual.

Q: How capable is it off-road out of the box?
A: Very. It has 264 mm of ground clearance, 800 mm wading depth, and approach, breakover and departure angles of 35.5°, 28.2° and 36.1°, with solid axles and up to three locking diffs. GearJunkie noted there's no disconnecting sway bar, but the soft coils still articulate well.

## Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster (2023–present (US: 2025–present))
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/quartermaster/
Codes: Double cab pickup, 3,227 mm WB

Verdict: A Grenadier with a foot of extra frame and a bed that takes a Euro pallet, as long as you lift the spare out first. It's a seriously capable off-roader that happens to have a tailgate, and in America it carries a 25% chicken tax on top.

Most pickups start as trucks and get dressed up as lifestyle accessories. The Quartermaster went the other way. Ineos took the Grenadier Station Wagon, stretched its ladder frame by 305 mm, cut the roof off behind the second row and fitted a bed sized for a 1,200 × 800 mm Euro pallet. It still has coil springs at all four corners, Carraro beam axles and a BMW straight-six, so it rides and crawls like an expedition wagon with an open load bay. AutoDaily put it neatly: it's "more of a 4×4 with an open load area than what we would call a pick-up."

### FROM GOODWOOD TO HAMBACH
The Quartermaster made its public debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed in July 2023. Series production began in November 2023 on the same Hambach, France, line that builds the wagon, in the former Smart factory Ineos bought from Mercedes. European deliveries were due from December 2023, with Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa next. A bare cab-chassis for tray bodies was added in Australia and New Zealand.
Australia, where Ineos partnered with tray maker Norweld, was a key market. There the Quartermaster goes head to head with the 70 Series LandCruiser ute, which still has a leaf-sprung rear. Caravan World drove both and found the Ineos more compliant over small bumps and "blasts the 79 Series out of the water" off-road. The Toyota keeps the edge on payload, price and parts availability.

### WHAT THE EXTRA FOOT BUYS (AND COSTS)
The bed is 1,564 mm long and 1,619 mm wide, with 1,337 mm between the wheel arches, four lashing eyes and a 400 W power outlet. The tailgate takes 225 kg (about 496 lb) when it's down. Payload depends on market and engine: Ineos quotes up to 907 kg for an Australian petrol truck and 832 kg for the diesel, and about 1,675 lb at US launch. Towing stays at 3,500 kg (about 7,700 lb), the same as the wagon. Petrol output is unchanged at 282 hp; the diesel makes 550 Nm.
The extra length costs some geometry. Approach angle is a strong 36.2°, but breakover falls from the wagon's 28.2° to 26.2° and departure from 36.1° to 22.6°. That's why the spare wheel lives upright in the bed rather than under it, where it would hang down and cut the departure angle further. The catch is that you have to lift the spare out before a pallet will go in. Turning circle grows to about 14.5 m, roughly a metre more than the wagon, and Top Gear called that figure "genuinely appalling."

### THE AMERICAN PROBLEM
Ineos opened US orders in April 2024 at $86,900 for the base Quartermaster and $94,900 for the Trialmaster and Fieldmaster, all before destination. That was $15,400 more than the Station Wagon, and most of the difference was the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. The September 2024 production stoppage, caused by a parts shortage after supplier Recaro Automotive went insolvent, pushed US deliveries back, and the first cargo ship of Quartermasters reached America in March 2025. A month later, new US tariffs took the total import duty on the truck to 50%.
Ineos said it would absorb most of the extra tariff, but the US starting price still rose 11%, from $85,500 to $94,500 including shipping, according to Automotive News. Ineos told the paper the Quartermaster could reach up to 20% of its US volume and pitched it against the Rivian R1T and F-150 Raptor rather than a Silverado. Expedition Portal's long-term test truck towed a 5,000-plus-pound Xplore overland trailer and drew this verdict: "Expect it to drive like the HD truck it is and not a car, and it won't disappoint."

### THE 2026 FIX AND THE BUILD SCENE
For 2026 the Quartermaster got the same fix as the wagon: a variable-ratio steering box that's firmer and more precise near straight-ahead, steering stops that cut the turning circle by about 5%, better climate-control components and a faster way to silence the Intelligent Speed Assist chime. A Black Edition joined the range, and US 2026 price lists show no base Quartermaster, starting instead at the Fieldmaster and Trialmaster. The off-road hardware didn't change.
The aftermarket has been quicker than the factory. Norweld builds trays and canopies, Dirtbox Overland sells a $11,499 canopy camper made for the bed, and Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack that bolts to the roll cage rather than the gutters. Owners on the INEOS Forum fit Dirtbox caps, adjustable shocks and spare-wheel relocations, and Expedition Portal has filmed a Quartermaster on Letech portal axles. It's the closest thing on sale to a new 130-inch Defender pickup, and owners are building it that way.

### Data plate
- Body: Double cab pickup, 5 seats
- Wheelbase: 3,227 mm (127.0 in)
- Length: 5,400 mm (212.6 in)
- Kerb Weight: 2,643 kg petrol / 2,718 kg diesel (AU)
- Engine (Us): BMW B58 3.0 turbo I6, 282 hp / 332 lb-ft
- Driveline: ZF 8-speed auto, Tremec 2-speed transfer, permanent 4WD
- Bed: 1,564 × 1,619 mm; 1,337 mm between arches
- Payload: ≈1,675 lb (US launch) / 832–907 kg (AU)
- Towing: 3,500 kg (≈7,700 lb) braked
- Angles: 36.2° approach / 26.2° breakover / 22.6° departure
- Ground Clearance: 264 mm (10.4 in)
- Turning Circle: ≈14.5 m (pre-2026)

### Engineering
Under the bed, the Quartermaster is a stretched Grenadier. The box-section ladder frame is 305 mm longer, and everything bolted to it carries over: Carraro beam axles on five-link coil suspension with progressive-rate Eibach springs, permanent 4WD through a Tremec two-speed transfer case, and BMW six-cylinder engines with a ZF eight-speed automatic. The rear body is the wagon's up to the back doors, then it becomes a steel bed with a pallet-width floor.
- Chassis: Box-section ladder frame, 305 mm longer than the wagon (3,227 mm (127 in) wheelbase; overall length 5,400 mm.)
- Suspension: Five-link coils front and rear (Progressive-rate Eibach springs on Carraro beam axles; no leaf springs.)
- Engines: BMW B58 petrol / B57 diesel 3.0 I6 (Petrol 282 hp / 450 Nm (US only engine); diesel 245 hp / 550 Nm.)
- Driveline: ZF 8-speed, Tremec 2-speed transfer (Permanent 4WD, 2.5:1 low range, centre lock; front and rear lockers on Trialmaster.)
- Bed: 1,564 × 1,619 mm, 1,337 mm between arches (Takes one Euro pallet; four lashing eyes, 400 W outlet, 225 kg tailgate.)
- Spare: Carried upright in the bed (Kept off the underside to protect a 22.6° departure angle.)

### Versions
- 2023–present · Quartermaster double cab, 3,227 mm WB · BMW B58 3.0 turbo I6 petrol · 282 hp / 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) · The only engine sold in the US; 0–100 km/h in 8.8 s.
- 2023–present · Quartermaster double cab, 3,227 mm WB · BMW B57 3.0 twin-turbo I6 diesel · 245 hp (183 kW) / 550 Nm · Europe, Australia, NZ and other markets; the big seller in Australia.
- 2024–present · Quartermaster cab-chassis · B58 or B57 · As above · Bare chassis for trays such as Norweld's; sold in Australia and NZ, priced just below the tub truck.
- 2023–present · Trialmaster Edition · B58 (US) / B58 or B57 · As above · Front and rear lockers, raised air intake, BFG KO2s; Expedition Portal's test truck added a factory winch.
- 2023–present · Fieldmaster Edition · B58 (US) / B58 or B57 · As above · Heated leather seats and comfort kit; aimed at lighter off-road use.
- MY2026 · Quartermaster update + Black Edition · Unchanged · Unchanged · Variable-ratio steering, about 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC; no base trim on US 2026 price lists.

### Year-by-year
- 2023: Quartermaster double-cab introduced in July; production starts in November
- 2024: Cab-chassis version for trays added in Australia and New Zealand
- 2024: Ineos Australia shows the one-off Kaiju build in December
- 2025: US sales begin in spring, B58 petrol only
- 2025: April tariffs raise duty to 50%; US price up 11% to $94,500 including shipping
- MY2026: Variable-ratio steering, about 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC; no base trim on US 2026 price lists [buy]

### Capability
- Towing: 7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked (7,000 kg GCM in Australian spec)
- Payload: About 1,675 lb (US launch figure; 907 kg petrol / 832 kg diesel in Australia)
- Fuel tank: 90 L (23.8 gal)
- Roof load: 120 kg (265 lb) dynamic, 375 kg (827 lb) static (Caravan World spec table (Australia); lower than the wagon's 150/420 kg)
- Ground clearance: 264 mm (10.4 in)
- Approach / departure / breakover: 36.2° / 22.6° / 26.2°
- Wading depth: 800 mm (31.5 in)
- Fuel economy: About 14 mpg combined (Edmunds, US petrol; 12.6 L/100 km petrol on the Australian test cycle)
- Curb weight: 2,643 kg petrol / 2,718 kg diesel (Australian figures)
- Turning circle: About 14.5 m (48 ft) (pre-2026 steering)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: LT265/70R17, 255/70R18
- Bolt Pattern: 6x130
- Offset: +55 mm (stock 17x7.5)
- Center Bore: 84.1 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 285/75R17 (≈34 in) (Same axles and front suspension as the wagon, where INEOS Forum owners run 285/75R17 on stock suspension and 285/70R17 without rubbing. The spare lives in the bed, so there's no rear-door carrier to fight.)
- Biggest tire, 2 in lift: 315/70R17 or narrow 35s (DVA Mechanics says 35s need at least 2 in of lift; a Quartermaster owner recommends narrow 35s (255/85R17, 35x10.5) on near-factory-offset wheels. Ineos Australia's Kaiju build ran 315/70R17 with JMACX remote-reservoir shocks.)

### Buying checks
- Run the VIN at NHTSA: Recalls 23V828 (auxiliary switch relay wiring), 23V903 (steering ball-joint nuts) and 25V147 (door buttons) are filed against 2023–2024 Grenadiers. As of October 2026, NHTSA's recall database lists none for 2025–2026 models. Check every truck by VIN anyway, and get proof that any open campaign was closed.
- Do the payload math before you buy a camper: Payload is modest for a pickup: about 1,675 lb at US launch, and 832–907 kg in Australia depending on engine. A canopy, fridge, water, a second battery and a winch use that up quickly. Expedition Portal says even its Trialmaster test truck (winch, dual batteries, bed rack) is rated at about 1,400 lb. In Australia, Caravan World quotes a GVM upgrade to roughly 3,900–4,000 kg for about A$5,800 plus fitting.
- Know where the spare will live: From the factory the spare stands in the bed, sticks up above the bed sides and has to come out before a pallet will fit. It also gets in the way of flat tonneau covers. Ask whether the spare has been relocated (owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle) and check that the new mount is solid.
- Drive it empty and on the highway: Several INEOS Forum owners describe an unladen Quartermaster as 'jittery' over bumps in a way the wagon isn't, though it settles once a canopy and gear go in. Pre-2026 trucks also have the slow, non-self-centring steering box and a 14.5 m turning circle. MY2026 trucks get the variable-ratio box and a turning circle about 5% tighter.
- Wellside or cab-chassis?: Outside the US you can buy a cab-chassis and fit a tray. Ineos and Norweld offered early Australian cab-chassis buyers a A$7,000 tray contribution, with conditions. Caravan World lists Norweld trays from A$18,990 and canopies from A$19,205, so a tray build costs a lot more than the tub truck, but it gives you a flat, wider deck.
- Confirm the lockers and Trialmaster kit: The centre diff lock is standard on every truck. Front and rear lockers come on the Trialmaster or with the Rough Pack. The locker switches are in the overhead panel, and the centre lock is on the transfer lever. Trialmaster trucks also get a raised air intake and all-terrain tires.
- Check the bed for tie-down track and holes: Some dealers fit L-track to the bed and sides. One forum owner noted that some trucks were built without bed rails, so adding them means drilling and countersinking. Look for neat, sealed holes and no rust starting around the fasteners.
- Ask about parts and the dealer: Caravan World scored accessibility of spare parts 7/10. The engine and gearbox come from BMW and ZF, but body, bed and chassis parts come through Ineos's small network. Ask the nearest dealer about lead times, especially if you travel remote.

### Common repairs
#### Engine oil and filter change (B58)
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour · cost About $150 for a dealer oil service, as quoted by a US Grenadier owner
Symptoms: Service due, an 'Engine Oil Low' message, or the first break-in change. Towing and camper weight are good reasons to shorten intervals.
Fix: This is the same job as on the wagon. Put the hood in its maintenance position and remove the engine cover. The canister filter housing is on top of the engine. Undo it with a 32 mm socket and replace the element and O-ring. Drain the sump, fit a new drain-plug washer, refill and check the level in the vehicle menu.
Tools: 32 mm socket · drain pan · filter with O-ring and crush washer · oil: an owner quoted the manual as 6.5 L of 0W-20, ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE (check your own manual)

#### Engine air filter
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 15 minutes · cost Filter only
Symptoms: Service interval, or after dusty trail use. With a camper or tray, you'll be on gravel roads more than you think.
Fix: Loosen the captive screws around the airbox (they don't come out) and lift off the top half. Note how the white felt pre-filter is fitted (glued to the filter on some trucks, clipped into the box on others), then swap the filter and close it up.
Tools: PZ3 (Pozidriv #3) screwdriver · filter (a forum member reports Mahle LX3985/1 matches OEM; not officially confirmed)

#### Cabin air filter
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 5–10 minutes once you know the trick · cost About $18 aftermarket
Symptoms: Weak airflow or a musty smell, especially after dusty trips.
Fix: This is the same as on the wagon. On a left-hand-drive truck, slide the passenger seat back, recline it and lie in the footwell with a headlamp. Unsnap the two clips under the filter frame, let the hinged plate swing down, pull the old filter out and fit the new one with the airflow arrow toward the cabin.
Tools: Headlamp · curved pick · OEM INEOS #100326881, or Microguard 3692 reported to fit

#### Rear sag under a canopy or camper
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Not documented; varies by kit · cost $599 for Owl/Eibach Pro-Lift springs (set of 4) or $765–795 for a Dirtbox air-bag kit, plus labor
Symptoms: The rear sits low with a cap, fridge, water and batteries on board. The front bump stops get hit, and the truck tows nose-high.
Fix: Weigh the truck loaded first. For a permanent build, Eibach's Pro-Lift springs (about +2.5 in. front, +1.2 in. rear; one kit for Grenadier and Quartermaster) restore height. Owl recommends matching bump stops. For a load that changes, Dirtbox sells a Traveler Mammoth rear air-bag kit that mounts at the factory bump-stop location with no drilling, in OEM-height and 2 in. versions. In Australia a GVM upgrade is the legal way to carry more.
Tools: Floor jack · axle stands · torque wrench · kit instructions · bump stops to suit

#### Unladen 'jitter': shock upgrade
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Not documented · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: The ride feels busy and jittery over small bumps when the bed is empty. Forum owners say the wagon doesn't do this.
Fix: Owners blame the longer wheelbase, the springs rated for payload, and possibly the bed mounts. One owner fitted Radflo adjustable shocks and reports a good ride on and off road. Another fitted MetalCloak suspension and still felt the jitter. Ineos's Kaiju build used JMACX remote-reservoir shocks. Adding the load you actually carry often settles it first, so try that before you spend money.
Tools: Floor jack · axle stands · sockets · torque wrench · shocks specified for Quartermaster length

#### Relocate the spare out of the bed
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Depends on the mount · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: The spare blocks the pallet space, a flat tonneau or a canopy floor.
Fix: Pick a mount that keeps the departure angle. Ineos put the spare in the bed because hanging it underneath costs ground clearance at the back. Forum owners have moved the spare under the deck (on a canopy build) or under the rear axle. Other options are a roof mount, which Ineos offers, or an aftermarket rear bumper with a carrier. Check the jack and lug wrench still reach.
Tools: Sockets · torque wrench · relocation bracket or bumper from your chosen supplier

#### Add L-track or O-track to the bed
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time Varies · cost Track and fasteners
Symptoms: The four lashing eyes aren't enough for bikes, boxes or a drawer system.
Fix: One owner's dealer fitted L-track on the bed floor and sides, which held a cargo bike sideways. The upper bed rails are held with plastic pop rivets on 8-inch centres. Another owner expects O-track to fit but says it may need shimming because the trim is recessed. On trucks without the rails fitted, drill, countersink and seal every hole.
Tools: Drill · countersink · rivnut tool or bolts · sealant · track sections

#### Diesel harshness at 1,700–2,000 rpm (non-US)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 15 minutes · cost Free
Symptoms: Vibration or harshness at a steady 1,700–2,000 rpm on B57 diesel trucks.
Fix: On a right-hand-drive diesel, one INEOS Forum owner found the 10 mm bolt holding the heat shield between the airbox and firewall loose. Tightening it removed about 90% of the harshness. Others traced rattles to an exhaust heat shield and to the heater pipes under the glovebox. These are owner fixes, not an Ineos bulletin.
Tools: 10 mm socket · flashlight

### Baseline service
Assume nothing was done early: the factory schedule is long (12 months / 12,000 miles in the US), the full service manual isn't sold to owners, and only dealers can reset the service counter. Baseline every fluid once, keep receipts with OEM-spec fluids to protect the 5-year warranty, and note that much of the drivetrain is shared with BMW (B58/B57 engines, ZF 8-speed), so FCP Euro and other BMW specialists carry many of the consumables. On a Quartermaster that has worked hard (towing, a camper or tray load), treat it as arduous use and shorten every interval.
- Engine oil & filter: B58 petrol: 0W-20, ACEA C2 (dealers also cite C5 / API SP), BMW Longlife-17 FE+ · 6.5 L per the manual as quoted by owners; buy 7 L. B57 diesel: 0W-30 (the diesel manual lists Petronas Syntium 7000 E 0W-30) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Factory 12 months / 12,000 mi (US); owners and some dealers recommend 5,000–6,000 mi, or 6,000 mi for heavy use (Hood in maintenance position, engine cover off. 32 mm socket on the canister cap on top of the engine, 17 mm drain plug with a new copper washer, 25 Nm. Owners report the BMW B58 filter fits. Check the level in the menu, not by dipstick.)
- Engine air filter: Panel filter with white felt pre-filter (glued on some, clipped into the box on others) · Every 2 years / 24,000 mi; much sooner after dusty trails (Captive PZ3 screws on the airbox. If the history is unknown, just replace it, because it's cheap.)
- Cabin air filter: OEM INEOS #100326881 · Every annual service (Behind a hinged plate under the passenger footwell (LHD). The glovebox stays in. Arrow toward the cabin.)
- Spark plugs (B58 petrol): BMW B58 plugs · gap/spec [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Dealer schedules list 48,000 mi (or 4 years) (If the truck is near 48k and there's no record, do them now. Plug fitment below is listed for the BMW 340i B58; confirm against the INEOS parts catalogue.)
- Fuel filter (B57 diesel only): [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Every 2 years per dealer schedule (Non-US diesels only. Replace if there's no record, and more often on questionable fuel.)
- Coolant: BMW LC-18 coolant (BMW 83195A42DF3 = Frostox HT-12), 50/50 with distilled water · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Every 4 years per dealer schedule (Don't top up with generic green or older BMW GS 94000 coolant. Owners note many aftermarket brands don't list LC-18.)
- Automatic transmission (ZF 8HP: 8HP51 petrol, 8HP76 diesel): ZF Lifeguard 8 ATF · ≈10.6 L reported by an owner [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Dealer schedule: check every 2 years, replace at 6 years. Owners plan a pan/filter at 40–50k mi. (Do a drain and pan/filter change (the filter is built into the pan), not a flush. The Grenadier pan has a second, smaller pickup port, so aftermarket aluminium pans may not match. Fill level at the right temperature: use the Offroad › Temperatures screen and keep the truck level.)
- Transfer case (Tremec 2-speed): Fuchs Titan Sintopoid 75W-90 (75W-85 also acceptable) · 1.8 L, or 2.64 L if the oil cooler and lines are drained too · Dealer schedule: check every 2 years, replace at 6 years. Owners change it much earlier: one found metal flakes at 800 mi, and some trucks had it changed under recall at ~5,000 km. (O-ring-sealed drain and fill plugs, 15 Nm (owner-reported). Owners quoting the workshop manual say it calls for fill to spill; because the cooler lines drain back, some owners also measure what comes out so they know how much to put back.)
- Front & rear differentials (Carraro axles): SAE 80W-90 GL-5 · 2.1 L per axle (workshop-manual figure quoted on the INEOS Forum). Note: Agile Offroad's diff-cover instructions call for 75W-140. · First change at 12 months / 12,000 mi, then 60,000 mi per the US schedule as quoted by owners. Owners who wade or tow do it every 10,000 mi. (Remove the FILL plug first, because owners have snapped fill plugs after draining. 12 mm hex plugs (M22×1.5), 31 Nm; INEOS plug part GRA-5000-021220 (the O-ring isn't sold separately). The fill plug is magnetic. Same fluid with or without the lockers.)
- Brake fluid: DOT 4 (SAE J1703) · Every 2 years (If the date is unknown, flush it, especially after water crossings.)
- Power steering fluid (hydraulic Bosch box): Penrite LDAS, as cited from an INEOS support document by an Australian owner on the INEOS Forum · [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Check level and condition at every service (The recirculating-ball steering is hydraulic. Owners with big tires and heavy steering look at Owl's upgraded pump. Check for leaks at the box and pump.)
- Suspension retorque, body drains & recalls: Retorque suspension and body mounts; clear the body and safari-hatch drains · At purchase, then every annual service (Dealer first-service packages include a suspension retorque and drain clearing. Run the VIN for open recalls (door button 25V147, steering ball-joint nut 23V903, aux switch panel 23V828) before anything else.)
- Battery & charging: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Test at purchase and every service (Dealers include a battery health test in the annual service. Trucks that sat on a lot often have a tired battery, which causes odd electrical warnings.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: The Quartermaster has the same axles and front suspension as the wagon, and it comes on LT265/70R17 or 255/70R18 (about 32 in.). Wagon owners on the INEOS Forum report 285/70R17 fits without rubbing and 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) fits on stock suspension. DVA Mechanics treats 35s as a 2-inch-lift job. One Quartermaster owner recommends narrow 35s on near-factory offset wheels, such as 255/85R17 or 35×10.5. Because the spare sits in the bed, there's no rear-door clearance problem like on the wagon, but a bigger spare stands taller in the bed. An owner at 7,000 ft stayed at 33s because of power loss on the factory gearing.

Q: How much payload does it have?
A: It depends on market and engine. Ineos quoted 1,675 lb at US launch. In Australia it quotes 907 kg for the petrol and 832 kg for the diesel, against a 3,550 kg GVM. That's below most one-tonne utes and the 79 Series LandCruiser. Expedition Portal says its Trialmaster test truck, with a winch, dual batteries and a bed rack, has a 1,400 lb payload.

Q: How much can it tow?
A: 3,500 kg braked (about 7,700 lb), the same as the wagon, with a 7,000 kg GCM and a 350 kg towball limit in Australian spec. With a heavy trailer and a loaded bed you'll reach the GCM and payload limits before the hitch rating.

Q: Will a Euro pallet really fit?
A: Yes. There's 1,337 mm between the wheel arches, enough for a 1,200 × 800 mm pallet. You have to take the spare wheel out of the bed first.

Q: Where's the spare, and why?
A: It stands upright in the bed. Mounted underneath, it would cut into a departure angle that's already down to 22.6°. Ineos also offers a roof mount and a 15-litre lockable box that fits in the middle of the spare. Owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle.

Q: Can I get the diesel in the US?
A: No. US trucks have only the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six (282 hp, 332 lb-ft). The B57 diesel (183 kW, 550 Nm) is sold in Europe, Australia, New Zealand and other markets.

Q: Why does it cost so much more than the wagon in the US?
A: Mostly the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. At launch the Quartermaster cost $15,400 more than the Station Wagon. When new tariffs arrived in April 2025, total duty rose to 50%. Ineos said it would absorb most of that, but still raised the price 11%, to $94,500 including shipping.

Q: How does it drive compared with the wagon?
A: It's much the same, with a longer turning circle: about 14.5 m against 13.5 m before 2026. Unladen it can feel jittery over small bumps, and it settles with weight in the bed. Expedition Portal found it quieter and more comfortable than the wagon. Top Gear noted the light rear end can lose grip on slippery climbs, which is where the lockers and all-terrain tires help.

Q: What fuel economy does it get?
A: Australian test-cycle (ADR) figures are 12.6 L/100 km for the petrol and 10.5 L/100 km for the diesel. Edmunds lists 14 mpg combined for the 2026 US truck. Towing a big caravan with the B57 diesel Grenadier, Caravan World saw mid-to-high 20s in L/100 km. The tank holds 90 litres. Caravan World says about 10% of Australian Grenadier buyers fit a Brown Davis long-range tank, which adds 78 litres.

Q: Which year should I buy?
A: The engines haven't changed, so the main question is steering. MY2026 trucks have the variable-ratio box, about a 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC and a quicker way to silence the speed-limit chime. Earlier trucks can be fitted with Owl's steering pump upgrade, which Owl says fits both the Grenadier and Quartermaster. Whichever year you buy, run the VIN for recalls. GearJunkie, which drove both, says the Quartermaster got the same 2026 updates and that with the new steering the long-wheelbase truck drives almost like a normal pickup.

Q: What camper and canopy options exist?
A: Dirtbox Overland sells a canopy camper made for the Quartermaster bed for $11,499, and Norweld makes full-length, compact and half canopies plus trays. Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack (375 lb on-road, 200 lb off-road). INEOS Forum owners have fitted Dirtbox caps. Ineos's own accessory list includes a canvas tonneau, a roll-top cover and a hardtop.
