## Jeep Wrangler JL (2018–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jl/
Codes: JL

Verdict: The JL two-door is the most capable short Wrangler Jeep has built, and the most civilized: it's lighter, quicker and quieter than the JK, with an 8-speed that makes the Pentastar feel like it finally found its gearbox. Early trucks had real teething trouble, so buy one with its recalls done and its steering sorted.

Jeep unveiled the JL at the Los Angeles Auto Show on November 29, 2017, and the short two-door, the purest Wrangler, followed the four-door into production at Toledo in early 2018. On paper it changed little: still body-on-frame, still solid axles front and rear, still doors and a windshield that come off. In practice it was a thorough rethink. Wikipedia puts it about 90 kg (198 lb) lighter than the JK, with a lower beltline, bigger windows and a grille whose seven slots lean back like the TJ's.

### WHAT CHANGED UNDERNEATH
The 3.6 Pentastar carried over at 285 hp and 260 lb-ft, now with an optional eTorque mild-hybrid system. It drove through either a six-speed manual or the 850RE eight-speed automatic. A 2.0-liter turbo four with 270 hp and 295 lb-ft arrived later as an eight-speed-only option. Steering stayed recirculating-ball, now with electric pump assistance, and three 4WD systems were offered: part-time Command-Trac, full-time Selec-Trac and the Rubicon's Rock-Trac with 4:1 low range.
The axles were new Dana designs. Way of Life's breakdown lists an M186 front and M200 rear (the familiar 'Dana 30 and Dana 35' sizes) on the Sport and Sahara, an optional M220 rear bundled with the limited slip, and wider M210/M220 Dana 44s with electric lockers on the Rubicon. Quadratec's 2020 specs give the two-door Rubicon 10.8 inches of ground clearance on a 96.8-inch wheelbase, and a 1,000-lb payload.

### A ROUGH START
Early JLs had real problems. Over 18,000 2018–2019 Wranglers were recalled for a poorly welded track-bar bracket, and NHTSA then opened an investigation covering about 270,000 JLs over frame-weld and steering complaints. In August 2019 FCA started fitting a stronger steering damper free of charge, after finding that the original could take in air in the cold and lose damping. Manual trucks were recalled because the clutch pressure plate could overheat, and Jeep later switched the early aluminum steering boxes to cast iron.
None of that stopped the JL from winning the 2019 Four Wheeler SUV of the Year as a Rubicon, along with Motor Trend's SUV of the Year. It even starred in a Super Bowl LII ad, with Jeff Goldblum recreating his Jurassic Park chase in a silver two-door Rubicon.

### THE 2024 REFRESH
For 2024 Jeep gave the JL a mid-cycle update rather than a replacement. Every Wrangler got a 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen, side-curtain airbags for both rows, a slimmer grille with blacked-out slot frames, and an antenna built into the windshield frame so it stops catching branches. Hagerty lists the rest: a factory 8,000-lb Warn winch option, power seats sealed for fording, a full-floating Dana 44 HD rear axle for the Rubicon, 33-inch tires and a rear locker for the Willys, and a new Rubicon X with 35s.
The refreshed two-door still faces the same rivals as before, and more of them: the Ford Bronco, and further up the price list the Defender 90 and the G-Class. None of them has removable doors, a fold-down windshield and solid axles at both ends.

### Data plate
- Platform: JL (two-door)
- Unveiled: Los Angeles Auto Show, November 29, 2017
- Production: Early 2018 – present, Toledo, Ohio
- Engines: 3.6 L Pentastar V6 (eTorque optional) · 2.0 L turbo I4
- Output: 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · 270 hp / 295 lb-ft
- Transmissions: 6-spd manual · 850RE 8-spd automatic
- 4Wd: Command-Trac · Selec-Trac · Rock-Trac 4:1
- Axles: Dana M186 / M200 (M220 opt.) · Rubicon M210 / M220
- Wheelbase: 96.8 in
- Length: 166.3 in
- Ground Clearance: 9.7 in Sport · 10.8 in Rubicon (Quadratec 2020; Jeep quoted 10.9 in at launch)
- Curb Weight: 3,970 lb Sport · 4,160 lb Rubicon (2020)
- Towing / Payload: 2,000 lb / 1,000 lb

### Engineering
The JL keeps a separate ladder frame, coil springs and solid axles at both ends, with a recirculating-ball steering box powered by an electrically driven hydraulic pump. The two-door rides on a 96.8-inch wheelbase. The engines are the 3.6 Pentastar V6, with an optional eTorque belt starter-generator, and a 2.0-liter turbo four.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, 96.8 in wheelbase (166.3 in long. About 90 kg lighter than the JK, per Wikipedia.)
- Front Axle: Dana M186 (Sport/Sahara) · Dana M210 (Rubicon) (Way of Life gives the M186 ring gear as about 7.32 in. The Rubicon axles are 1.5 in wider.)
- Rear Axle: Dana M200 · M220 (limited slip or Rubicon) (From 2024 a full-float Dana 44 HD rear is offered on the Rubicon (Hagerty).)
- 4Wd Systems: Command-Trac · Selec-Trac · Rock-Trac 4:1 (Selec-Trac adds a full-time mode; Rock-Trac is Rubicon-only.)
- Engines: 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 2.0 turbo I4 (285 hp / 260 lb-ft; 270 hp / 295 lb-ft. eTorque mild hybrid optional on the V6, standard on the early 2.0.)
- Transmissions: 6-speed manual · 8-speed 850RE automatic (The 2.0T is automatic-only.)

### Versions
- 2018–2023 · JL 2-door 3.6 · 3.6 L Pentastar V6 (eTorque optional) · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto. Early trucks: track-bar weld, damper and steering-box fixes.
- 2018–2023 · JL 2-door 2.0T · 2.0 L turbo I4 · 270 hp / 295 lb-ft · 8-speed automatic only. Wikipedia says the eTorque version of the 2.0 was dropped in 2020.
- 2018–2023 · JL Rubicon 2-door · As above · — · M210/M220 Dana 44s with lockers, Rock-Trac 4:1, sway-bar disconnect, LT285/70R17 tires.
- 2024– · JL 2-door (refresh) · 2.0 L turbo I4 · 3.6 L V6 · As above · 12.3-in Uconnect 5, side-curtain airbags, new grille, windshield-frame antenna, Warn winch option.
- 2024– · Rubicon X 2-door · 2.0T / 3.6 · — · 35-in tires, steel bumpers, front camera and a full-time Rock-Trac case (The Drive, Hagerty).
- 2024– · Willys 2-door · 2.0T / 3.6 · — · 33-in all-terrains, standard rear locker, 2.72:1 low range.

### Year-by-year
- 2018: JL launch (four-door production from November 2017, two-door from early 2018): 3.6 Pentastar with a 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto, plus a 2.0 turbo with eTorque (auto only). The year to be wary of: NHTSA recalls cover track-bar bracket welds (18V-675), the intermediate steering shaft weld (18V-343) and rear frame-rail corrosion (18V-231), manual trucks are in the clutch recalls, and SlashGear counts more than 1,000 owner complaints, mostly highway wander. Buy one only with every fix documented [avoid]
- 2020: 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp) arrives, four-door only; later subject to high-pressure fuel pump recalls
- 2021: Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid (375 hp, 21-mile EV range) and Rubicon 392 (6.4 Hemi, 470 hp), both four-door only. Xtreme Recon package (35s, 4.56 gears, 1.5 in lift) for the four-door Rubicon and 392; 4.88 axles optional on Rubicon.
- 2023: Lower-priced Willys 4xe; Rubicon 20th Anniversary edition
- 2024: Facelift: new grille (except Sport/Sport S), standard 12-inch Uconnect 5, new Rubicon X trim. Xtreme 35 package reaches the two-door. EcoDiesel dropped. Rubicon 392 'Final Edition'.
- 2025: Rubicon 392 continues, still badged 'Final Edition'; Stellantis drops the 4xe from the US market (Wikipedia)
- 2026: Moab 392 tops the range (four-door only); reworked door hinges for easier removal; 3.6 still offered with the manual; no 4xe in the US

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: 245/75R17 (Sport), 255/70R18 (Sahara), LT285/70R17 (Rubicon), LT315/70R17 (Xtreme 35 package, 2024+)
- Bolt Pattern: 5x127 (5x5")
- Offset: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] — factory offsets not verified from a manufacturer or supplier source
- Center Bore: 71.5 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5
- Lug Torque: 130 lb-ft (176 N·m), 22 mm socket (Northridge4x4, owner's-manual figure); spare [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 33 in (e.g. 285/70R17); 35 in on Rubicon with bump-stop spacers (A 35 clears a Rubicon at ride height but rubs the inner fenders on compression and at full lock. Bump-stop extensions fix it at the cost of about 2 in of up-travel. On Sport and Sahara, a 33 is the sensible stock limit.)
- Biggest tire, 1.5 in (factory Xtreme 35) lift: LT315/70R17 (35 in) (Jeep's factory Xtreme 35 package for the two-door from 2024, on Rubicon and Willys with the 2.0 turbo only ($4,495): 1.5 in lift, 4.56 gears, 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels and a reinforced swing gate. Standard on the 2.0T two-door Rubicon X.)
- Biggest tire, 2–2.5 in lift: 35 in (What Sport and Sahara need for 35s, together with bump stops and a wheel with about 4.5–5.0 in backspacing.)

### Buying checks
- Run the VIN for recalls before anything else: JL recalls include the 2018–2019 track-bar bracket weld (18V-675), the manual-clutch pressure plate (20V-124, 21V-028 and 23V-116), the 2018 transmission park-lock rod (18V-280) and cruise-control software (18V-332) campaigns, and the 2021–2025 power-steering pump wiring fire risk (26V-363). Make sure they've all been done.
- Feel the steering at highway speed: Vague, light or wandering steering on a 2018–2020 truck points to the early aluminum steering box (owners cite TSB 08-074-20). A shake after bumps points to the damper, track bar or worn front-end parts.
- Look at the track-bar welds: ExtremeTerrain warns 2018 owners to be 'mindful of the track bar to body weld.' Check both track-bar brackets for cracks and the frame welds for poor penetration, which is what owners complained about to NHTSA.
- Manual trucks: clutch history: Ask whether the clutch recall was done, test for slip in a high gear at low revs, and smell for a cooked clutch after a short climb.
- Peek at the valley on a 3.6: Oil weeping at the back of the engine, under the intake, means the oil cooler/filter housing is going.
- 2.0T: coolant level and plug receipts: Check the coolant bottle and turbo lines for leaks, and ask for proof of the 30,000-mile spark plug changes the factory schedule calls for.
- eTorque: listen for start-stop faults: Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists early auxiliary-battery failures as a known JL issue, with flickering dash lights and random warnings.
- Decide whether you need the 2024 refresh: The 2024 update brought side-curtain airbags, the 12.3-inch screen and the full-float rear axle option. A 2018–2023 truck with its fixes done is the value buy.

### Common repairs
#### Fix steering wobble: damper, track bar, then the rest
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours to inspect and fit a damper · cost Free damper replacement on affected early trucks under FCA's 2019 customer-satisfaction program; otherwise a damper or track bar
Symptoms: Front-end shimmy or full death wobble after a bump at 45–65 mph, with the steering wheel shaking side to side.
Fix: On 2018–2019 trucks, check the history first. In August 2019 FCA began offering a stronger steering damper at no charge. FCA said its engineers found air could get into the original damper in cold weather, when the oil thickens, so it lost damping. Its Customer Satisfaction Notification V41 covered about 192,000 2018–2019 JLs. Then inspect the front end the same way as on any solid-axle Jeep: have a helper rock the wheel while you watch both ends of the track bar, then check the tie-rod and drag-link ends, ball joints, control-arm bushings and wheel bearings. Replace worn parts, torque everything at ride height, and get an alignment. A damper on its own masks wobble; it doesn't cure it.
Tools: Helper · torque wrench · sockets · jack and stands.

#### Replace a loose aluminum steering box (TSB 08-074-20)
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours plus an alignment check · cost JLWranglerForums members report dealer quotes of $1,500+ out of warranty
Symptoms: Light, vague, loose steering and wandering on the highway, sometimes with play you can see at the pitman arm. One owner described it as 'super light, vague and loose' at nearly 100,000 miles.
Fix: Early JLs used an aluminum steering gear, and Quadratec says Jeep moved to cast-iron boxes. Owners on JLWranglerForums cite TSB 08-074-20 for the swap (we couldn't see the bulletin itself), who also note it won't cure death wobble by itself. DIY: disconnect the battery, mark and remove the pitman arm with a puller, unbolt the intermediate shaft, disconnect the pressure and return lines (catch the fluid), then unbolt the box from the frame. Fit the new box with new bolts, refill and bleed the system with the specified fluid, and center the steering wheel.
Tools: Pitman-arm puller · line wrenches · large sockets · torque wrench · drain pan · power steering fluid.

#### Clutch: check the recall, then replace if it slips
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time ≈ A long day (transmission out) · cost Recall work is free; an out-of-warranty clutch kit plus labor
Symptoms: Slipping under load, a burning smell, or a clutch-overheat warning after crawling. Recall 20V-124 covered manual Wranglers built from August 23, 2017 to February 13, 2020 because the pressure plate could overheat, fracture and, in the worst case, start a fire.
Fix: Run the VIN through NHTSA first. TFLcar reported 29,818 Wranglers in the original recall, and later recalls widened it: 21V-028 (2018–2021 manuals) and 23V-116 (2018–2023 manuals), with 24V-572 re-flashing some 2021 trucks already fixed under 23V-116. If the recall work has been done and the clutch is simply worn, support the transmission and transfer case, remove the driveshafts, crossmember and exhaust as needed, and drop the transmission. Replace the clutch disc, pressure plate and release bearing, and check the flywheel. Bleed the hydraulics, and replace the slave cylinder while the transmission is out.
Tools: Transmission jack · alignment tool · torque wrench · brake bleeder · a friend.

#### Replace a leaking Pentastar oil cooler / filter housing
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 4–6 hours · cost Housing assembly plus gaskets, coolant and oil
Symptoms: Oil, and sometimes coolant, pooling in the valley under the intake and running down the back of the engine. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists cracked Pentastar oil-filter housings and cooler adapters as a known JL issue.
Fix: The job follows the JK procedure. Remove the engine cover and intake plumbing, the upper and lower intake manifolds, and the cooler's sensors and bolts. Clean the valley, fit the new housing with new seals, then refill the oil and coolant and check for leaks. Torque the oil filter cap to 18 ft-lb; overtightening is a suspected contributor to cracking.
Tools: External-Torx and metric sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose pliers · shop towels to plug the intake ports.

#### Fix 2.0T coolant hose leaks
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours · cost A Mopar hose and coolant
Symptoms: A dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or crusty residue around the turbo coolant lines or the coolant bottle hoses on a 2.0 turbo. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists a TSB for turbo coolant return line leaks.
Fix: Pressure-test the cold system to find the leak. Drain enough coolant to get below the leak, replace the hose and its clips, refill with OAT coolant and bleed the loop. Remember the 2.0T has a separate intercooler loop. Check the dealer history too, since the TSB repair may already have been done.
Tools: Cooling-system pressure tester · hose-clamp pliers · drain pan · Mopar OAT coolant.

#### Replace a front hub and bearing
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours per side · cost A hub assembly per side
Symptoms: A speed-related growl, play when you rock the wheel top to bottom, or an ABS fault. Worn bearings are also on every death-wobble checklist.
Fix: Lift the corner, remove the wheel, caliper and rotor, unplug the ABS sensor, remove the axle nut and the hub-to-knuckle bolts, and pull the hub. Clean the knuckle bore, fit the new hub, and torque to the factory specification.
Tools: Axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · wire brush · anti-seize.

#### Press in new front ball joints
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time ≈ A day for both sides · cost Ball-joint kit plus an alignment
Symptoms: Clunks, wander, uneven tire wear, or movement when you rock a lifted wheel top to bottom. It's more common on lifted trucks with heavy tires.
Fix: Remove the hub, axle shaft and knuckle, press out the old upper and lower joints with a JL-specific adapter set, press in the new ones square, and reassemble. Torque everything to the factory specs and finish with an alignment.
Tools: Ball-joint press with JL adapters · breaker bar · torque wrench · pickle fork.

### Baseline service
Baseline a used JL by engine. The 3.6 Pentastar, the 2.0 turbo use different oils, plugs and cooling loops, and the 8-speed takes ZF-spec fluid, not ATF+4. Before spending money, run the VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup: JLs have had recalls for frame welds, clutches, power-steering pumps. Then change the gear oil, which owners skip most.
- Engine oil & filter: 3.6: 5 qt SAE 0W-20 meeting MS-6395 · 2.0T: 5 qt full-synthetic SAE 5W-30, API SN PLUS (Mopar MS-13340) · Then per the oil-life monitor [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (The JL Pentastar takes a quart less, and a thinner grade, than the JK's: Quadratec specifies the Mopar MO-349 (68191349AA) cartridge, the 24 mm cap torqued to 18 ft-lb and the 13 mm drain plug to 20 ft-lb. The owner's-manual sheet warns that non-SN PLUS oil in the 2.0T 'can cause engine damage not covered by the vehicle warranty.')
- Engine air filter: Panel filter · Way of Life's index of the factory schedule lists it at 30,000 mi; sooner on dusty trails (Check the airbox seal after any off-road trip in fine dust.)
- Cabin air filter: Behind the glovebox · Every 20,000 mi in the factory schedule (Way of Life index) (Diesel trucks use a different part.)
- Spark plugs: 3.6: Mopar SP225755AA (2018–20) · 2.0T: Mopar 68292346AA · gaps per the 2020 manual sheet: 3.6 0.043 in, 2.0T 0.024–0.025 in · 3.6 at 100,000 mi; 2.0T every 30,000 mi (Way of Life index of the factory schedule) (The 2.0T's 30,000-mile plug interval is easy to miss on a used truck, so ask for receipts.)
- Coolant (engine, intercooler, eTorque/battery loops): Mopar 10-year/150,000-mile OAT (MS.90032) · 3.6 engine: 11.2 qt (10.6 L), plus 1.9 qt motor-generator and 2.5 qt battery loops on eTorque trucks · 2.0T engine: 10.3 qt (9.7 L), plus a 3.2–3.5 qt intercooler loop · Flush at 10 years or 150,000 mi (factory schedule per Way of Life) (The 2.0T and eTorque trucks have more than one cooling loop, and the owner's-manual sheet lists separate capacities for the intercooler, the motor-generator unit and the battery. Bleed each one correctly.)
- 8-speed automatic (850RE / ZF 8HP): Mopar ZF 8&9 Speed ATF · about 9 L total (8HP50 figure on the owner's-manual sheet) · KBB's schedule lists transmission fluids at 100,000 mi (This is not ATF+4. The level is set hot at the fill plug, so it's a shop job for most owners. Mopar also sells a JL transmission filter.)
- 6-speed manual: Mopar ATF+4 · 2.25 L · Every 30,000 mi under severe use (factory schedule per Way of Life) (Before you buy a manual truck, check that the clutch recall has been done.)
- Transfer case (Command-Trac / Rock-Trac / Selec-Trac): Mopar ATF+4 · ≈1.6 L part-time cases, ≈1.76 L full-time Selec-Trac · Inspect at 30,000 mi; replace at 60,000 mi under severe use or 150,000 mi normally (Way of Life index) (If you use low range on the trail, treat the severe-service interval as normal.)
- Front axle: GL-5 75W-85 (later manuals; the 2018 manual listed 80W-90) · M186/Dana 30: 0.86 L · M210/Dana 44: 1.03 L · Every 40,000 mi under severe use (Way of Life index); after any deep water crossing (JL front axles take very little oil, so a slightly low level matters.)
- Rear axle: M220/Dana 44: GL-5 75W-85, 1.45 L (1.36 L with Trac-Lok) · M200/'Dana 35': 1.15 L of synthetic 75W-140 per the 2020 owner's-manual sheet · Trac-Lok axles need 70 ml (2.37 oz) of Mopar limited-slip additive · Every 40,000 mi under severe use (Way of Life index) (Check which rear axle you have before buying oil (see the axle FAQ). Synthetic 75W-140 is the usual towing upgrade.)
- Power steering fluid: Mopar electric steering pump fluid (2020 owner's-manual sheet) · Check the level at every oil change (JLWranglerForums members warn against topping up with ATF+4, even though some charts list it. Check for the 2021–2025 power-steering pump recall (26V-363).)
- Brake & clutch fluid: Mopar DOT 3 (DOT 4 acceptable) · Flush on purchase, then every 2–3 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Manual trucks share the fluid type in the clutch master cylinder.)
- Driveline & front-end inspection: CV and U-joints, tie-rod ends, front suspension · Every 20,000 mi (factory schedule per Way of Life) (Lug nuts are 130 ft-lb (22 mm socket). Re-torque the track bar and steering hardware after any lift.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: On a Rubicon, 35s. Driving Line ran 35x12.50R17s on a stock-height JL Rubicon with JKS bump-stop spacers and the stock flares. They cleared on level ground but hit the inner fenders when flexed, and the spacers cost about 2 inches of up-travel. On a Sport or Sahara, the realistic answer is a 33 with a wheel change; 35s on those trims usually need bump stops, less backspacing and often a 2–2.5-inch lift. Driving Line's test truck was a four-door, but the two-door uses the same axles and flares.

Q: 3.6 V6 or 2.0 turbo?
A: The 2.0T makes more torque (295 against 260 lb-ft), and the EPA rated the 2018 two-door 2.0T at 23/25 mpg against 18/23 for the 3.6 automatic (17/25 manual). It's automatic-only, has extra cooling loops and needs spark plugs every 30,000 miles. The Pentastar is the one with a manual option and a long, well-understood service history.

Q: How much can a two-door JL tow?
A: Quadratec lists 2,000 lb for every two-door trim, against 3,500 lb for the four-door.

Q: What's the payload?
A: Quadratec's 2020–2021 specs list 1,000 lb for the two-door. Check the door-jamb sticker on the truck in front of you.

Q: Which axles do I have?
A: Sport and Sahara: Dana M186 front and M200 rear, with an M220 rear if the limited slip was ordered. Rubicon: wider M210 front and M220 rear with electric lockers. Way of Life notes the Sahara always has the 186 front.

Q: Is death wobble still a thing on the JL?
A: Yes. Any solid front axle can do it. FCA offered early JL owners a stronger steering damper in 2019, and later fixes addressed the track-bar welds and the steering box. A worn or loose track bar, ball joints or tie-rod ends are still the usual cause, and Quadratec warns that a new damper alone only hides it.

Q: What oil does the JL Pentastar take?
A: Five quarts of 0W-20 meeting MS-6395, with the Mopar MO-349 cartridge filter. That's a quart less and a thinner grade than the JK, so don't copy JK numbers. The 2.0T takes 5 quarts of full-synthetic 5W-30 rated API SN PLUS.

Q: What changed with the 2024 refresh?
A: A 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen on every model, first- and second-row side-curtain airbags, a new grille, an antenna built into the windshield frame, an available 8,000-lb Warn winch, power seats, a Dana 44 HD full-float rear axle on the Rubicon, a better-equipped Willys, and a new Rubicon X with 35s.

Q: Which years should I avoid?
A: 2018, mainly. SlashGear counted 11 recalls and more than 1,000 owner complaints for the 2018 Wrangler, most about wandering at highway speed, and says steering complaints carried on, less often, for two more years. NHTSA's 2018 list includes track-bar bracket welds (18V-675, also 2019), the intermediate steering shaft (18V-343) and rear frame-rail corrosion (18V-231), and manual trucks from 2018 on are covered by the clutch recalls (20V-124, 21V-028, 23V-116). Quadratec says Jeep later moved from aluminum to cast-iron steering boxes. No later year is a write-off: buy any JL with its recalls and steering fixes documented.

Q: Is the JL safe?
A: It's better equipped than any earlier Wrangler: side airbags and stronger B-pillars from launch, and side-curtain airbags from 2024. But Euro NCAP gave it 1 star in 2018, and the IIHS rated the four-door Marginal after it tipped over in the small-overlap test.

## Jeep Wrangler JL Unlimited (2018–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jl-unlimited/
Codes: JL Unlimited, 4xe, 392

Verdict: The four-door JL is the Wrangler with a choice of engines: a diesel, a plug-in hybrid and a 470-hp Hemi V8, all with solid axles and doors that come off. Pick the powertrain that suits how you travel, and check the recalls first. Several of them tell you to park outside.

The four-door was the JL that mattered most, so it came first: Wrangler Unlimited production began at Toledo in November 2017, months ahead of the two-door, and it ran alongside the outgoing JK Unlimited until April 2018 so dealers could keep up with demand. It grew 3.5 inches in overall length over the JK Unlimited, to 188.4 inches on a 118.4-inch wheelbase, while losing weight. It kept the separate frame, the solid axles and the removable doors. Then, over the next few years, Jeep gave it more powertrains than any Wrangler before.

### DIESEL, HYBRID, HEMI
Launch engines were the 285-hp 3.6 Pentastar, with optional eTorque, and the 270-hp 2.0 turbo four. For 2020 North America got the VM-built 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 with 260 hp and 443 lb-ft (600 Nm). It was dropped for 2024. The 4xe plug-in hybrid followed for 2021: the 2.0 turbo plus electric motors and a 17 kWh battery, for 375 hp, 470 lb-ft and an EPA-rated 21 miles of electric range.
Also for 2021 came the Rubicon 392, with the 6.4-liter Hemi V8 from Dodge's Scat Pack cars making 470 hp and 470 lb-ft. Quadratec's specs show it uses the full-time Selec-Trac case and the heavier ZF 8HP75 automatic rather than the Rubicon's Rock-Trac. Its 1,351-lb payload is the highest in the range. Jeep announced 'final editions' for 2024 and 2025, then reversed course in August 2025: CEO Bob Broderdorf said the 392 would stay, and a V8 Gladiator would join it.

### THE FAMILY OVERLANDER
For overlanders the Unlimited is the obvious JL. It tows 3,500 lb, or 5,000 lb with the 2024 full-float Dana 44 HD rear axle and the automatic on non-4xe trucks, and it has a cargo area that takes a fridge and drawers. Payload is the limit: Quadratec lists 880 lb for a 2020 Sahara and 892 lb for a Rubicon, so a steel-bumpered, roof-racked build overruns it fast. The JL Unlimited is also the basis for the Gladiator pickup, which borrows its styling and interior.
It isn't perfect. The IIHS rated it Marginal in the small-overlap crash test after a 2020 Unlimited rolled onto its side, and a 2022 retest ended the same way. The 4xe has been recalled for battery fire risk, and 2021–2025 trucks have been recalled for power-steering pump wiring. Both recalls told owners to park outside until repaired.

### 2024 AND BEYOND
The 2024 refresh brought the four-door the same updates as the two-door: a 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen, side-curtain airbags in both rows, a new grille, a windshield-frame antenna, an available Warn winch and the Rubicon X with 35s. The 4xe gained a cheaper Sport S trim and a four-outlet 'Power Box'. Wikipedia reports that Stellantis then dropped the Wrangler 4xe from the US market in 2025. The JL Unlimited competes with the Bronco, the Defender 110, the Ineos Grenadier and the sixth-gen 4Runner, and it's still the only one with doors you can leave at home.

### Data plate
- Platform: JL (Wrangler Unlimited, four-door)
- Production: November 2017 – present, Toledo, Ohio
- Engines: 3.6 V6 · 2.0T I4 · 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (2020–23) · 4xe PHEV (2021–) · 6.4 Hemi V8 (2021–)
- Max Output: 470 hp / 470 lb-ft (Rubicon 392)
- Transmissions: 850RE 8-spd auto · ZF 8HP75 (392) · 6-spd manual
- 4Wd: Command-Trac · Selec-Trac · Rock-Trac 4:1
- Wheelbase: 118.4 in
- Length: 188.4 in
- Ground Clearance: 9.7 in Sport · 10.8 in Rubicon/392
- Curb Weight: 4,201 lb Sport · 4,439 lb Rubicon · 5,103 lb 392
- Towing: 3,500 lb · 5,000 lb with 2024+ Dana 44 HD rear (auto, non-4xe)
- 4Xe Battery: 17 kWh · 21 mi EPA electric range
- Fuel Tank: 21.5 gal (gas)

### Engineering
The JL Unlimited uses the JL's ladder frame, coil springs and solid axles on a 118.4-inch wheelbase. It has offered the widest engine choice of any Wrangler: gas V6, turbo four, diesel V6, a plug-in hybrid and a Hemi V8, all through 8-speed automatics, plus a six-speed manual on the Pentastar.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, 118.4 in wheelbase (188.4 in long; 3.5 in longer than the JK Unlimited (Wikipedia).)
- Axles: Dana M186/M200 · Rubicon & 392: M210/M220 Dana 44s (An M220 rear comes with the optional limited slip; a full-float Dana 44 HD rear was offered on the Rubicon from 2024.)
- 4Wd: Command-Trac · Selec-Trac · Rock-Trac 4:1 (The Rubicon 392 uses full-time Selec-Trac (MP3022) instead of Rock-Trac; Selec-Trac is otherwise a Sahara option.)
- Engines: 3.6 V6 · 2.0T I4 · 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 · 4xe · 6.4 Hemi V8 (285 · 270 · 260 hp (443 lb-ft) · 375 hp / 470 lb-ft combined · 470 hp / 470 lb-ft.)
- 4Xe Hybrid: 17 kWh lithium-ion battery (EPA 21-mile electric range and 49 MPGe.)
- Transmissions: 8-speed automatics (850RE, ZF 8HP75 on 392) · 6-speed manual (The manual is offered only with the gas engines.)

### Versions
- 2018– · JLU 3.6 · 3.6 L Pentastar V6 (eTorque optional) · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto. Production began November 2017.
- 2018– · JLU 2.0T · 2.0 L turbo I4 · 270 hp / 295 lb-ft · 8-speed auto only; Quadratec lists 23/25 mpg.
- 2020–2023 · JLU EcoDiesel · 3.0 L VM V6 turbodiesel · 260 hp / 443 lb-ft · North America; dropped for 2024. Recall 23V-263 for the high-pressure fuel pump on some 2021–23 trucks.
- 2021–2025 (US) · JLU 4xe · 2.0 turbo + electric motors, 17 kWh · 375 hp / 470 lb-ft · 21-mile EPA electric range. Battery fire recalls. Sport S 4xe added for 2024.
- 2021– · Rubicon 392 · 6.4 L Hemi V8 · 470 hp / 470 lb-ft · Selec-Trac full-time 4WD, ZF 8HP75. 'Final Edition' for 2025, then confirmed to continue.
- 2024– · JLU (refresh) · As above, less the EcoDiesel · — · 12.3-in screen, side curtains, Rubicon X, Warn winch, Dana 44 HD full-float rear (5,000-lb towing).

### Year-by-year
- 2018: JL launch (four-door production from November 2017, two-door from early 2018): 3.6 Pentastar with a 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto, plus a 2.0 turbo with eTorque (auto only). The year to be wary of: NHTSA recalls cover track-bar bracket welds (18V-675), the intermediate steering shaft weld (18V-343) and rear frame-rail corrosion (18V-231), manual trucks are in the clutch recalls, and SlashGear counts more than 1,000 owner complaints, mostly highway wander. Buy one only with every fix documented [avoid]
- 2020: 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp) arrives, four-door only; later subject to high-pressure fuel pump recalls
- 2021: Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid (375 hp, 21-mile EV range) and Rubicon 392 (6.4 Hemi, 470 hp), both four-door only. Xtreme Recon package (35s, 4.56 gears, 1.5 in lift) for the four-door Rubicon and 392; 4.88 axles optional on Rubicon.
- 2023: Lower-priced Willys 4xe; Rubicon 20th Anniversary edition
- 2024: Facelift: new grille (except Sport/Sport S), standard 12-inch Uconnect 5, new Rubicon X trim. Xtreme 35 package reaches the two-door. EcoDiesel dropped. Rubicon 392 'Final Edition'.
- 2025: Rubicon 392 continues, still badged 'Final Edition'; Stellantis drops the 4xe from the US market (Wikipedia)
- 2026: Moab 392 tops the range (four-door only); reworked door hinges for easier removal; 3.6 still offered with the manual; no 4xe in the US

### Capability
- Towing: 3,500 lb (1,588 kg) (gas, diesel and 4xe)
- Fuel tank: 21.5 gal (81 L) (17.2 gal (65 L) on the 4xe)
- Ground clearance: 9.7–10.8 in (246–274 mm) (Sport to Rubicon; 12.9 in (328 mm) with the Xtreme Recon package)
- Approach / departure / breakover: 43.9° / 37° / 22.6° (Rubicon; 47.4° / 40.4° / 26.7° with the Xtreme Recon package)
- Wading depth: 30 in (76 cm) (31.5 in on Rubicon 4xe; 33.6 in with the Xtreme Recon package)
- Fuel economy: EPA 22 mpg combined (2.0 turbo, 2022) (4xe: EPA 49 MPGe / 20 mpg combined; 21-mile electric range at launch, 22 miles for 2022)
- Curb weight: 4,196–4,478 lb (1,903–2,031 kg) (2.0 turbo Sport to Rubicon; 4xe 5,049–5,265 lb)
- Turning circle: 39.4 ft (12.0 m) (curb to curb, 2021 spec)
- Wheelbase: 118.4 in (3,007 mm)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: P245/75R17 (Sport), P255/70R18 (Sahara), 255/55R20 (Sahara 4xe), LT285/70R17 (Rubicon, Rubicon 4xe), LT315/70R17 (Xtreme Recon package; Performance Plus says current Rubicon 392s ship on them)
- Bolt Pattern: 5x127 (5x5")
- Offset: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] — factory offsets not verified from a manufacturer or supplier source
- Center Bore: 71.5 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5
- Lug Torque: 130 lb-ft (176 N·m), 22 mm socket (Northridge4x4, owner's-manual figure); spare [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 33 in; 35 in on gas Rubicon with bump-stop spacers (A 35 clears a gas Rubicon at ride height but rubs the inner fenders under compression; bump stops fix it at the cost of about 2 in of up-travel. Performance Plus Tire says Jeep lists the Rubicon 4xe with about 2.1 in less running clearance (it's 600-plus lb heavier on the same springs), so bump stops are a must.)
- Biggest tire, 1.5 in (factory Xtreme Recon) lift: LT315/70R17 (35 in) (Jeep's factory package from 2021 for the four-door Rubicon and 392: 1.5 in lift, 4.56 gears and 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels.)
- Biggest tire, 2–2.5 in lift: 35 in (What Sport and Sahara (and the 4xe) need for 35s, together with bump stops and about 4.5–5.0 in backspacing.)

### Buying checks
- Run the VIN for every recall: Look for the frame and track-bar welds and the steering damper on 2018–19 trucks, the clutch on manuals, the 2018 park-lock rod (18V-280) and cruise-control software (18V-332) campaigns, the power-steering pump (26V-363, 2021–2025), the 4xe battery (24V-720 / 25V-741) and the EcoDiesel fuel pump (22V-767 and 23V-263). Get dealer printouts showing they're complete.
- 4xe: test the charging: Plug it in. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk says owners often complain the 4xe won't charge from an outlet, blaming software, connections or an overheating control module.
- EcoDiesel: fuel and emissions history: Ask for fuel-filter receipts and the recall record. A high-pressure pump failure is expensive, and debris contamination is what the recall addressed.
- 392: it's a different 4WD system: The 392 uses full-time Selec-Trac and the ZF 8HP75, not Rock-Trac. Check the differential and transfer-case fluids. KBB put a new 2025 Rubicon 392 at $101,990, so price used ones against the trim and condition.
- Steering feel: Wandering or vague steering on 2018–2020 trucks points to the early aluminum steering box (owners cite TSB 08-074-20). Shake after bumps points to the damper, track bar or worn joints.
- Pentastar oil cooler: Look for oil in the engine valley and down the back of the block.
- Payload versus build: Read the door sticker, then add up the bumpers, winch, rack, drawers and passengers. Quadratec lists 880–1,351 lb for 2020–21 four-doors depending on trim.
- Do you want the 2024 updates?: Side-curtain airbags, the bigger screen, a 5,000-lb tow option and the factory winch all arrived for 2024, the same year the EcoDiesel disappeared.

### Common repairs
#### Fix steering wobble: damper, track bar, then the rest
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours to inspect and fit a damper · cost Free damper replacement on affected early trucks under FCA's 2019 customer-satisfaction program; otherwise a damper or track bar
Symptoms: Front-end shimmy or full death wobble after a bump at 45–65 mph, with the steering wheel shaking side to side.
Fix: On 2018–2019 trucks, check the history first. In August 2019 FCA began offering a stronger steering damper at no charge. FCA said its engineers found air could get into the original damper in cold weather, when the oil thickens, so it lost damping. Its Customer Satisfaction Notification V41 covered about 192,000 2018–2019 JLs. Then inspect the front end the same way as on any solid-axle Jeep: have a helper rock the wheel while you watch both ends of the track bar, then check the tie-rod and drag-link ends, ball joints, control-arm bushings and wheel bearings. Replace worn parts, torque everything at ride height, and get an alignment. A damper on its own masks wobble; it doesn't cure it.
Tools: Helper · torque wrench · sockets · jack and stands.

#### Replace a loose aluminum steering box (TSB 08-074-20)
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours plus an alignment check · cost JLWranglerForums members report dealer quotes of $1,500+ out of warranty
Symptoms: Light, vague, loose steering and wandering on the highway, sometimes with play you can see at the pitman arm. One owner described it as 'super light, vague and loose' at nearly 100,000 miles.
Fix: Early JLs used an aluminum steering gear, and Quadratec says Jeep moved to cast-iron boxes. Owners on JLWranglerForums cite TSB 08-074-20 for the swap (we couldn't see the bulletin itself), who also note it won't cure death wobble by itself. DIY: disconnect the battery, mark and remove the pitman arm with a puller, unbolt the intermediate shaft, disconnect the pressure and return lines (catch the fluid), then unbolt the box from the frame. Fit the new box with new bolts, refill and bleed the system with the specified fluid, and center the steering wheel.
Tools: Pitman-arm puller · line wrenches · large sockets · torque wrench · drain pan · power steering fluid.

#### Replace a leaking Pentastar oil cooler / filter housing
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 4–6 hours · cost Housing assembly plus gaskets, coolant and oil
Symptoms: Oil, and sometimes coolant, pooling in the valley under the intake and running down the back of the engine. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists cracked Pentastar oil-filter housings and cooler adapters as a known JL issue.
Fix: The job follows the JK procedure. Remove the engine cover and intake plumbing, the upper and lower intake manifolds, and the cooler's sensors and bolts. Clean the valley, fit the new housing with new seals, then refill the oil and coolant and check for leaks. Torque the oil filter cap to 18 ft-lb; overtightening is a suspected contributor to cracking.
Tools: External-Torx and metric sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose pliers · shop towels to plug the intake ports.

#### Power-steering pump: recall check, then replacement
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2 hours DIY; recall work at the dealer · cost Free under recall 26V-363 where it applies; otherwise a Mopar pump
Symptoms: Loss of power assist or a 'Service Power Steering' message. AARP reports that the June 2026 recall covers about 1,077,000 2021–2025 Wranglers and Gladiators whose electro-hydraulic pump connection can overheat and start a fire, even when parked. Owners were told to park outside until it's fixed, and at least 51 fires were linked to the fault.
Fix: Check the VIN on nhtsa.gov first. If the recall applies, the dealer inspects and repairs or replaces parts free of charge, so don't DIY around it. For an out-of-warranty pump failure on a truck that isn't covered: disconnect the battery, drain the reservoir, unplug the pump's electrical connector and pressure/return lines, unbolt the pump, fit the new one, then refill with the Mopar electric steering pump fluid listed in the manual and bleed by turning lock to lock with the engine running.
Tools: Line wrenches · drain pan · sockets · the specified power steering fluid.

#### EcoDiesel: fuel-pump recall and fuel-filter service
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour for the filter · cost Recall work free; a fuel filter for routine service
Symptoms: Stalling, hard starting or a diesel smell. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists recall 23V-263 for possible high-pressure fuel pump failure on some 2021–2023 EcoDiesels, where debris in the fuel system can cause a stall or a fuel leak.
Fix: Confirm the recall has been done. Then treat the fuel filter as a wear item, because the 3.0's high-pressure pump hates water and dirt. Relieve the pressure, change the filter, prime the system as the service manual describes, and check for leaks. Use only ultra-low-sulfur diesel; the owner's-manual sheet allows biodiesel up to B5, or B7 with shorter service intervals.
Tools: Filter wrench · drain pan · rags · service manual for the priming procedure.

#### Fix 2.0T / 4xe coolant hose leaks
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours · cost A Mopar hose and coolant
Symptoms: A dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or crusty residue around the turbo coolant lines or the coolant bottle hoses on a 2.0 turbo (the 4xe uses the same 2.0 turbo engine). Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists a TSB for turbo coolant return line leaks.
Fix: Pressure-test the cold system to find the leak. Drain enough coolant to get below the leak, replace the hose and its clips, refill with OAT coolant and bleed the loop. Remember the 2.0T has a separate intercooler loop, and that the 4xe also has high-voltage battery cooling. Leave anything orange-cabled to a trained technician. Check the dealer history too, since the TSB repair may already have been done.
Tools: Cooling-system pressure tester · hose-clamp pliers · drain pan · Mopar OAT coolant.

#### Re-spring for an overland load
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours for rear coils; a day for a full kit · cost A pair of coils, or a heavy-load lift kit
Symptoms: Rear sag, bottoming out on washboard, or the truck sitting on its bump stops once the drawers, fridge and water are loaded. Payload can be as low as 880 lb (Quadratec lists that for the 2020 Sahara four-door).
Fix: Weigh the loaded truck at a scale first. Then fit springs rated for the real load: support the frame, unbolt the shocks and sway-bar links, lower the axle, swap the coils, and refit at ride height before torquing the bushings. For a permanently heavy build, a heavy-load kit with matched shocks is the better answer. Re-check the track bar and alignment afterwards.
Tools: Floor jack and stands · sockets · torque wrench · access to a vehicle scale.

### Baseline service
Baseline a used JL by engine. The 3.6 Pentastar, the 2.0 turbo, the 3.0 EcoDiesel, the 4xe and the 392 use different oils, plugs and cooling loops, and the 8-speed takes ZF-spec fluid, not ATF+4. Before spending money, run the VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup: JLs have had recalls for frame welds, clutches, power-steering pumps and 4xe batteries. Then change the gear oil, which owners skip most.
- Engine oil & filter: 3.6: 5 qt SAE 0W-20 meeting MS-6395 · 2.0T: 5 qt full-synthetic SAE 5W-30, API SN PLUS (Mopar MS-13340) · 4xe: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · 3.0 EcoDiesel: 9 qt 5W-40 synthetic (MS-12991) · 6.4 392: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Then per the oil-life monitor [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (The JL Pentastar takes a quart less, and a thinner grade, than the JK's: Quadratec specifies the Mopar MO-349 (68191349AA) cartridge, the 24 mm cap torqued to 18 ft-lb and the 13 mm drain plug to 20 ft-lb. The owner's-manual sheet warns that non-SN PLUS oil in the 2.0T 'can cause engine damage not covered by the vehicle warranty.')
- Engine air filter: Panel filter · Way of Life's index of the factory schedule lists it at 30,000 mi; sooner on dusty trails (Check the airbox seal after any off-road trip in fine dust.)
- Cabin air filter: Behind the glovebox · Every 20,000 mi in the factory schedule (Way of Life index) (Diesel trucks use a different part.)
- Spark plugs: 3.6: Mopar SP225755AA (2018–20) · 2.0T: Mopar 68292346AA · 392: Mopar SP149212AC · gaps per the 2020 manual sheet: 3.6 0.043 in, 2.0T 0.024–0.025 in · 3.6 at 100,000 mi; 2.0T every 30,000 mi (Way of Life index of the factory schedule) (The 2.0T's 30,000-mile plug interval is easy to miss on a used truck, so ask for receipts.)
- Coolant (engine, intercooler, eTorque/battery loops): Mopar 10-year/150,000-mile OAT (MS.90032) · 3.6 engine: 11.2 qt (10.6 L), plus 1.9 qt motor-generator and 2.5 qt battery loops on eTorque trucks · 2.0T engine: 10.3 qt (9.7 L), plus a 3.2–3.5 qt intercooler loop · 3.0 EcoDiesel: 12 qt (11.4 L) · Flush at 10 years or 150,000 mi (factory schedule per Way of Life) (The 2.0T and eTorque trucks have more than one cooling loop, and the owner's-manual sheet lists separate capacities for the intercooler, the motor-generator unit and the battery. Bleed each one correctly.)
- 8-speed automatic (850RE / ZF 8HP): Mopar ZF 8&9 Speed ATF · about 9 L total (8HP50 figure on the owner's-manual sheet) · KBB's schedule lists transmission fluids at 100,000 mi (This is not ATF+4. The level is set hot at the fill plug, so it's a shop job for most owners. Mopar also sells a JL transmission filter.)
- 6-speed manual: Mopar ATF+4 · 2.25 L · Every 30,000 mi under severe use (factory schedule per Way of Life) (Before you buy a manual truck, check that the clutch recall has been done.)
- Transfer case (Command-Trac / Rock-Trac / Selec-Trac): Mopar ATF+4 · ≈1.6 L part-time cases, ≈1.76 L full-time Selec-Trac · Inspect at 30,000 mi; replace at 60,000 mi under severe use or 150,000 mi normally (Way of Life index) (If you use low range on the trail, treat the severe-service interval as normal.)
- Front axle: GL-5 75W-85 (later manuals; the 2018 manual listed 80W-90) · M186/Dana 30: 0.86 L · M210/Dana 44: 1.03 L · Every 40,000 mi under severe use (Way of Life index); after any deep water crossing (JL front axles take very little oil, so a slightly low level matters.)
- Rear axle: M220/Dana 44: GL-5 75W-85, 1.45 L (1.36 L with Trac-Lok) · M200/'Dana 35': 1.15 L of synthetic 75W-140 per the 2020 owner's-manual sheet · Trac-Lok axles need 70 ml (2.37 oz) of Mopar limited-slip additive · Every 40,000 mi under severe use (Way of Life index) (Check which rear axle you have before buying oil (see the axle FAQ). Synthetic 75W-140 is the usual towing upgrade.)
- Power steering fluid: Mopar electric steering pump fluid (2020 owner's-manual sheet) · Check the level at every oil change (JLWranglerForums members warn against topping up with ATF+4, even though some charts list it. Check for the 2021–2025 power-steering pump recall (26V-363).)
- Brake & clutch fluid: Mopar DOT 3 (DOT 4 acceptable) · Flush on purchase, then every 2–3 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Manual trucks share the fluid type in the clutch master cylinder.)
- Driveline & front-end inspection: CV and U-joints, tie-rod ends, front suspension · Every 20,000 mi (factory schedule per Way of Life) (Lug nuts are 130 ft-lb (22 mm socket). Re-torque the track bar and steering hardware after any lift.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: On a Rubicon, 35s. Driving Line ran 35x12.50R17s on a stock-height JL Unlimited Rubicon with bump-stop spacers and the factory flares. They cleared on level ground but hit the inner fenders when flexed. Performance Plus Tire says Jeep ships the Rubicon 392 on LT315/70R17s, which are nearly 35s (check early 392s: the 35s were also part of the optional Xtreme Recon package). Performance Plus Tire says a Rubicon 4xe has about 2.1 inches less clearance than the gas Rubicon, so it needs bump-stop extensions for 35s. On a Sport or Sahara, stay with 33s and a wheel change, or lift 2–2.5 inches for 35s.

Q: Which engine should I buy?
A: 3.6 if you want a manual or the simplest drivetrain; 2.0T for torque and economy; EcoDiesel (2020–23) for towing range; 4xe for silent electric trail driving and short commutes on battery; 392 for 470 hp. Each brings its own recalls, so check them before you choose.

Q: How much can it tow?
A: 3,500 lb for most four-doors. From 2024, Hagerty says the full-float Dana 44 HD rear axle raises that to 5,000 lb on non-4xe trucks with the eight-speed automatic.

Q: What's the payload?
A: Quadratec lists 1,190 lb for a 2020 Sport four-door, 880 lb for a Sahara, 892 lb for a Rubicon and 1,351 lb for the 2021 Rubicon 392. The door sticker on your truck has the real figure.

Q: Is the 4xe safe to buy after the fire recalls?
A: Yes, once the recall work is done. The October 2024 recall covered 154,032 Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe models, with a software update and, where needed, a battery replacement. Owners were told to park outside and stop charging until it was fixed. Confirm completion on NHTSA, and test that the truck charges.

Q: How far does the 4xe go on electricity?
A: The EPA rates it at 21 miles and 49 MPGe on its 17 kWh battery. Hagerty says the 2024 update recalibrated E-Save mode to recover energy about 50 percent more effectively.

Q: Is the Rubicon 392 being discontinued?
A: Not any more. Jeep announced final editions for 2024 and 2025, then in August 2025 CEO Bob Broderdorf said, 'We will extend the availability of the 392 on Wrangler,' and announced a V8 Gladiator too.

Q: What oil does each engine take?
A: 3.6: 5 quarts of 0W-20 (MS-6395). 2.0T: 5 quarts of full-synthetic 5W-30, API SN PLUS (MS-13340). 3.0 EcoDiesel: 9 quarts of 5W-40 synthetic (MS-12991). For the 4xe and the 392, use the owner's manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL].

Q: How did the JL Unlimited do in crash tests?
A: Badly in one test. In the IIHS small-overlap test, a 2020 Unlimited's front axle tucked under the structure and the truck tipped onto its side. A 2022 retest ended the same way, so it was rated Marginal both times. Side-curtain airbags arrived with the 2024 refresh.

Q: Does the JL Unlimited get death wobble?
A: It can, like any solid-axle Jeep. Early trucks got a free stronger damper in 2019. The cure is a tight front end: track bar, tie-rod ends, ball joints, bushings and bearings, followed by an alignment.

Q: What do I need to know about the power-steering recall?
A: Recall 26V-363 (June 2026) covers about 1,077,000 2021–2025 Wranglers and Gladiators. A high-resistance connection at the electro-hydraulic pump can overheat and start a fire even when parked, and owners were told to park outside until dealers can inspect and repair it free.

Q: Which years are the best to buy?
A: No year is the consensus pick, so we don't flag one. The one to be wary of is 2018: SlashGear counted 11 recalls and more than 1,000 complaints, mostly about highway wander, and NHTSA's list includes track-bar bracket welds (18V-675, 2018–19), the steering shaft (18V-343) and rear frame-rail corrosion (18V-231). SlashGear calls 2020-on trucks the more enticing buy for their engine choices, but each brings its own recalls: EcoDiesel fuel pumps (22V-767, 23V-263), 4xe high-voltage batteries (23V-787, 25V-741) and, on 2021–25 trucks, the power-steering pump wiring (26V-363). Buy the truck whose recall list you can see closed.

- fueleconomy.gov — 2022 Jeep Wrangler 4dr 4xe: https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/noframes/44932.shtml

## Jeep Gladiator JT (2020–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/gladiator-jt/
Codes: JT, Rubicon, Mojave

Verdict: A JL Unlimited with 19.4 inches more wheelbase and a five-foot steel bed: the first Jeep pickup since the Comanche, and the only one whose roof, doors and windshield still come off. It tows and hauls like a midsize truck and crawls nearly like a Wrangler. Check the recall list before you check the paint.

Jeep went 27 years without a pickup. The Comanche left Toledo in June 1992, Chrysler handed trucks to Dodge, and the closest thing to a Jeep pickup was AEV's licensed Brute conversion. The Gladiator, revealed at the Los Angeles Auto Show on November 28, 2018 and sold as a 2020 model from spring 2019, ended that. It is a JL Unlimited from the B-pillar forward, on a new frame 31 inches longer than the four-door Wrangler's, with a five-foot steel bed behind. Doors, roof and windshield still come off. No other pickup offers that.

### A WRANGLER WITH A BED
Jeep had been teasing this truck for years. A Scrambler pickup on a stretched Wrangler was shown to dealers in 2003, and a 2005 Gladiator concept with a VM diesel and a manual gearbox previewed the JK. The production JT took its name from the 1962–88 full-size Gladiator and rides on a 137.3-inch wheelbase, 19.4 inches longer than the four-door Wrangler's. The bed has four steel cross-members, an aluminum damped tailgate, an optional 400 W outlet and a full-size spare slung underneath. The grille slots were opened up for towing.
Under it, Jeep fitted third-generation Dana 44 axles front and rear and a five-link coil rear suspension with two upper and two lower forged control arms and a track bar. Launch coverage called that suspension exclusive to the Gladiator. Power came from the 285 hp 3.6 Pentastar V6 with Aisin's six-speed manual or the eight-speed automatic. The Max Tow package on the Sport rated the truck at 7,650 lb, with 4.10 gears and a wider axle track.

### RUBICON, MOJAVE AND A DIESEL
The Rubicon has the hardware Wrangler people expect: the Rock-Trac transfer case with a 4:1 low range, Tru-Lok lockers at both ends, 4.10 gears, an electronic front sway-bar disconnect and 33-inch tires. The crawl ratio is 84.2:1 with the manual. On 4,190 Rubicon Launch Editions, Jeep's nod to Toledo's 419 area code, were offered for preorder on a single day, April 4, 2019. The Mojave followed in 2020 as Jeep's first 'Desert Rated' model. It gets 2.5-inch FOX internal-bypass shocks with external reservoirs, hydraulic front jounce bumpers and a rear locker that works at speed in 4-High. It is built for whoops, not ledges.
For 2021 the 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 arrived, with 260 hp, 442 lb-ft from 1,400 rpm and the eight-speed automatic only. Motor1 measured it at about 300 lb heavier than the gas truck, rated to tow 6,500 lb, and EPA-rated at 22/28/24 mpg against 17/22/19 for the automatic Pentastar. It lasted three model years. Jeep closed the chapter with 1,000 Rubicon FarOut editions for 2023, and the diesel was dropped after that.

### THE 2024 REFRESH AND WHAT CAME AFTER
The 2024 update brought a seven-slot grille with narrower slots that Jeep says cools better, an antenna hidden in the windshield, a standard 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen, and standard first- and second-row curtain airbags with structural changes for side impacts. Mojave X and Rubicon X trims added steel bumpers, a full-time transfer case and an off-road camera. The Willys got a standard rear locker. AEV's Upcountry packages added a 2-inch lift and 35-inch BFGoodrich KO2s, and a Rubicon-only Level II package fitted 37s.
The six-speed manual was dropped for 2025. A Gladiator 4xe plug-in hybrid was announced for 2025 and then cancelled in September 2025. For 2026 a Sahara trim joined the range, and every Gladiator now uses the Pentastar with the automatic. Mopar Insiders lists 2026 prices from $38,830 for a Sport to $59,995 for a Rubicon X or Mojave X, before destination. For the Cherokee XJ and Comanche generation, a Jeep pickup costing that much would have seemed absurd. Owners don't seem to mind.

### LIVING WITH THE LONG ONE
The extra wheelbase is the trade-off. Breakover is 18.4° on a stock Sport and 20.3° on a Rubicon, and the turning circle is 44.5–45 ft, so tight switchbacks can take a three-point turn, and the long belly between the axles is more exposed on ledges. In return the Gladiator is calmer on washboard, steadier with a trailer, and Jeep's first bed for a muddy cooler since the Comanche, and the spiritual heir of the CJ-8 Scrambler. Its natural rivals are other overland pickups such as the Ineos Quartermaster and the 70 Series pickups sold outside North America.

### Data plate
- Platform: JT (JL-based body-on-frame)
- Production: April 2019–present, Toledo, Ohio
- Model Years: 2020–present
- Wheelbase: 137.3 in (3,487 mm)
- Length: 218.0 in (5,539 mm)
- Bed: 60.3 in (81.3 in tailgate down), 35.5 cu ft
- Engine: 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft
- Diesel: 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 · 260 hp / 442 lb-ft (2021–23)
- Transmissions: D478 6-speed manual (to 2024) · 850RE 8-speed auto
- Transfer Cases: Command-Trac 2.72:1 · Rock-Trac 4:1 · Selec-Trac
- Axles: Dana 44 front and rear; Tru-Lok on Rubicon
- Curb Weight: 4,650–5,072 lb (2020 gas)

### Engineering
The JT is a body-on-frame truck: a ladder frame under an open steel and aluminum body, with a 137.3-inch wheelbase and a separate five-foot bed. Both axles are solid Dana 44s on coil springs, located by four links and a track bar at each end. Steering is electro-hydraulic, with a 13.3:1 ratio. Every Gladiator is 4WD: part-time Command-Trac (2.72:1), full-time Selec-Trac on non-Rubicon trims, and the Rubicon's Rock-Trac (4:1) in part-time or full-time form.
- Frame: Ladder frame, high-strength steel, 137.3 in wheelbase (31 in longer than the four-door Wrangler's frame, with a 19.4 in longer wheelbase.)
- Front Suspension: Solid Dana 44, five-link coil, track bar (Rubicon has an electronic sway-bar disconnect. Mojave adds FOX hydraulic jounce bumpers.)
- Rear Suspension: Solid Dana 44, coils, 2 upper and 2 lower forged arms, track bar (Gladiator-specific; coil springs, not leaves, despite the bed.)
- Engines: 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (2021–23) (285 hp / 260 lb-ft gas; 260 hp / 442 lb-ft diesel. No 2.0 turbo, 392 or 4xe.)
- Transmissions: Aisin D478 6-speed manual (to 2024) · 850RE 8-speed auto (Diesel was automatic-only. Manual dropped for 2025.)
- 4Wd And Lockers: Command-Trac 2.72:1 · Rock-Trac 4:1 · Selec-Trac (Rubicon: front and rear Tru-Lok. Mojave: rear locker. Willys: rear locker from 2024.)

### Versions
- 2020 · JT launch · 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · Sport, Sport S, Overland, Rubicon, plus 4,190 Rubicon Launch Editions. Max Tow 7,650 lb. Mojave added mid-year.
- 2021–2023 · JT · 3.6 V6 · 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 · 285 hp · 260 hp / 442 lb-ft · Diesel on all trims except Mojave; auto only; 6,500 lb tow. Willys, Willys Sport and 80th Anniversary editions; High Altitude returns for 2023.
- 2023 · JT FarOut · 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 · 260 hp / 442 lb-ft · 1,000 Rubicon FarOut editions mark the end of the diesel.
- 2024 · JT refresh · 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · Seven-slot grille, 12.3 in Uconnect 5, curtain airbags, Mojave X and Rubicon X, AEV packages.
- 2025–2026 · JT · 3.6 Pentastar V6 · 285 hp / 260 lb-ft · Automatic only. 4xe cancelled. Sahara trim for 2026.

### Year-by-year
- 2018: Revealed November 28 at the Los Angeles Auto Show: JL-based crew-cab pickup, 137.3 in wheelbase, five-foot steel bed, Dana 44 axles
- 2019: Production starts in Toledo in April. 4,190 Rubicon Launch Editions offered for preorder on April 4 (Jeep 4x4 Day)
- 2020: First model year: 3.6 Pentastar with 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto; Sport, Sport S, Overland, Rubicon; Max Tow 7,650 lb. Mojave ('Desert Rated') and High Altitude shown at Chicago. Rear driveshaft recall 19V-636 on early builds
- 2021: 3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp, 442 lb-ft, auto only) on all trims except Mojave; Willys and Willys Sport added; Texas Trail edition. The diesel later drew two high-pressure fuel-pump recalls (22V-767, 23V-263)
- 2022: Uconnect 4 7.0 standard on base trims; Alpine audio standard on Overland, Mojave and Rubicon
- 2023: Last EcoDiesel year: 1,000 Rubicon FarOut editions. High Altitude returns
- 2024: Refresh: seven-slot grille, windshield antenna, 12.3 in Uconnect 5, standard curtain airbags, Mojave X and Rubicon X, rear locker standard on Willys, AEV Upcountry and Level II packages
- 2025: Six-speed manual dropped. 4xe plug-in hybrid announced, then cancelled in September 2025
- 2026: Sahara trim added; all trucks 3.6 V6 with 8-speed auto. Steel-wheel recall 26V-456; power-steering pump wiring recall 26V-363 covers 2021–2025

### Capability
- Towing: Up to 7,650 lb (3,470 kg) (2020 Sport Max Tow, automatic; Rubicon auto 7,000 lb; manuals 4,000–4,500 lb; EcoDiesel 6,500 lb (Rubicon 6,000 lb))
- Payload: 1,105–1,700 lb (501–771 kg) (2020 spec sheet, by trim and gearbox; up to 1,720 lb quoted for 2026)
- Fuel tank: 22 US gal (83 L)
- Ground clearance: 10.0 in (253 mm) Sport · 11.1 in (283 mm) Rubicon · 11.6 in Mojave
- Approach / departure / breakover: 43.4° / 26° / 20.3° (Rubicon) (Sport 40.8° / 25° / 18.4°; Mojave 44.7° / 25.5° / 20.9°)
- Wading depth: 30 in (762 mm)
- Fuel economy: EPA 17 city / 22 hwy (3.6 auto) (16/23 manual; EcoDiesel 22/28 (Rubicon 21/27))
- Curb weight: 4,650–5,072 lb (2,109–2,301 kg) (2020 gas trucks; EcoDiesel about 300 lb heavier)
- Turning circle: 44.5–45.0 ft (13.6–13.7 m) (curb to curb)
- Bed: 60.3 in long (81.3 in tailgate down), 44.8 in between wheelhouses

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: 245/75R17 (Sport, Sport S), 255/70R18 (Overland), LT285/70R17C (Rubicon, Mojave)
- Bolt Pattern: 5x127 (5x5")
- Center Bore: 71.5 mm
- Lug Thread: M14x1.5
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 33 in (285/70R17) on Sport; 35x11.50R17 on Rubicon/Mojave (Drivingline says a stock Rubicon runs 35x11.50R17 on the factory 17x7.5 wheel. JeepGladiatorForum owners report 33s on stock Sports without rubbing; opinions differ on 35s, which may touch the flares at full flex.)
- Biggest tire, 1 in front spacer + bump stops lift: 37 in (Rubicon) (Drivingline's minimum for 37s on a Rubicon; expect some rubbing off-road. Wheel backspacing is critical, and 4.88 or 5.13 gears are recommended.)
- Biggest tire, 2 in (AEV Upcountry, 2024+) lift: 35 in BFGoodrich KO2 (AEV package offered with the 2024 refresh on Sport, Willys, Mojave and Rubicon. AEV's Rubicon-only Level II package uses 37s.)

### Buying checks
- Run the VIN for recalls first: Gladiators have had recalls for rear driveshafts (19V-636), manual clutches (20V-124, 21V-028, 23V-116 and 24V-572), EcoDiesel fuel pumps (22V-767, 23V-263), instrument clusters (24V-652) and, in June 2026, power-steering pump wiring that can start a fire with the truck parked (26V-363). Confirm each one is done.
- Manual trucks: ask about the clutch: The clutch pressure plate can overheat and fracture. FCA first issued software, then replaced clutch assemblies under 23V-116, and some 2021 trucks needed a second software fix under 24V-572. Ask for dealer paperwork, not a shrug.
- Drive it at 50–65 mph over a bump: Gladiators can shimmy or wobble after a highway expansion joint, as JLs can. Owners on JeepGladiatorForum report dealers replacing the steering damper or the steering box. Any wobble means the front end needs inspecting before you hand over money.
- Diesel? Check the fuel pump history: EcoDiesels were recalled twice for high-pressure fuel pumps that can fail and stall the engine. Look for the recall paperwork, ask about fuel-filter changes and look at the oil level. Diesel trucks are also about 300 lb heavier, so payload is lower.
- Look under the bed and behind the bumpers: Check the frame, bed mounts and spare-tire carrier for damage from off-road use. Check the rock rails and skids for dents that hint at hard use, and the hitch area for signs of heavy towing.
- Know which axle and gearing you're buying: Sport and Overland trucks came with 3.73 gears and a narrower 62.9 in track. The Max Tow package, Rubicon and Mojave have 4.10 gears and wider track. Rubicons add front and rear lockers and the 4:1 transfer case. Check the window sticker or build sheet.
- Lifted trucks: inspect the steering and track-bar mounts: Big tires and lifts load the steering box, track bars and their mounts. Look for elongated holes, fresh paint on welds, and torque marks that have moved. Ask what was done to correct the track-bar geometry.
- Hardtop and doors: Make sure the Freedom panels, hardtop seals and removable doors come with the truck and fit without leaking. Water stains on the carpet usually mean worn seals or poorly fitted panels.

### Common repairs
#### Cure steering wobble: damper, track bar, steering box
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–3 hours to inspect and fit parts · cost Parts plus alignment; dealer work if under warranty
Symptoms: Front-end shimmy or full death wobble after a bump at highway speed, or a steering wheel that shakes side to side. JeepGladiatorForum owners report dealers finding a weak damper or play in the steering box.
Fix: Inspect before you buy parts. With the truck on its wheels and the engine running, have a helper rock the steering wheel while you watch both ends of the front track bar, the tie-rod and drag-link ends, the pitman arm and the steering box mounting. Check ball joints and wheel bearings with the front end raised. Replace what's worn, torque the suspension at ride height, then get an alignment. A new damper helps a weak original, but on its own it only hides wobble. On lifted trucks, an adjustable track bar re-centers the axle.
Tools: Helper · torque wrench · pry bar · sockets · jack and stands · alignment afterward

#### Replace a leaking Pentastar oil filter housing / cooler
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 4–6 hours · cost Housing plus gaskets, oil and coolant
Symptoms: Oil, and sometimes coolant, pooling in the engine valley under the intake and running down the back of the block. The 3.6 Pentastar shares this housing with the JK and JL.
Fix: Remove the engine cover and air intake, then the upper intake manifold and lower intake runners to reach the valley. Disconnect the sensors on the housing, unbolt it, clean the valley thoroughly and fit the new housing with new seals. Refit the intake with new gaskets, refill oil and coolant, bleed the cooling system and check for leaks. Don't over-tighten the plastic filter cap.
Tools: Metric and Torx sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose pliers · shop towels to plug intake ports

#### Power steering: recall check, then hoses and reservoir
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2 hours DIY; recall work at the dealer · cost Free under recall 26V-363 where it applies
Symptoms: Loss of power assist, a 'Service Power Steering' warning, fluid weeping from the hoses or reservoir, or a burning smell. NHTSA's June 2026 recall 26V-363 covers 2021–2025 Wranglers and Gladiators whose electro-hydraulic pump wiring can overheat and start a fire, even when parked.
Fix: Check the VIN on NHTSA's lookup first. If 26V-363 applies, the dealer does the repair; until then, park outside. Out of recall, find leaks with the engine cold: clean the area, run the engine and turn lock to lock, then look at the hose crimps and reservoir. To replace a hose, drain the reservoir, swap the hose with new O-rings, refill with Mopar power-steering fluid (MS-11655 per the forum's Mopar fluid list) and bleed by turning lock to lock.
Tools: Line wrenches · drain pan · sockets · the specified power steering fluid

#### EcoDiesel: fuel-pump recalls and fuel-filter service
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour for the filter · cost Recall work free; a fuel filter for routine service
Symptoms: Stalling, hard starting or a diesel smell on a 2021–2023 EcoDiesel. NHTSA recalls 22V-767 and 23V-263 cover high-pressure fuel pumps that may fail and stall the engine.
Fix: Confirm both recalls are closed. Then treat the fuel filter as a wear item, because the high-pressure pump is sensitive to water and dirt. Relieve fuel pressure, replace the filter element and seals, prime the system as the service manual describes, and check for leaks. Drain water from the separator if the warning light comes on.
Tools: Filter wrench · drain pan · rags · service manual for priming

#### Manual trucks: clutch recall status, then clutch replacement
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time ≈ A day · cost Free under recall where open; otherwise a clutch kit and a long day
Symptoms: A burning smell after slow off-road work or towing, slipping, or a 'clutch overheating' message. NHTSA recalls 20V-124, 21V-028 and 23V-116 cover pressure plates that can overheat and fracture on 2020–2023 manual Gladiators.
Fix: Check the recalls first; the dealer remedy is a new clutch assembly and software. For a worn clutch on a truck that's already been remedied, support the truck, drop the front and rear driveshafts and the transfer case, unbolt the starter and bellhousing, and lower the transmission. Fit the new clutch and flywheel to the manufacturer's specifications, refit everything, bleed the hydraulics and follow the service manual for any clutch or software relearn.
Tools: Transmission jack · clutch alignment tool · torque wrench · jack stands · service manual

#### Driveshafts: recall check and U-joint service
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours · cost Recall replacement free; U-joints or a CV shaft otherwise
Symptoms: Vibration under acceleration, a clunk on take-off, or a squeak from the driveshafts. Recall 19V-636 covered 2020 Gladiators built between December 15, 2018 and June 25, 2019 whose rear driveshaft monoblock joint may have been assembled without grease. Wikipedia counts about 3,427 trucks.
Fix: Confirm 19V-636 on early trucks. Then grab each driveshaft and twist: any clunk or play at the U-joints means replacement. Mark the shaft's position, unbolt it, press out the old joint and press in the new one with new clips. On lifted trucks, steeper angles may call for a CV-style shaft.
Tools: U-joint press or vise · snap-ring pliers · paint marker · sockets · torque wrench

#### Re-spring the rear for a real load
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours for rear coils · cost A pair of coils, or a full lift kit
Symptoms: The rear sags or bottoms out once a camper shell, bed rack, rooftop tent or trailer is added. Payload is as low as 1,105 lb on a 2020 Sport automatic with 3.73 gears, per Stellantis's specification sheet.
Fix: Weigh the loaded truck at a scale first. Then fit coils rated for the load: support the frame, unbolt the shocks, sway-bar links and brake-line brackets, lower the axle carefully, swap the coils and isolators, and refit at ride height before torquing the bushings. Check the rear track bar and driveshaft angle afterwards, and re-aim the headlights.
Tools: Floor jack and stands · sockets · torque wrench · access to a vehicle scale

### Baseline service
Assume a used Gladiator has had oil changes and nothing else. Run the VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup first, then do the gear oils, transfer case and brake fluid, which owners most often skip. Fluid types below come from Mopar's specifications as compiled on JeepGladiatorForum and a 2021 owner's-manual excerpt posted there; engine capacities come from Stellantis's 2020 specification sheet. The EcoDiesel and Pentastar use different oils and filters.
- Engine oil & filter: 3.6: SAE 0W-20 full synthetic meeting MS-6395 · ≈5.7 qt (5.4 L) per the 2020 spec sheet · 3.0 EcoDiesel: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · Baseline now; then per the oil-life monitor (The Pentastar uses a cartridge filter in a plastic housing; don't over-tighten the cap. Check the valley for housing leaks while you're there.)
- Engine air filter: Panel filter; Mopar 68257030AA on the 3.6 · Baseline now; more often in dust (Desert and trail dust load it quickly. The diesel uses a different element.)
- Cabin air filter: Behind the glovebox; Mopar 68535621AA (gas) · Baseline now (Diesel trucks use a different part.)
- Spark plugs (3.6): Mopar SP225755AA · Per the maintenance schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Ask for receipts; a used truck may be near its first plug change.)
- Coolant: Mopar OAT (MS.90032 concentrate / MS-12106 pre-diluted) · 3.6: 10 qt (10.1 L) per the 2020 spec sheet · Inspect now; flush per schedule (Don't mix in older HOAT or green coolant. Pressure-test if the level drops.)
- 8-speed automatic (850RE / 8HP): Mopar 68218925AB, a ZF-approved ATF (ZF LifeguardFluid 8/9 equivalent) · filter 68417054AB · Baseline if history is unknown; shop job (Not ATF+4. The level is set hot at the fill plug, so most owners leave it to a shop.)
- 6-speed manual (D478): Mopar ATF+4 (MS-9602) · Baseline now (Confirm the clutch recalls are done before you spend money here.)
- Transfer case: Mopar ATF+4 · about 2 qt (member report, [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]) · Baseline now; sooner if you use low range a lot (Same fluid for Command-Trac, Rock-Trac and Selec-Trac.)
- Front axle (Dana 44): Mopar 75W-85 GL-5 synthetic (MS-A0450, 68378949AB) · Baseline now; after any deep water crossing (Both axles together take about 4 qt by one member's count; fill to the bottom of the fill hole.)
- Rear axle (Dana 44): 75W-85 GL-5 normally · 75W-140 synthetic (MS-8985, 68218657AB) for towing or heavy loads · friction modifier with Trac-Lok · Baseline now (Trucks that tow or carry heavy loads should run the 75W-140 that Mopar specifies for that use.)
- Power steering fluid: Mopar power steering fluid MS-11655 (68088485AB) · Check the level now (Check recall 26V-363 (2021–2025) before anything else.)
- Brake & clutch fluid: DOT 3 (DOT 4 acceptable), Mopar 04318080AD · Flush now; then every 2–3 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Manual trucks share the fluid with the clutch hydraulics.)
- Driveshafts & front end: U-joints, CV joints, tie-rod ends, track bars, ball joints · Inspect now and after every hard trail day (Re-torque track-bar and steering hardware after any lift.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: On a Rubicon or Mojave, a 35x11.50R17 on the stock 17x7.5 wheel, per Drivingline's Rubicon fitment guide, which also says 37s need at least a 1-inch front spacer and bump stops and still rub off-road. On Sport and Sport S trucks, JeepGladiatorForum owners run 33s (285/70R17) without rubbing. Some say 35s work on stock suspension with little rubbing; others say they hit the flares at full flex.

Q: Gas or EcoDiesel?
A: The 2021–23 EcoDiesel makes 442 lb-ft from 1,400 rpm and rates 22/28/24 mpg against 17/22/19 for the automatic Pentastar. But it's about 300 lb heavier, tows less (6,500 lb, or 6,000 lb on a Rubicon), was automatic-only, and has had two fuel-pump recalls. Pick the diesel for range and low-speed torque; pick the gas truck for maximum towing and simpler ownership.

Q: How much can it tow and carry?
A: Stellantis's 2020 specification sheet rates a Sport automatic with 4.10 gears (the Max Tow package) at 7,650 lb and a Rubicon automatic at 7,000 lb. Manual trucks are rated 4,000–4,500 lb. Payload runs from 1,105 lb to 1,700 lb depending on trim and gearbox. For 2026, Mopar Insiders quotes up to 7,700 lb towing and 1,720 lb payload.

Q: Rubicon or Mojave?
A: The Rubicon is for rocks: 4:1 low range, front and rear lockers and a disconnecting front sway bar. The Mojave is for speed on rough dirt: 2.5-inch FOX internal-bypass shocks with reservoirs, hydraulic front jounce bumpers, 2.72:1 low range and a rear locker that works at speed in 4-High.

Q: Has the Gladiator had frame or track-bar recalls?
A: As of October 2026, NHTSA's recall list for 2020–2026 Gladiators shows no frame-weld or track-bar recall. The well-known track-bar bracket weld recall (18V-675) covered 2018–2019 Wranglers, before the JT existed. Gladiator recalls have instead covered driveshafts, clutches, fuel pumps, the instrument cluster, cameras, seat belts, steel wheels (2026) and power-steering pump wiring.

Q: Does it get death wobble?
A: Some do. JeepGladiatorForum owners report wobble on new trucks, with dealers replacing the steering damper or the steering box. Treat it as a front-end inspection, not a damper purchase: check the track bar, tie-rod and drag-link ends, ball joints and the steering box mount.

Q: What changed for 2024?
A: A seven-slot grille, an antenna in the windshield, a standard 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen, standard first- and second-row curtain airbags with side-impact structural changes, new Mojave X and Rubicon X trims, a standard rear locker on the Willys, and AEV upfit packages with 35- or 37-inch tires. The diesel was gone.

Q: What fuel economy should I expect?
A: EPA ratings for the 3.6 are 17/22/19 mpg with the automatic and 16/23/19 with the manual. The EcoDiesel is rated 22/28/24, or 21/27/24 as a Rubicon. Big tires, lifts and racks take more.

Q: What fluids does it take?
A: Per Mopar's specs as compiled on JeepGladiatorForum: 3.6 oil 0W-20 (MS-6395), OAT coolant, ZF-approved ATF in the eight-speed, ATF+4 in the manual and transfer case, 75W-85 GL-5 in both axles (75W-140 in the rear for towing), friction modifier with Trac-Lok, MS-11655 power steering fluid and DOT 3 brake fluid. See 'After you buy it'.

Q: Is the long wheelbase a problem off-road?
A: Sometimes. Breakover is 18.4° on a Sport and 20.3° on a Rubicon, and the turning circle is 44.5–45 ft, so tight trails take more shuffling than in a Wrangler. Rock sliders matter more on a Gladiator than on a Wrangler.

Q: Manual or automatic?
A: The six-speed manual is rare and was dropped for 2025. It's also the gearbox with the clutch recalls and the lower tow ratings. The eight-speed automatic tows more and was the only choice with the diesel.

Q: Which years are the best to buy?
A: There's no consensus year yet, so we don't flag one. The recall history is the better guide. Early 2020 trucks had the rear driveshaft recall (19V-636). Manual trucks from 2020 to 2023 are covered by the clutch pressure-plate recalls (20V-124, 21V-028, 23V-116), and some 2021s needed a second fix (24V-572). Diesels have fuel-pump recalls 22V-767 (2021–22) and 23V-263 (2021–23), and 2021–25 trucks are in the power-steering pump wiring recall (26V-363). The 2024 refresh added curtain airbags and the big screen, if those matter to you. Buy whichever year you can prove every recall on.
