## Lexus LX 570 (2008–2021)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx570/
Codes: J200, URJ200, 3UR-FE

Verdict: Nearly three tons of hydraulically levitated V8 that Car and Driver called the most desirable SUV on the planet. The punchline is that a used one often costs less than the Land Cruiser it's built on.

The LX 570 is the 200 Series Land Cruiser in Lexus clothes, and for 13 US model years it was the most capable thing in a Lexus showroom. It sits on a new ladder frame with double-wishbone front suspension and a multi-link solid rear axle, and it uses the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE V8 with 383 hp and 403 lb-ft. Full-time four-wheel drive runs through a Torsen center differential that can be locked, and Crawl Control does the throttle and brake work for you on steep, slow terrain. Then Lexus added four-corner hydraulic Active Height Control with Adaptive Variable Suspension. That system is the main difference between the LX and the Land Cruiser, and it divides owners.

### FIRST, FOR ONCE
Development of both the 200 Series and the LX began in 2002, and the design was approved in 2004. Lexus showed the 2008 LX 570 at the New York International Auto Show on April 4, 2007. It was the first LX to be revealed before its Land Cruiser twin. The frame was all new. A third of its mass is high-tensile steel, all three crossmembers are hydroformed, and the tow hitch is built into the frame, as on the Tundra. Lexus said the platform covered 240,000 test kilometers in subtropical forest, the Australian Outback and American deserts.
The LX was 102 mm longer than the LX 470 on the same 112.2-in wheelbase, and it lost the old truck's plastic lower cladding. The front suspension gave 9 in of wheel travel. ClubLexus quotes Car and Driver calling it "the most desirable SUV on the planet" and cites a 0–60 mph time of 6.7 seconds for a truck weighing about three tons.

### THE V8 AND THE ROBOTS
The 3UR-FE is a 32-valve, chain-driven quad-cam V8 with dual VVT-i, shared with the Tundra and Sequoia. It drove a six-speed AB60F automatic, and from the 2016 refresh an eight-speed AE80F. Towing was rated up to 8,500 lb at launch; the 2016-on owner's manual lists 7,000 lb with trailer brakes. The electronics did as much as the hardware. Crawl Control works like an off-road cruise control in both directions. The truck also has multi-terrain ABS, Hill-start Assist and A-TRAC traction control, and from 2013 Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist, which brakes the inside rear wheel in tight low-range turns.
The AHC has six settings and can raise the truck about 3 in or lower it about 2 in from normal ride height, using a knob on the console. The AVS dampers are diagonally cross-linked through a hydraulic system, an idea Wikipedia compares to the 4Runner's X-REAS. One thing the LX doesn't have is the Land Cruiser's KDSS. An IH8MUD member fitting 35s points out that this actually makes big tires easier to fit on the Lexus.

### THREE FACES
The LX 570 had three distinct looks. The 2008–2011 trucks are the plain-faced originals, with a 2011 bumper update that hinted at the spindle grille. There was no 2012 model year in the US. For 2013 came the first proper spindle grille, plus Multi-Terrain Select, Turn Assist and a five-speed Crawl Control. Lexus unveiled the 2016 refresh at Pebble Beach in August 2015, and it kept only the doors and roof. It brought an all-new interior and the eight-speed, and it was the first LX sold officially in Japan.
The last years brought niche variants. A two-row, five-seat version arrived for 2018. There were 500-unit Inspiration Series runs in 2019 and 2021, and a Sport package for 2020. US sales peaked at 7,915 in 2008, the launch year, and ran between about 3,100 and 6,000 a year after that, ending at 3,563 in 2021.

### HOW IT ENDED
Production ended in October 2021, when the 300 Series-based LX 600 replaced the V8 with a twin-turbo V6. Toyota pulled the 200 Series Land Cruiser from North America after 2021 as well, so the LX 570 and its twin bowed out together as the last of the V8s.
On the used market the LX 570 is something of a bargain. DrivingLine noted that used LX 570s typically sold for less than comparable Land Cruisers, even though they were pricier and better equipped new. The discount is mostly fear of AHC repair bills. After a decade of ownership, one long-time IH8MUD poster concluded that the system had turned out to be "brilliantly engineered and built," without the catastrophic tales of woe owners had expected.

### Data plate
- Chassis: J200 (URJ201)
- Years: 2008–2021 MY (no US 2012)
- Engine: 3UR-FE 5.7 L V8, timing chain
- Output: 383 hp / 403 lb-ft (US)
- Transmission: AB60F 6-spd → AE80F 8-spd (2016+)
- 4Wd: Full-time, Torsen center diff, lockable, low range
- Suspension: Double-wishbone front, multi-link solid rear, AHC/AVS
- Ahc Range: ≈ +3 in / −2 in from normal
- Wheelbase: 112.2 in (2,850 mm)
- Weight: 2,685–2,750 kg (≈ 5,920–6,060 lb)
- Towing: 8,500 lb (launch) · 7,000 lb (2016+ owner's manual)
- Stock Tire: 285/50R20 (21-in optional from 2016)

### Engineering
The LX 570 rides on the new J200 ladder frame, with double-wishbone independent front suspension, a multi-link solid rear axle and a frame-integrated hitch. Full-time 4WD runs through a two-speed transfer case and a Torsen center differential that can be locked, backed by A-TRAC. US trucks have no factory axle lockers. Instead of the Land Cruiser's coil springs and KDSS, every LX uses four-corner hydraulic AHC with AVS adaptive damping and automatic load leveling.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, J200 (A third high-tensile steel, hydroformed crossmembers, integrated hitch. Same frame as the 200 Series Land Cruiser.)
- Engine: 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 (32-valve DOHC with a timing chain and dual VVT-i. 383 hp / 403 lb-ft in US trim. EPA-rated on premium fuel.)
- Transmission: AB60F 6-spd → AE80F 8-spd (Eight-speed from the 2016 model year.)
- 4Wd: Full-time, Torsen center (Lockable center diff and low range. A-TRAC brake traction control. No factory axle lockers in the US.)
- Suspension: AHC + AVS (Six height settings: about +3 in / −2 in. Double-wishbone front with 9 in of travel. No KDSS.)
- Terrain Tech: Crawl Control (Plus multi-terrain ABS, Hill-start Assist and, from 2013, Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist.)

### Versions
- 2008–2011 · URJ201 · 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 · 383 hp / 403 lb-ft · Launch. AB60F six-speed, 20-in wheels, Crawl Control. 2011 brought a bumper facelift and heated steering wheel. No 2012 MY in the US.
- 2013–2015 · URJ201 · 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 · 383 hp / 403 lb-ft · First spindle-grille facelift. Multi-Terrain Select, Turn Assist and five-speed Crawl Control.
- 2016–2017 · URJ201 · 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 · 383 hp / 403 lb-ft · Major refresh (only the doors and roof carried over). AE80F eight-speed, new interior, available 21-in wheels.
- 2018–2021 · URJ201 · 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 · 383 hp / 403 lb-ft · Two-row option from 2018. Inspiration Series (500 units) in 2019 and 2021. Sport package in 2020.
- 2015–2021 (export) · VDJ201 · LX 450d · 1VD-FTV 4.5 turbodiesel V8 · 268 hp / 479 lb-ft · Not sold in North America.

### Year-by-year
- 2008: Debuts in April 2007 at the New York show. 3UR-FE 5.7 V8 (383 hp), AB60F six-speed, Torsen center diff, double-wishbone front, six-height AHC, Crawl Control and a frame-integrated hitch rated to 8,500 lb.
- 2008–2010: Most of the radiator-crack reports come from these years (the radiator part number changed after 2010), and owners say 2008s had water-pump issues. [avoid]
- 2011: Mild facelift with a new front bumper. First year of the heated steering wheel.
- 2012: No US model year. 2011 production ran late and 2013 started early.
- 2013: First spindle-grille facelift. Five-speed Crawl Control, Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist.
- 2016: Major refresh (only the doors and roof carry over). AE80F eight-speed, all-new interior, all-speed radar cruise and optional 21-in wheels.
- 2018: Two-row, five-seat version available.
- 2019: Inspiration Series: 500 trucks, all black.
- 2020: Sport package (three-row models only).
- 2021: Final year, with a second 500-unit Inspiration Series. Production ends in October 2021.

### Capability
- Towing: 8,500 lb (3,855 kg) at launch (frame-integrated hitch; the 2016-on owner's manual lists 7,000 lb (3,175 kg) with trailer brakes)
- Roof load: 154 lb (70 kg) (roof luggage carrier limit, owner's manual)
- Fuel tank: 24.5 US gal (93 L) (premium fuel)
- Ride height range: AHC: about +3 in / −2 in from normal
- Fuel economy: EPA 12 city / 18 hwy / 14 combined (2008) (13 / 18 / 15 for 2016; 12 / 16 / 14 for 2020)
- Wheelbase: 112.2 in (2,850 mm)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: 285/50R20 112V on 20x8.5 alloys, 275/50R21 113V XL on 21x8.5 alloys (2016+ option)
- Bolt Pattern: 5x150
- Lug Torque: 97 lb-ft (131 N·m)
- Biggest tire, Stock (AHC) lift: ≈33 in (The practical limit. Even 33s meant moving the front fender liner forward about 1 in.)
- Biggest tire, Stock AHC + 1 in wheel spacers lift: 35x12.50R20 (One IH8MUD build: liner moved about 1.75 in, sidestep return trimmed, body mount reshaped. The builder recommends an effective offset of +30 to +35 mm. It's easier than on a Land Cruiser because the LX has no KDSS bar.)

### Buying checks
- AHC leaks and behavior: Cycle the truck through Low, Normal and High and make sure it levels evenly. The IH8MUD AHC sticky includes a Toyota diagram of leak-prone junctions. Fluid at those points means you're about to learn a lot about hydraulics. A healthy system also lifts an extra inch or so in some low-range recovery situations, one owner reports.
- Radiator (2008–2010): Owners of early trucks report cracks in the top plastic tank, next to the molded platform. Look for a wet line or dried pink coolant along the top. Later radiators carry a different part number.
- Water pump: Forum members say 2008 trucks had water-pump problems that have since been fixed. Look for pink crust at the pump weep hole and ask whether it's been replaced. One high-mileage owner paid about $700.
- Valley coolant leak: Pink coolant dripping from the top of the transmission hump at the back of the engine usually means the valley leak: the heat-exchanger cover and union pipe under the intake. It's not hard to fix, but it takes a lot of labor.
- Driveshaft clunk: A 'thunk' when taking off or stopping often points to dry slip yokes and U-joints. Ask when the driveshafts were last greased. One owner paid about $780 for a propeller-shaft assembly to cure it.
- Starter: Several owners have had the starter solenoid fail with no warning and leave them stranded. On a high-mileage truck, proactive replacement is common.
- Records by VIN: The IH8MUD FAQ points out that the Toyota and Lexus owner sites show dealer service history once you enter the VIN, which is a good check before buying.
- HVAC recirculation door: IH8MUD members warn that the recirculation door hinge can be broken by a careless cabin-filter change. Check that the recirc control actually changes the airflow.

### Common repairs
#### Radiator replacement (cracked top tank)
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Parts plus labor. The FSM procedure is posted on IH8MUD. · cost Parts plus labor. Some owners have had Toyota cover it out of warranty.
Symptoms: A wet line or pink crust along the top plastic tank next to the molded platform, slow coolant loss and a sweet smell after a drive. It's most often reported on 2008–2010 trucks.
Fix: Drain the coolant and follow the factory removal and installation steps posted in the IH8MUD radiator-replacement thread linked from the Common Failures FAQ. Fit the current (later) part number, then refill with Toyota pink long-life coolant and bleed the system. Check the water pump while the front of the engine is open.
Tools: Basic metric sockets · drain pan · hose pliers · Toyota Super Long Life Coolant · new radiator (later part number)

#### Water pump replacement
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Most of a day · cost About $700 at a shop (owner report)
Symptoms: Pink crust or drips around the water pump weep hole at the front of the engine. It's commonly reported on 2008 trucks.
Fix: Drain the coolant and do the usual front-of-engine teardown to reach the pump. Unbolt the pump, clean the mating surface and fit the new pump with its gasket. Refill and bleed the system. Before you start, confirm the leak is really the pump and not the valley leak. One owner pulled the front of the engine apart only to find the pump dry and the coolant coming from the back of the engine.
Tools: Metric sockets · fan clutch wrench · drain pan · new pump and gasket · Toyota SLLC

#### Valley coolant leak (heat-exchanger cover)
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time A long weekend · cost FIPG sealant and two union-pipe O-rings, plus a lot of labor if a shop does it
Symptoms: Pink coolant dripping from the top of the transmission hump at the back of the engine, with the water pump area dry.
Fix: Remove the plastic intake runners and intake to expose the engine valley. Remove the aluminum heat-exchanger cover, clean both surfaces and reseal with grey FIPG. Replace the union pipe and both of its O-rings while you're in there. One IH8MUD member called it "a PHH job on FZJs on steroids": nothing technical, just a lot of hard-to-reach bolts.
Tools: Long extensions · swivel sockets · gasket scraper · grey FIPG · union pipe O-rings · new intake gaskets

#### Driveshaft service (grease and re-index)
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time An afternoon · cost A tube of MP grease
Symptoms: A clunk or 'thunk' when pulling away or stopping, driveline vibration and dry slip yokes.
Fix: With the wheels on the ground, chocked and the parking brake on, remove the transfer-case insulator (four 12 mm bolts). Paint-mark both flanges, then unbolt the rear shaft at the transfer case (captured bolts, 14 mm nuts) and at the diff. Clean the shaft, grease the U-joints and slip yoke until fresh grease purges, and reinstall on your marks with the fasteners torqued. Do the front shaft the same way. Remember that with both shafts off, only the parking brake is holding the truck.
Tools: 12 mm and 14 mm sockets · 14 mm wrench · extensions · torque wrench · pry bar · paint pen · grease gun with MP grease

#### Starter replacement
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time Parts plus labor · cost Parts plus labor (the replacement starter is noticeably smaller than the original)
Symptoms: A sudden no-crank, usually with no warning. The failure is typically in the solenoid, the high-current relay built onto the back of the starter.
Fix: Disconnect the battery, gain access to the starter, unplug and unbolt it, and fit the replacement. Some owners do it proactively at high mileage instead of waiting to get stranded.
Tools: Metric sockets · long extensions · battery terminal wrench · new or reman starter

#### Spark plugs
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time An afternoon · cost 8 plugs plus any intake hardware
Symptoms: Service interval due (one high-mileage owner did his at 120k miles), misfires or rough idle.
Fix: Follow the IH8MUD plug-change write-ups in the 200 Series FAQ. Clean around the coils before removal, swap one cylinder at a time, torque to spec and clear any codes.
Tools: Spark plug socket · extensions · torque wrench · compressed air · OEM-spec plugs

#### AHC leak inspection
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1 hour to inspect · cost Inspection is free. Leaking actuators, accumulators or lines are parts plus labor.
Symptoms: Wet hydraulic fluid at line junctions or actuators, uneven leveling, a sagging corner or a harsh ride.
Fix: Use the Toyota leak-point diagram in IH8MUD's LX570 AHC sticky. Look up under the running boards at each corner, at the accumulator globes and at the line junctions. Cycle through Low, Normal and High and watch each corner respond. Use Techstream or a similar scan tool to read AHC pressures and codes before replacing parts.
Tools: Flashlight · mirror · Techstream-capable scan tool · factory repair manual

### Baseline service
The 3UR-FE has a timing chain, so there's no belt to worry about. The LX 570's baseline is about fluids, the AHC and the known coolant weak spots: early radiators, the water pump and the valley leak. Before buying, enter the VIN on the Lexus owners site to see dealer service history, as the IH8MUD FAQ suggests. Capacities below come from the Lexus-hosted LX 570 owner's manual (OM60P32U), a 2016-or-later edition, so confirm them for earlier trucks.
- Engine oil & filter: SAE 0W-20 ILSAC GF-5 (5W-20 only as a stopgap) · 7.9 US qt (7.5 L) with filter, per the 2016-on owner's manual · cartridge filter element with O-rings · At purchase, then per the maintenance schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (A skid plate has to come off. The cartridge cap takes a 64 mm, 14-flat wrench, and the kit includes a plastic drain tube (IH8MUD).)
- Air filter: 3UR-FE element · Inspect every oil change
- Cabin filter: 200 Series element · At purchase (Set the HVAC recirculation door correctly before pulling the filter. IH8MUD members have broken the hinge by forcing it.)
- Spark plugs: Denso SK20HR11 iridium (Toyota 90919-01191) ×8 · gap 1.1 mm, do not adjust (owner's manual) · Owners report first changes around 120k–129k mi (The plugs sit deep, so you'll need several extensions and a swivel, especially for the passenger-side rear plug. Don't drop the coil-to-cover rubber seal (IH8MUD).)
- Coolant, radiator & water pump check: Toyota Super Long Life Coolant · 17.1 US qt (16.2 L) (owner's manual) · Inspect at purchase (On 2008–2010 trucks, check the top of the radiator next to the molded platform for cracks. Look for weeping at the water pump and pink drips at the back of the engine (the valley leak).)
- Automatic transmission fluid: AB60F (2008–2015) / AE80F (2016+) · Toyota Genuine ATF WS · 10.7 US qt (10.1 L) reference, per the 2016-on owner's manual · Drain-and-fill at purchase (Repeat the drain-and-fill rather than power-flushing a high-mileage transmission.)
- Transfer case & differentials: Transfer: Toyota Transfer Gear Oil LF, SAE 75W, 1.53 US qt (1.45 L). Diffs: Toyota Differential Gear Oil LT 75W-85 GL-5, front 2.01 US qt (1.90 L), rear 4.44 US qt (4.20 L) (2016-on owner's manual) · fill until level is 0–5 mm below the fill plug · Every 50k mi, or 30k if you tow or go off-road (IH8MUD) (An IH8MUD member who posted video how-tos recommends an early change on low-mile trucks, because break-in metal contaminates the first fill. The front service means dropping the skid plates.)
- AHC hydraulic system: Suspension fluid AHC (owner's manual) · inspect the leak-prone junctions shown in the Toyota diagram in IH8MUD's AHC sticky · At purchase, then yearly (Cycle through Low, Normal and High and watch each corner. Read AHC codes with Techstream before you buy parts.)
- Driveshafts & U-joints: MP grease, with flanges match-marked if you remove them · At purchase and every oil change (Dry slip yokes cause the classic 'thunk'. Overland Tailor's IH8MUD write-up covers removal and greasing.)
- Drive belt & idlers: 3UR-FE serpentine belt · Inspect at purchase
- Brake fluid & pads: SAE J1703 or FMVSS No. 116 DOT 3 (owner's manual) · Flush at purchase (IH8MUD's 200 Series brake thread lists part numbers and torque values. Torque specs differ between 2013 and 2016+ trucks.)
- PCV valve: URJ200/LX570 PCV · At purchase if there's no record
- Starter: Inspect the age and records of the original starter · Consider replacing proactively on high-mileage trucks (Several owners have had the starter solenoid fail with no warning (IH8MUD common-failures FAQ).)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: The stock size is 285/50R20. The practical limit is about 33 in, and even that meant moving the front fender liner forward about an inch on one IH8MUD member's LX. His 35x12.5R20 build needed the liner moved further, the sidestep return trimmed and the body mount reshaped, with spacers giving about +35 mm effective offset. The LX is easier to fit than a Land Cruiser because it doesn't have the KDSS bar.

Q: How much can an LX 570 tow?
A: Up to 8,500 lb at launch. The 2016-on owner's manual lists 7,000 lb (with trailer brakes) for the facelifted truck, so check the manual for your year. The hitch receiver is built into the frame.

Q: What fuel economy should I expect, and does it need premium?
A: Yes, the EPA lists premium fuel. The six-speed 2008 is rated 12 city, 18 highway and 14 combined. The eight-speed 2016 is rated 13 city, 18 highway and 15 combined.

Q: Does it have lockers?
A: The US LX 570 has a lockable Torsen center differential plus A-TRAC, Crawl Control and, from 2013, Multi-Terrain Select. It has no factory front or rear axle lockers. Owners who want them fit aftermarket units such as ARB Air Lockers.

Q: Is the AHC going to bankrupt me?
A: Probably not, if you buy a healthy one. One long-time IH8MUD poster wrote that after ten years in service the LX 570's AHC had turned out to be well engineered, without the expected horror stories. But leaks at line junctions and actuators are expensive, so inspect the system carefully before you buy.

Q: LX 570 or 200 Series Land Cruiser?
A: They share the same frame, V8, transmission and transfer case. The LX swaps coil springs and KDSS for AHC, adds more luxury equipment and 20-in wheels, and over time got its own styling, with unique front and rear ends from 2016. DrivingLine noted that used LX 570s were typically priced below comparable Land Cruisers.

Q: Which years should I buy?
A: There's no consensus best year, but there is one to be careful with: 2008–2010 trucks have the most radiator-crack reports (IH8MUD notes the part number changed after 2010), and owners say 2008s had water-pump issues. After that it's taste. 2013–2015 add Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist; 2016-on gets the eight-speed and a new interior. ClubLexus owners split on 2015 versus 2016: some find the facelift's tech and radar cruise worth it, others say the 2016 drives worse. There is no 2012 model year in the US.

Q: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
A: A chain. The 3UR-FE is a chain-driven DOHC V8, so there's no 90k belt service like the LX 470's.

Q: Is there a 2012 LX 570?
A: Not in the US. Production of the 2011 model ran late and the 2013 started early, so the 2012 model year was skipped.

Q: What does Crawl Control actually do?
A: It works like an off-road cruise control. It controls throttle and brakes to hold a slow, steady speed over obstacles, forward or in reverse. From 2013 you can choose from five speeds, and Turn Assist brakes the inside rear wheel to tighten low-range turns.

## Lexus LX 600 (2022–present)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx600/
Codes: J310, V35A-FTS

Verdict: The only 300 Series Land Cruiser America could buy, sold with 22-inch wheels and an apology for the missing V8. Brilliant chassis, so check the engine's paperwork.

When Toyota decided the 300 Series Land Cruiser wouldn't be sold in North America, the LX 600 became the only way to buy one here. Unveiled on October 13, 2021, it moved to the new GA-F ladder frame, lost 441 lb compared with the LX 570 and swapped the old 5.7-liter V8 for a 409-hp, 479 lb-ft 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6 and a 10-speed automatic. The trim is fancier than any Land Cruiser buyer asked for, but the low range, locking center diff and solid rear axle are pure Land Cruiser.

### THE LAND CRUISER AMERICA COULDN'T BUY
The LX has always been a Land Cruiser in a better suit, from the 80 Series-based LX 450 through the 200 Series-based LX 570. Lexus says the LX has been sold in more than 50 countries and regions, with over 500,000 sold by August 2021. Its 112-in wheelbase dates back to the first LX of 1995. When the 300 Series arrived without a US version, one launch report summed up the mood: 'Many were disappointed to learn that the 300-Series Toyota Land Cruiser wouldn't come to the U.S.'
The LX 600 filled that hole with five grades at launch: Standard, Premium, Luxury, F Sport and Ultra Luxury. The Ultra Luxury is a four-seat limousine with 48-degree reclining rear seats. The F Sport adds 22-inch forged wheels, a rear stabilizer and a Torsen limited-slip rear differential. None of the US grades got front or rear lockers. Those stayed in Japan, which got an LX 'Offroad' grade with all three differentials locking.

### WHAT THE NEW CHASSIS BROUGHT
Lexus describes the GA-F frame as 20 percent more rigid. The front uses high-mounted double wishbones, and the rear keeps a four-link axle with lateral control arms. Suspension travel is 100 mm of bound and 145 mm of rebound, and rear rebound alone grew by 20 mm. Active Height Control offers Low, Normal, Hi1 and Hi2 heights, and adaptive dampers use linear solenoid valves. At normal height, the approach, breakover and departure angles are 25°, 23° and 20°.
The off-road electronics got smarter too. Multi-Terrain Select has six modes, including a first-for-Lexus Auto setting that reads the terrain from sensor data. Crawl Control offers five speeds, and the Multi-Terrain Monitor adds four cameras and an underfloor view. Lexus rates it to climb 45 degrees and wade 700 mm (27.5 in). Not everyone wants the gadgets, though. Slee Off-Road's 'Marshmello' build was a Premium LX 600 custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension.

### THE ENGINE QUESTION
The V35A-FTS is where the LX 600 story gets complicated. In 2024, Toyota recalled 102,092 Tundras and LX 600s, 3,524 of them LXs built from July 30, 2021 to November 25, 2022, because machining debris could damage the main bearings. The remedy was a new engine. In November 2025, recall 25V-767 added another 9,895 US-market LXs built from February 26, 2022 to April 2, 2024. That count includes 10 trucks that had received affected service engines. At first Lexus told dealers the remedy was still being developed. NHTSA's record now says dealers inspect the No. 1 main bearing using inspection software and drive data and replace the engine if necessary, with owner letters mailed August 28, 2026.
The recall report notes that some later engines use improved manufacturing processes or an improved main bearing. On IH8MUD, owners argue about it constantly. Some see the recall as an open-ended engine warranty, while others are waiting for Toyota to name a root cause. Owners also report a clunk into first gear on rolling stops and laggy throttle tied to the pre-collision system. Neither is dangerous, but both are worth knowing about before you test-drive one.

### WHERE IT STANDS
The LX 600 has sold steadily for something this expensive, with 3,642 US sales in 2022, 6,959 in 2023, 6,830 in 2024 and 7,464 in 2025, when 2,883 of those were the new LX 700h hybrid. That hybrid makes 457 hp and 583 lb-ft. In October 2024, Lexus finally gave Americans the triple-locked LX it had kept in Japan: the LX 700h Overtrail, with front and rear lockers on top of the center lock.
For 2027, the gas LX 600 continues in Premium, Luxury and F Sport Handling grades. The EPA rates the 2025 LX 600 at 17 city, 22 highway and 19 combined. It's still the most luxurious way into a 300 Series chassis, and with the shorter, boxier GX 550 now on the same platform, it's no longer the only GA-F Lexus that can go off-road.

### Data plate
- Chassis: J310, GA-F ladder frame
- Years: 2022 MY–present
- Engine: V35A-FTS 3.4 L twin-turbo V6
- Output: 409 hp / 479 lb-ft
- Transmission: Direct Shift 10-speed automatic
- 4Wd: Two-speed transfer case, center diff lock
- Suspension: Double wishbone / 4-link solid axle, AHC + AVS
- Wheelbase: 112 in (2,850 mm)
- Angles: 25° / 23° / 20° (normal height)
- Wading: 700 mm (27.5 in)
- Epa (2025): 17 city / 22 hwy / 19 combined
- Towing: 8,000 lb (braked trailer)

### Engineering
The LX 600 is a 300 Series Land Cruiser underneath. It sits on the GA-F ladder frame, which Lexus says is 20 percent more rigid, with high-mounted double wishbones up front and a four-link solid rear axle with lateral control arms. Power from the 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6 goes through a 10-speed automatic and a two-speed transfer case to a lockable center differential. Hydraulic Active Height Control and AVS adaptive damping manage ride height and comfort, and Multi-Terrain Select, Crawl Control and an underfloor camera handle the trail.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, GA-F (441 lb lighter than the LX 570 and 20% more rigid. The wheelbase stays at 112 in.)
- Engine: V35A-FTS 3.4 TT V6 (409 hp and 479 lb-ft. Covered by recalls 24V-381 and 25V-767.)
- Driveline: 10-speed, two-speed transfer case (Center diff lock standard. The F Sport adds a Torsen rear LSD. No US LX 600 has axle lockers.)
- Front: High-mount double wishbone (100 mm bound and 145 mm rebound travel.)
- Rear: 4-link solid axle (Lateral control arms. Rear rebound up 20 mm over the LX 570.)
- Ride Height: AHC + AVS (Low, Normal, Hi1 and Hi2 heights with adaptive damping. Some buyers custom-order without AHC.)

### Versions
- 2022–present · J310 / GA-F · V35A-FTS 3.4 TT V6 · 409 hp / 479 lb-ft · LX 600. Launched in Standard, Premium, Luxury, F Sport and Ultra Luxury grades. 2022–2024 builds are in the engine recalls.
- 2022–present (export) · J310 / GA-F · F33A-FTV 3.3 TT V6 diesel · 304 hp / 516 lb-ft · LX 500d. Not sold in the US.
- Japan only · J310 / GA-F · V35A-FTS 3.4 TT V6 · 409 hp / 479 lb-ft · LX Offroad grade, with front, center and rear diff locks.
- 2025–present · J310 / GA-F · V35A-FTS hybrid · 457 hp / 583 lb-ft · LX 700h. 2,883 US sales in 2025.
- 2025–present · J310 / GA-F · V35A-FTS hybrid · 457 hp / 583 lb-ft · LX 700h Overtrail, revealed October 10, 2024. Front and rear lockers.

### Year-by-year
- 2022: Revealed October 13, 2021 on the GA-F platform: V35A 3.4 twin-turbo V6 (409 hp, 479 lb-ft), 10-speed automatic, 441 lb lighter than the LX 570. Standard, Premium, Luxury, F Sport and four-seat Ultra Luxury grades.
- 2022–2024: Engine recalls 24V-381 and 25V-767 cover main-bearing debris. Owners also report a clunk into first on rolling stops. [avoid]
- 2024: Largely a carryover. Lexus's 2024 release lists Lexus Safety System+ 2.5 as standard and an F Sport Handling grade with 22-in forged wheels and a Torsen limited-slip rear differential.
- 2025: LX 700h hybrid joins the range, including the Overtrail with front and rear lockers plus the center lock (revealed October 10, 2024). 2025 trucks are outside the V35A engine recalls but have their own transmission-ECU recall (26V-094).
- 2027: Minor updates: darker 20-in wheels and a digital mirror on Premium, red calipers and Palomino leather on F Sport Handling, and power-folding rear seats on F Sport Handling and Overtrail.

### Capability
- Towing: 8,000 lb (3,630 kg) (braked trailer, owner's manual; 1,650 lb unbraked)
- Wading depth: 27.5 in (700 mm)
- Roof load: 165 lb (75 kg) (roof luggage carrier limit, owner's manual)
- Fuel tank: 21.1 US gal (80 L) (premium fuel)
- Approach / breakover / departure: 25° / 23° / 20° (normal height)
- Fuel economy: EPA 17 city / 22 hwy / 19 combined (2025 model year (fueleconomy.gov))
- Climbing ability: 45° (Lexus figure; max stable inclination 44°)
- Suspension travel: 3.93 in bound / 5.7 in rebound (100 / 145 mm)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: 265/50R22 112V on 22x8, 265/55R20 113V on 20x8, 265/65R18 114V on 18x7.5
- Bolt Pattern: 6x139.7 (6x5.5")
- Lug Torque: 97 lb-ft (131 N·m)
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 275/60R20 or 285/55R20 (≈33 in) (Owners on aftermarket 20s report no rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18s. 285/50R22 on the factory 22s needed cutting and spacers.)

### Buying checks
- Recall status, in writing: Run the VIN for 24V-381 (engine replacement, trucks built July 2021 to November 2022) and 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07, built February 2022 to April 2024). Get dealer paperwork showing what was done. A replaced engine is a selling point.
- Listen for a knock: The recalls list knocking, rough running, a no-start and a loss of power as symptoms. Start it cold and listen at idle and under light load.
- Rolling-stop behavior: Owners report a clunk into first gear during rolling stops on 2022–2024 trucks, plus sluggish throttle that eases when the pre-collision system is set to its shortest distance. Test both so you know what's normal for these trucks.
- Which grade?: The F Sport gets a Torsen rear LSD and a rear stabilizer bar, but also 22-in forged wheels that limit tire choice. Ultra Luxury is a four-seater. US LX 600s have no axle lockers in any grade.
- AHC health: Cycle through Low, Normal, Hi1 and Hi2 and confirm each height is reached and held. Some trucks were ordered without AHC. Know which one you're buying, because lift options differ.
- Tailgate and electronics: An owner-reported power hatch that beeps and refuses to close was usually a weak key-fob signal or a hatch that needed a manual close to relearn its position. Check that everything works before you assume a fault.
- Bulletin and warranty history: Ask for the dealer service history. Lexus has issued bulletins for front-brake squeal on 2022–2024 trucks (L-SB-0036-24), a windshield-molding buzz above 55 mph (L-SB-0019-24) and a head-unit software update for 2022 models (L-SB-0027-24). Work already done under them is a good sign.
- Power back door: Open and close the hatch several times with the button, the key and the kick sensor. If it beeps twice and won't move, suspect a pinch sensor. IH8MUD owners have had them replaced under warranty.

### Common repairs
#### Engine recall check (24V-381 / 25V-767)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 10 minutes to check. Dealer time varies. · cost Free under recall
Symptoms: Possible engine knocking, rough running, a no-start or a loss of motive power. Many trucks show nothing.
Fix: Enter the VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov/recalls. Under 24V-381, Toyota replaces the engine at no cost. Under 25V-767, NHTSA's record now says dealers inspect the No. 1 main bearing using inspection software and drive data and replace the engine if necessary; owner letters were mailed August 28, 2026. Keep every piece of paperwork.
Tools: VIN · Lexus dealer

#### Early differential, transfer case and transmission fluid service
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours · cost Fluids only (DIY)
Symptoms: None. This is preventive work. Some owners choose to change gear oil early after reports of debris in V35A Tundra differentials after break-in.
Fix: One IH8MUD owner did a 20k-mile service on an LX 700h. That covered the differential gear oil, a transmission fluid exchange and the transfer case, plus greasing the driveline zerks. Their wear-metal results were reassuring. Another owner reports Red Line 75W-85 working fine in the front diff. Remove the skid plates for access, and follow the factory manual's fluid specs and fill levels.
Tools: Socket set · fluid pump · drain pan · torque wrench · gear oil per factory spec · grease gun

#### Front skid plate install
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours · cost Parts plus your time
Symptoms: The factory underbody protection on most LX 600s isn't trail-ready. The LX 700h Overtrail is the exception, with a steel skid from the factory.
Fix: Bolt the aftermarket skid to the frame mounts, and change the front diff fluid while you're under there. One owner fitting Slee's skid to an F Sport found that a bracket didn't line up with the tow-hook points, likely because of the F Sport's different bumper and chassis vibration damper. Confirm fitment for your grade before you start.
Tools: Floor jack · sockets · torque wrench · skid plate kit (e.g. Slee Off-Road)

#### Laggy throttle at rolling stops
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time ≈ 5 minutes · cost Free
Symptoms: Delayed or missing throttle response pulling out of a rolling stop on 2024 trucks. Owners say it's worse in Sport and Sport+.
Fix: Owners traced it to the pre-collision system limiting torque. As an interim fix, set PCS to its shortest warning distance, one green bar, in the gauge-cluster menu. Turning PCS off removes the lag but also disables a key safety system. Ask your dealer about software updates.
Tools: None

#### Bigger tires on aftermarket wheels
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 1–2 hours · cost Wheels and tires
Symptoms: Not a fault. The factory 22s limit you to low-profile tires that dislike rocks.
Fix: Owners report running 275/55R20 and 285/55R20 on 30-offset Vossen 20s without rubbing, 275/60R20 (about 33 in) on aftermarket 20s, and 275/70R18 on Toyota TRD 18s. One dealer forced 285/50R22 A/Ts onto factory wheels, but it took cutting and spacers.
Tools: Lug wrench · torque wrench · hub-centric wheels in the right offset · TPMS sensors

#### Front brake squeal (bulletin L-SB-0036-24)
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 2 hours for front pads and rotors (estimate) · cost Covered under the bulletin while in warranty (owner report). Otherwise pads and rotors.
Symptoms: A squeal from the front brakes when moving forward or in reverse. Owners mostly hear it on the first stops of a cold or humid morning, and it fades once the brakes warm up.
Fix: Lexus bulletin L-SB-0036-24 (October 2024) covers front-brake squeal on 2022–2024 LX 600s and 2024 GX 550s. An IH8MUD owner's dealer said the fix was new front pads and rotors at no charge, though the parts were back-ordered at the time. Ask a dealer to check your VIN against the bulletin first. Out of warranty, fit new pads and rotors, clean the caliper hardware and pad abutments, use a thin film of brake grease where the pads slide, and bed the new pads in.
Tools: Lug wrench · socket set · torque wrench · brake cleaner · high-temperature brake grease · pads and rotors

#### Windshield rattle or buzz at speed (bulletin L-SB-0019-24)
Difficulty 1 / 5 · time Dealer visit. A few minutes to clear leaves from the cowl. · cost Warranty work under the bulletin. Free for the cowl clean-out.
Symptoms: A rattle or buzz from the windshield's outer edge molding above about 55 mph. Separately, owners chasing a rattle at the lower driver's-side corner of the windshield found leaves trapped near the hood hinge and in the wiper well.
Fix: Lexus bulletin L-SB-0019-24 (April 2024) covers a rattle or buzz from the windshield outer edge molding above 55 mph on 2022–2024 LX 600s, so have a dealer inspect and repair the molding under it. Before you book, open the hood and vacuum leaves and debris out of the cowl and wiper well. One owner plans to add foam to keep the leaves out.
Tools: Shop vacuum · flashlight · trim tools if you inspect the molding yourself

#### Power back door won't close (pinch sensor)
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 5 minutes for the checks. Dealer visit for sensors. · cost Warranty (owner reports)
Symptoms: The hatch opens normally, but when you press close it beeps once or twice and won't move, so you have to shut it by hand. The hands-free kick sensor may only beep.
Fix: Rule out the easy causes first. A weak key signal, such as from the credit-card key, can stop it, and a hatch left open for hours can forget its position until you close it by hand once. If it keeps happening, have the pinch (touch) sensors along the hatch edges tested. Two IH8MUD owners, with a 2023 and a 2024 LX 600, had pinch sensors replaced under warranty, one on the left side and the other on both sides. For a kick sensor that only beeps, one owner reset it this way: turn hands-free off in the center console, switch the truck off, open and close the hatch from outside, switch it back on and re-enable hands-free. A bike rack over the bumper sensors can also stop it working.
Tools: Key fob · Lexus dealer for sensor diagnosis

### Baseline service
The LX 600 is still young enough that a baseline is mostly about proving what's been done. Check the engine recall status first, then do the early gear-oil change owners recommend, and service the AHC on trucks that have it. Specs come from the LX 600 owner's manual (OM60V34U), and intervals from the 2023 Lexus maintenance schedule.
- Engine oil & filter: SAE 0W-20, ILSAC GF-6A · 7.7 US qt (7.3 L) with filter · At purchase, then every 10,000 mi / 12 months. Every 5,000 mi / 6 months for off-road, towing or dusty use. (Lexus says to replace the element and the filter-cap O-ring together at every oil change.)
- Air filter: V35A-FTS element · Every 30,000 mi. Inspect more often off-road.
- Cabin filter: Cabin air filter element · Every 30,000 mi
- Spark plugs: Denso EC22HPR-D7 iridium · gap 0.7 mm. Do not adjust the gap. · Every 40,000 mi (40k, 80k and 120k in the 2023 schedule) (The interval is much shorter than on the old V8s, so check the records.)
- Engine & intercooler coolant: Toyota Super Long Life · engine 15.5 US qt, intercooler circuit 4.0 US qt · First at 100,000 mi / 120 months, then every 50,000 mi / 60 months (Two separate circuits. The twin-turbo V6 has its own water-to-air intercooler loop.)
- Automatic transmission (10-speed): Toyota Genuine ATF WS · 12.13 US qt (reference) · Every 60,000 mi if you tow or carry heavy loads (An IH8MUD owner did a fluid exchange at 20,000 mi on an LX 700h and got good wear-metal results.)
- Transfer case: Toyota Genuine Transfer Gear Oil LF, SAE 75W · 1.89 US qt (1.79 L) · Early change at purchase, then every 30,000 mi off-road or towing
- Front & rear differentials: 75W-85 GL-5: Toyota LT oil for open diffs, LX oil for a rear limited-slip · front 1.23 US qt, rear 5.76 US qt (5.55 US qt with LSD) · Early change at purchase, then every 15,000 mi off-road or towing (Some owners change gear oil early after reports of debris in V35A Tundra diffs. Use the LX-type oil if the rear is a limited-slip. The skid plates have to come off.)
- AHC suspension fluid: Lexus Suspension Fluid AHC (trucks with AHC) · Replace at 60,000 mi (2023 schedule). Inspect the AHC system and gas chambers at every major service. (Cycle through the heights and watch each corner before you buy.)
- Brake fluid: DOT 3 or DOT 4 (SAE J1703 / J1704) · Replace at 60,000 mi (2023 schedule)
- Propeller shaft grease: Spiders: lithium chassis grease NLGI No. 2 · front slide yoke: moly lithium or lithium NLGI No. 2 · At purchase, then within 24 hours of any water crossing
- Drive belt: Serpentine belt · Inspect at purchase

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: The factory size on 22s is 265/50R22, about 32 in. Owners on aftermarket 20s run 275/60R20 (about 33 in) and 285/55R20 without rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18-inch wheels. 285/50R22 on factory wheels needed cutting and spacers. Without a lift, plan on about 33 in.

Q: Is my LX 600 part of the engine recall?
A: If it's a 2022–2024, possibly. Recall 24V-381 covered 3,524 LX 600s built from July 30, 2021 to November 25, 2022, with engine replacement as the remedy. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 9,895 LXs built from February 26, 2022 to April 2, 2024. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov. The 25V-767 remedy is a No. 1 main-bearing inspection, with engine replacement if needed.

Q: How much can it tow?
A: 8,000 lb with trailer brakes, per the owner's manual (1,650 lb without). KBB lists the same 8,000-lb rating for every 2027 LX.

Q: Is the LX 600 just a 300 Series Land Cruiser?
A: Underneath, yes: same GA-F platform and 112-in wheelbase. Toyota didn't sell the LC300 in North America, which made the LX 600 the US version.

Q: Does it have lockers?
A: There's a lockable center diff, but no US LX 600 has front or rear lockers. The F Sport gets a Torsen limited-slip rear. Triple locks came on Japan's LX Offroad grade and, in the US, on the LX 700h Overtrail.

Q: How do I use 4L and the diff locks?
A: Owners say the center diff lock can be engaged while moving slowly in Drive. Shifting into 4L requires the truck to be stopped and in neutral. On trucks with axle lockers, the front and rear lockers need 4L and the center lock engaged first, at very low speed. If you switch off the engine in 4L, MTS won't come back on automatically.

Q: What fuel economy should I expect?
A: The EPA rates the 2025 LX 600 at 17 mpg city, 22 highway and 19 combined, on premium fuel.

Q: How much lighter is it than the LX 570?
A: Lexus says 441 lb (200 kg) lighter, with a frame it calls 20 percent more rigid.

Q: What are the off-road angles?
A: At normal ride height, 25° approach, 23° breakover and 20° departure. Lexus hasn't published figures for the Hi1 and Hi2 heights. Maximum wading depth is 700 mm (27.5 in).

Q: Why does it clunk into first gear?
A: Owners report a clunk into first on rolling stops, and sometimes on 6–5 downshifts, in 2022–2024 LX 600s. There's no known fix. Gentle throttle while the transmission decides helps, and larger tires make it less noticeable. Owners say the LX 700h hybrid doesn't do it.

Q: Should I buy one without AHC?
A: If you plan to lift it, maybe. Slee Off-Road's LX 600 build was a Premium custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension. AHC trucks keep the adjustable ride heights but limit your lift choices.

Q: Which years are the best to buy?
A: Too new for a consensus. 2022–2024 trucks are the ones with paperwork to check: engine recalls 24V-381 and 25V-767, plus a neutral-rollaway software recall. NHTSA doesn't list those engine recalls for 2025, but 2025–2026 trucks have their own transmission-ECU software recall (26V-094). Whichever year, run the VIN.

## Lexus GX 470 (2003–2009)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/gx470/
Codes: J120, UZJ120, 2UZ-FE

Verdict: A Prado in a dinner jacket with a V8 that refuses to die. The trick is buying one before the previous owner's deferred maintenance becomes yours.

The Lexus GX 470 is a Land Cruiser Prado 120, the mid-size Land Cruiser the rest of the world got and North America never did, dressed for a suburb it was always overqualified for. Underneath the wood trim are a ladder frame, a four-link solid rear axle with a lateral rod, full-time four-wheel drive with low range and a lockable center differential, plus Toyota's 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8. It was sold to people who wanted a nice SUV. It is now bought by people who want to cross Nevada on dirt roads.

### A PRADO FOR AMERICA
Development started in 1999, two years after the J120 Prado program it was built on, and design work was finished in the first half of 2000. Lexus showed the GX at the 2002 North American International Auto Show as a 2003 model, and sales began in November 2002. It was slotted underneath the LX 470, which was itself a 100 Series Land Cruiser in a suit.
The GX had company on the Tahara assembly line. Expedition Portal notes it was built on the same line as the Prado and the 4th-gen 4Runner, and the 4Runner shares its suspension layout, rear air springs included on some trims. That family resemblance is useful. Forum regulars routinely borrow 4Runner parts, tire-fitment data and even used steering racks for their GXs.

### THE 2UZ AND THE GADGETS
At launch the 2UZ-FE made 235 hp and 320 lb-ft. Variable valve timing (VVT-i) arrived for 2005 and pushed output to 270 hp. A change in SAE testing procedures restated that as 263 hp from 2006, with no actual change to the hardware. Midway through 2004, a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch raised the tow rating from 5,000 to 6,500 lb. The transmission also became a sealed unit with no dipstick that year.
Lexus being Lexus, the clever hardware came with complications. The rear axle rides on air springs with ride-height control, and the dampers are driver-adjustable through Adaptive Variable Suspension. Downhill Assist Control handles steep descents, and KDSS, a hydraulically linked anti-roll system, became an option late in the 2004 model year. All of it works brilliantly until it gets old. Then the air springs leak, the compressor wears itself out chasing them, and the truck sits on its bump stops.

### WHY OVERLANDERS LOVE IT
Four Wheeler magazine named the GX its Four Wheeler of the Year for 2003 and 2004, which was unusual praise for a vehicle with a Mark Levinson stereo option. Expedition Portal's project truck called the J120 "often considered the pinnacle of the body-on-frame era" and called the V8 "one of the most reliable engines ever sold in the USA." It also pointed to a 109-inch wheelbase and payload higher than the 4Runner's.
The weak points are well mapped. Owners report aging steering racks, CV boots, lower ball joints and cracked exhaust manifolds (often the driver's side), plus the timing belt that someone eventually has to pay for. Lexus ran a warranty enhancement program for cracked or sticky dashboards on 2003–2008 trucks. None of these problems scares off people who own a floor jack, which is why aftermarket support is now deep: lifts, rear coil conversions, skids, sliders and bumpers built specifically for this truck.

### HOW IT ENDED
US sales peaked at 35,420 in 2004 and slid to 6,235 in 2009. A 2008 facelift brought a dark metallic grille, graphite-finish wheels and more chrome. The GX 460 replaced it after debuting in November 2009, followed by the boxy GX 550, which shares its bones with the 250 Series Land Cruiser.
The GX 470's afterlife has been kinder than its retirement. Cheap examples with high mileage and full service records are the starter overland rig of choice, because the V8 lasts and the chassis was always a Land Cruiser. The suspension complexity is optional. You can retire it with a coil conversion and a Saturday afternoon.

### Data plate
- Chassis: J120 (UZJ120)
- Years: 2003–2009 MY
- Engine: 2UZ-FE 4.7 L V8
- Output: 235 hp → 270 hp (2005) → 263 hp (2006+ SAE)
- Transmission: 5-speed auto (A750F)
- 4Wd: Full-time, low range, locking center diff
- Rear Suspension: 4-link solid axle, air springs
- Wheelbase: 109.8 in (2,790 mm)
- Ground Clearance: 8.3 in
- Towing: 5,000 lb → 6,500 lb (mid-2004)
- Stock Tire: 265/65R17
- Us Sales: ≈174,500 (2002–2009)

### Engineering
The GX 470 is a J120 Prado underneath: a high-strength ladder frame, coil-over independent front suspension and a four-link solid rear axle with a lateral rod. Full-time 4WD runs through a two-speed transfer case and a helical limited-slip center differential that can be locked, with open differentials front and rear and brake-based A-TRAC traction control to cover for them. Lexus then layered on rear air springs with height control, adjustable dampers and, as an option from 2004, KDSS.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, J120 (Shared with the Land Cruiser Prado 120. The 4th-gen 4Runner shares its suspension layout.)
- Engine: 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 (32-valve quad-cam with a timing belt. VVT-i from 2005.)
- Driveline: Full-time 4WD (Two-speed transfer case and a lockable helical LSD center diff. VSC switches off when the center diff is locked.)
- Front: Independent, coilover (Owners call the factory spring rate soft. Optional KDSS adds a hydraulically linked anti-roll system.)
- Rear: 4-link solid axle (Lexus calls it a 4-link (plus a lateral rod). Air springs with height control. Many owners convert to coils.)
- Traction: A-TRAC + DAC (Brake-based traction control plus Downhill Assist Control. There are no factory axle lockers.)

### Versions
- 2003 · UZJ120 · 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 · 235 hp / 320 lb-ft · Launch year. Rated to tow 5,000 lb.
- 2004 · UZJ120 · 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 · 235 hp / 320 lb-ft · Added curtain airbags, TPMS and a sealed transmission. A mid-year hitch upgrade raised towing to 6,500 lb, and KDSS became optional late in the year.
- 2005 · UZJ120 · 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 VVT-i · 270 hp · VVT-i and ULEV II certification. New Sport model.
- 2006–2007 · UZJ120 · 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 VVT-i · 263 hp · Same engine, restated under revised SAE testing.
- 2008–2009 · UZJ120 · 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 VVT-i · 263 hp · Facelift with a dark grille, graphite wheels and more chrome.

### Year-by-year
- 2003: Launch at the 2002 Detroit show, on sale November 2002. 2UZ-FE 4.7 V8 at 235 hp, five-speed automatic, rear air suspension. Rated to tow 5,000 lb.
- 2004: Sealed transmission (no dipstick), TPMS, roll-sensing curtain airbags and an optional backup camera. A mid-year hitch upgrade raised towing to 6,500 lb, and KDSS became optional late in the year.
- 2005: VVT-i lifts output to 270 hp with ULEV II certification. Bluetooth and a new Sport model with KDSS standard.
- 2006: Same engine, restated at 263 hp under revised SAE testing. Lexus Link telematics offered.
- 2007: New-generation navigation, auxiliary input jack and a larger optional rear-seat screen.
- 2008: Facelift: dark metallic grille, liquid-graphite wheels, more chrome and revised turn signals.
- 2009: Final year. Only 6,235 GXs were sold in calendar 2009 before the GX 460 took over.

### Capability
- Towing: 6,500 lb (2,948 kg) (2003 and early-2004 trucks: 5,000 lb)
- GVWR: 6,150 lb (2,790 kg) (2009 Canadian spec)
- Fuel tank: 23 US gal (87 L)
- Ground clearance: 8.3 in (210 mm)
- Approach / departure: 31° / 25° (breakover not published)
- Fuel economy: EPA 14 city / 18 hwy / 15 combined (2007, premium fuel)
- Curb weight: 4,740 lb (2,150 kg) (base, 2009 Canadian spec)
- Turning circle: 38.4 ft (11.7 m)
- Wheelbase: 109.8 in (2,790 mm)

### Wheels and tires
- Stock tires: P265/65R17 110S on 17x7.5 alloys
- Bolt Pattern: 6x139.7 (6x5.5")
- Lug Torque: 82 lb-ft (112 N·m)
- Biggest tire, Stock lift: 265/70R17 (GXOR's limit with no modification at all; 255/75R17 also fits with no rubbing. One owner reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse on 265/70.)
- Biggest tire, Stock, trimmed lift: 285/70R17 (Fits without a lift only with a body mount chop and the fender liner reshaped with a heat gun (and maybe a knife).)
- Biggest tire, 2–3 in lift: 285/70R17 or 255/80R17 (33 in) (The usual route to 33s. Expect some fender-liner trimming; owners on 285/70R17 with about 2.5–3 in of lift still cut a little liner.)
- Biggest tire, 4.5 in (suspension + body lift) lift: 295/70R18 (One GXOR database entry, on 18x9 −12 wheels, with the body mounts cut back.)

### Buying checks
- Frame rust: Forum veterans call this the biggest concern on trucks from the salt belt. Get underneath with a light and a screwdriver, or ask for close-up photos of the frame. Rust on the rear air-spring perches is also what kills the airbags.
- Rear air suspension: Look for a rear end that sags overnight, a blinking height-control light, a harsh ride or a compressor that runs constantly. Spray soapy water where each airbag folds over its lower perch. If the system is already converted to coils, ask whose kit was used.
- Timing belt history: The 2UZ-FE uses a belt that Toyota schedules at 90,000 miles, and the water pump runs off it. If there's no receipt, budget roughly $1K at a shop or a weekend of your own time. Engine Builder classes all belt-driven Toyota V8s as interference engines, so don't gamble on an unknown belt.
- Cold-start tick: A tick that fades as the engine warms is the classic sign of a cracked exhaust manifold, often on the driver's side. The repair is a big one, so treat it as a price negotiation point.
- Steering rack: Look for wet rack boots and power-steering fluid on the crossmember, and listen for creaking or whining at full lock. One ClubLexus owner's rack began creaking and whining loudly at about 130k miles.
- Front end wear: Check for torn lower ball-joint boots and grease slung from the CV boots, and listen for clunks over bumps. Many trucks need lower control arms or ball joints, CV axles and front bearings at this age.
- KDSS or not?: Turn the key and watch for a momentary KDSS light, or look for the oversized front sway bar. KDSS improves stability and articulation, but some skids and sliders need KDSS-specific versions or modifications.
- Dashboard: Heat cracks and sticky dashboard surfaces are common enough that Lexus ran a warranty enhancement program for 2003–2008 GX 470s. Check whether the dash was already replaced, and confirm with a dealer whether any coverage still applies.

### Common repairs
#### Rear air spring replacement or coil conversion
Difficulty 2 / 5 · time ≈ 2 hours (simple coil swap) to half a day (with new trailing arms) · cost Under $200 in parts for a basic coil swap (owner report)
Symptoms: The rear sits low or sags overnight, the ride turns harsh, the height-control light blinks, the compressor runs nonstop, and in the worst case the truck is sitting on its bump stops.
Fix: First confirm the leak with soapy water where each bag folds over its perch. To keep air, replace both springs, and the compressor if it has worn out chasing leaks. To convert, support the axle, remove the shocks, cut the air lines and pop each bag's upper U-clip with a flat-head screwdriver, then fit a coil conversion kit with springs, retainers and isolators. The ride-height sensor sits on the upper trailing arm, and the compressor and reservoir live on the driver's side. Recheck bolt torque after 100 miles.
Tools: Floor jack · jack stands · flat-head screwdriver · line cutters · torque wrench · coil conversion kit (e.g. Metal Tech 4x4 hardware with Icon 52800 3-in coils) · or Arnott air springs and compressor (P-3192) to stay on air

#### Timing belt and water pump
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time ≈ a full weekend for a first-timer · cost About $950–$1,770 at shops, as quoted by owners on ClubLexus (the higher figure included a radiator and plugs)
Symptoms: No symptoms until it fails, which is the problem. Due every 90,000 miles. The water pump is belt-driven, so a weeping pump or coolant crust behind the timing covers is a good reason to do both now.
Fix: Remove the fan and shroud, accessory belts and crank pulley, then the timing covers. Set the engine to its timing marks and replace the belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump, plus the thermostat and hoses while you're in there. Before installing the new belt, compare its tooth count and alignment marks against the old one, because Engine Builder warns that even a half-tooth error means doing the job twice. Watch for P0011, P0016, P0018 or P0021 afterward, which can point to timing misalignment.
Tools: Crank pulley holder · long breaker bar · torque wrench · coolant · belt kit with tensioner, idlers and water pump (OEM or Aisin-type kit)

#### Exhaust manifold replacement (often the driver's side)
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time Same-day job at a specialist shop · cost Parts plus labor (high: engine mounts have to come out)
Symptoms: A ticking noise from the engine bay that is loudest cold and often fades as the manifold heats and expands. The cause is a paper-thin crack where the flange meets the first pipe.
Fix: Soak every fastener in penetrating oil for days beforehand. The engine mounts must be released, and the engine raised, to reach the lower manifold studs. Replace the manifold assembly with new gaskets, studs and nuts. Expect seized or broken studs on rusty trucks. Afterward, idle the engine for about half an hour to burn off manufacturing oil.
Tools: Engine support or jack · penetrating oil · stud extractor set · new manifold, gaskets, studs and nuts

#### Steering rack replacement
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ half a day plus an alignment · cost $1,900 at an independent shop including tie-rod ends and high-pressure hoses (owner report). Parts run from about $300 for an aftermarket rack to about $1,000 for new OEM.
Symptoms: Wet rack boots, a falling power-steering reservoir, and creaking or whining on every turn of the wheel.
Fix: First confirm the source: clean the engine bay and recheck, because hoses and the pump can drip onto the rack. Then disconnect the tie-rod ends and pressure lines, unbolt the rack and swap in an OEM reman unit with new bushings. While it's out, remove and clean the reservoir and its mesh screen, and consider an inline filter. Bleed the system, then get an alignment.
Tools: Tie-rod end puller · flare-nut wrenches · drain pan · ATF/PS fluid · OEM reman rack (e.g. CVJ or Cardone) · new rack bushings

#### Front lower ball joints and control arms
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ half a day for both sides · cost About $270 per OEM lower control arm (owner report, 4Runner V8 part). The OEM ball joint is only sold with the arm.
Symptoms: Torn ball-joint boots weeping grease, clunks over bumps, and vague steering. Worn lower control arm bushings add knocks of their own.
Fix: Either replace the whole lower control arm with its new ball joint and bushings, or press out the old joint and press in an aftermarket one (owners cite MOOG K500017 and Sankei 555). Make sure the grease fitting faces an accessible direction, and grease the new joint if it shipped dry. Buy KDSS or non-KDSS parts to match your truck, then align it.
Tools: Ball-joint press · pickle fork or joint separator · torque wrench · grease gun · lower control arm or ball joint

#### Front CV axle replacement
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours per side · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: Grease slung around the inside of the wheel, split CV boots, and clicking on tight turns.
Fix: Loosen the axle nut with the wheel on the ground, then lift the truck. Separate the lower ball joint or tie rod enough to swing the knuckle, pull the axle out of the hub and pop the inner joint from the differential. Install a new axle; Expedition Portal's project truck used factory Toyota parts. Torque the axle nut, then stake or pin it.
Tools: Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · pry bar · joint separator · torque wrench · new axle nut and OEM axle

#### Front differential support upgrade (2003–early 2005)
Difficulty 3 / 5 · time ≈ 2–3 hours (estimate) · cost Parts plus labor
Symptoms: Usually nothing until it breaks. GXOR warns that the original passenger-side front differential support can fail catastrophically, which can take out nearby parts, the oil pan included, and the engine with it.
Fix: Lexus revised the passenger-side front differential support for 2006, and some 2005s got the new part at the factory. On a 2003 to early-2005 truck, get under the passenger side of the front diff and read the number on the support. The revised part is ordered as 52380-60021 but stamped 52391-60021. If yours is the old one, take the diff's weight on a jack, unbolt the old support, fit the revised one and torque the bolts to factory spec.
Tools: Floor jack and stands · socket set · torque wrench · revised support 52380-60021 (stamped 52391-60021)

#### Secondary air injection pump (2005–2009)
Difficulty 4 / 5 · time A long day. The intake manifold has to come off (GXOR). · cost A mechanic quoted one ClubLexus owner about $2,000
Symptoms: A 'vacuum cleaner' whine for about 30 seconds after a cold start that gets rougher as the pump fails. Owners report codes including P2440, P2442, P2445 and P2432, and one reported random limp mode. GXOR says a failed system usually affects only cold-start emissions, not driveability.
Fix: Scan the codes first. The pump and its air switching valves sit under the intake manifold, so the manifold has to come off to reach them. GXOR lists two routes: repair with a Dorman OE-replacement pump, or delete with a Hewitt Technologies bypass kit. A delete may fail emissions inspection where you live. One ClubLexus owner's bypass worked for about a year before P2445 returned. Fit new intake gaskets on reassembly. One owner said the pump was covered by a 10-year/150,000-mile extension, which has long expired on most trucks.
Tools: Scan tool · socket set with extensions · torque wrench · intake manifold gaskets · air pump and switching valves

### Baseline service
Most GX 470s are well past the 90,000-mile timing-belt interval, so a used one should be treated as overdue until you see a receipt. Baseline every fluid as well. The 2005 factory repair manual (posted on GXOR) gives the specs below, and GXOR flags two GX-specific checks: the 2003–05 front differential support and the rear air springs.
- Engine oil & filter: SAE 5W-30 multigrade (5W-30 is the manual's best choice) · 6.5 US qt (6.2 L) with filter · At purchase, then every 5,000 mi / 6 months (2008 Lexus schedule) (Spin-on filter. Replace the drain-plug gasket every time.)
- Timing belt, water pump & tensioner: Belt, water pump, tensioner and idlers. GXOR's parts list adds a fan pulley bracket, radiator hoses, drive belt, thermostat and radiator cap. · Every 90,000 mi / 108 months (2008 Lexus schedule) (If there's no receipt, assume it's due. Use about two gallons of Toyota Super Long Life pink premix for the refill (GXOR).)
- Coolant: Toyota Super Long Life coolant or equivalent · 13.6 US qt (12.9 L) · First at 100,000 mi / 120 months, then every 50,000 mi / 60 months (Usually done alongside the timing belt and water pump.)
- Spark plugs: Denso SK20R11 or NGK IFR6A11 · gap 1.0–1.1 mm · Every 120,000 mi (2008 Lexus schedule) (Replace the spark-plug tube seals if the valve covers come off.)
- Air filter: 2UZ-FE panel element · Replace every 30,000 mi. Inspect more often on dusty roads. (If the filter is oily, the factory manual says the PCV valve may be stuck.)
- Cabin filter: Air conditioner filter element · At purchase, then every 30,000 mi / 36 months (2008 Lexus schedule)
- Automatic transmission (A750F): Toyota Genuine ATF WS only · 3.2 US qt (3.0 L) per drain-and-refill, 11.0 US qt (10.4 L) dry fill · At purchase. The schedule only calls for ATF changes when towing (60,000 mi), but GXOR says many owners change it anyway. (A drain-and-fill swaps only about a quarter of the fluid, so do it two or three times. GXOR lists a pan gasket (35168-60010), strainer (35330-60050), strainer O-ring (90301-31014) and drain/fill plug gaskets (35178-30010, two required) if you drop the pan.)
- Transfer case: Hypoid gear oil API GL-5, SAE 75W-90 · 1.5 US qt (1.4 L) · At purchase, then every 30,000 mi if you tow (2008 schedule) (Fill until oil reaches within 5 mm of the bottom edge of the filler hole.)
- Front & rear differentials: Hypoid gear oil API GL-5: SAE 90 above 0 °F, SAE 80W or 80W-90 below · front 1.48 US qt (1.40 L), rear 3.22 US qt (3.05 L) · At purchase, then every 15,000 mi if you tow (2008 schedule) (Rear is the 8 in axle GXOR calls weak. Check the magnetic plug for metal.)
- Front differential support (2003–early 2005): Revised passenger-side support, Toyota 52380-60021 (stamped 52391-60021) · Check once at purchase (GXOR says the early support can fail catastrophically and take the oil pan with it. Some 2005s have the updated part from the factory.)
- Power steering fluid: ATF Dexron II or III · 1.0 US qt (1.0 L) total · Check level and leaks at purchase (Leaks from hoses and the pump can drip onto the rack and look like a rack leak.)
- Brake fluid: SAE J1703 or FMVSS No. 116 DOT 3 · At purchase, then every 30,000 mi (2008 schedule)
- Propeller shafts & front bearings: Lithium-base chassis grease NLGI No. 2 for the spiders and slide yoke · Grease at purchase. Grease after water crossings. (The factory chassis checklist also calls for repacking the front wheel bearings and the drive-shaft bushing grease. Wipe mud off the fittings before you pump in grease.)
- Rear air suspension: Air springs, compressor and height sensor · Inspect at purchase (Check that the truck holds height overnight and listen for the compressor running often. GXOR says the bags will eventually fail, and the usual fix is a coil conversion.)

### FAQ
Q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
A: The stock size is 265/65R17. On a stock or nearly stock GX 470, the safe consensus is about 31.5 inches. Owners report 265/70R17 working with little or no rubbing (one reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse), and 255/75R17 with zero rubbing. Going to 33 inches (285/70R17, or the narrower 255/80R17) generally means a 2–3 in lift and some liner trimming.

Q: How much can a GX 470 tow?
A: 2003 models are rated for 5,000 lb. Midway through the 2004 model year, Lexus fitted a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch and raised the rating to 6,500 lb.

Q: What fuel economy should I expect?
A: The EPA rates it at 14 mpg city, 18 highway and 15 combined (2007), and it calls for premium fuel. Bigger tires typically cost owners another 1 to 1.5 mpg.

Q: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
A: It's a belt. Toyota's interval for UZ V8s is 90,000 miles, and the belt drives the water pump, so most owners replace both together.

Q: What fluids and capacities does it take?
A: Per the 2005 factory repair manual: engine oil 5W-30, 6.5 US qt (6.2 L) with filter. The A750F automatic takes Toyota Genuine ATF WS only, about 3.2 qt (3.0 L) per drain-and-fill and 11.0 qt (10.4 L) dry. Transfer case: 1.5 qt (1.4 L, about 3 pints) of GL-5 75W-90. Front diff 1.48 qt (1.40 L) and rear diff 3.22 qt (3.05 L), both GL-5 SAE 90 (80W-90 below 0°F). Coolant is about 13.6 qt (12.9 L) of Toyota Super Long Life. Confirm against your own manual for your model year.

Q: When should I lock the center diff?
A: Lock it whenever you're off pavement with loose traction. Many owners leave it locked for all trail driving, because it cuts down how much A-TRAC has to work on climbs. Unlock it for very tight turns on grippy surfaces and back on pavement. VSC is disabled while the center diff is locked.

Q: Should I keep the rear air suspension?
A: It works well while healthy, and Expedition Portal's build kept it for load leveling. But aging bags leak where they fold over rusty perches, compressors wear out chasing those leaks, and a failure can leave you on the bump stops. Many owners convert to coils for well under the cost of new air parts.

Q: How do I tell if a GX 470 has KDSS?
A: Watch for a momentary KDSS light when you turn the key, or look for the noticeably large front sway bar. It was optional from late in the 2004 model year. It helps both stability and articulation, but it complicates some armor installs.

Q: Which years should I buy?
A: There's no consensus year. Every GX 470 has the same 2UZ-FE V8 and A750F five-speed automatic; 2005 added VVT-i (270 hp, restated as 263 hp from 2006). Some Expedition Portal members hold out for a VVT-i truck, but the thread's own starter calls it a mixed bag, one ClubLexus owner who drove both says you can't tell the difference to 60 mph, and that thread's starter reckons quality is much the same across the model years. Trucks from mid-2004 get the 6,500 lb hitch and 2008–2009 the facelift. In practice, rust, timing-belt records, air suspension, steering rack and manifold matter more than the build date.

Q: What lift options are there?
A: Common choices are Icon's 0–3.5 in systems (sold by Metal Tech 4x4), ToyTec kits, and Old Man Emu BP-51 coilovers, which Expedition Portal used. ARB doesn't list the GX as an approved application, so check warranty terms first. Pair any front lift with a rear coil conversion or an air spacer to level it.

Q: Is it really just a 4Runner?
A: Not quite. It's a Land Cruiser Prado 120 underneath. The 4th-gen 4Runner shares its suspension layout and was built on the same Tahara line, so many parts and much of the forum knowledge carry across. The GX had the V8 and full-time 4WD with a center lock as standard.

## Lexus GX 460 (2010–2023)
URL: https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/gx460/
Codes: J150, URJ150, 1UR-FE

Verdict: Fourteen years, one V8, zero reinventions. The GX 460 was the luxury SUV your accountant approved of, and it turns out it was also a Prado 150 with a locking center diff.

The Lexus GX 460 is the Land Cruiser Prado 150 in a tailored suit, and it wore that suit for fourteen model years. Underneath are a ladder frame, a solid rear axle, a 301-hp 4.6-liter 1UR-FE V8, a six-speed automatic and full-time four-wheel drive with a Torsen center differential that locks. Lexus sold it to people who liked heated seats. The second-hand market sells it to people who like the fact that it shares its bones with the 5th-gen 4Runner and still has a V8.

### A ROUGH FIRST MONTH
The second-generation GX debuted at the Guangzhou auto show in November 2009 and kept the GX 470's formula: body-on-frame construction and full-time four-wheel drive. Lexus made the Kinetic Dynamic Suspension System (KDSS) standard, swapped the floor-mounted transfer lever for a toggle switch and fitted a Torsen center differential that normally splits torque 40:60 front to rear, moving to 50:50 when it detects rear-wheel slip.
Then, on April 13, 2010, Consumer Reports gave the GX 460 its first 'Don't Buy: Safety Risk' label since 2001. In a lift-off oversteer test, the stability control reacted too slowly. Toyota suspended sales that day, confirmed the result itself three days later and recalled the trucks for a VSC software update on April 19. Sales resumed April 29, and Consumer Reports lifted the label on May 7.

### SPINDLES, SCREENS AND SLOW EVOLUTION
After that rocky start, Lexus left the hardware alone and changed the face. The 2014 refresh brought the spindle grille, LED headlights and a $4,750 price cut. It also reshuffled the trims, so the 2010–2013 Premium roughly equals the 2014-on Luxury, which is where you find the rear air suspension and adaptive dampers. For 2020 came a sharper grille, triple-beam LEDs and an Off-Road package with a 360-degree camera, a transmission cooler, a fuel-tank protector, Crawl Control and Multi-Terrain Select.
Apple CarPlay and Android Auto finally showed up in 2022, along with a new dashboard. Through all of it, the 1UR-FE and the six-speed stayed put. In China, Lexus sold a GX 400 with a 4.0-liter V6 from 2012 to 2017. Everywhere else, the GX 460 kept its V8 until the end. Toyota's habit of running a platform for a long time is usually a sign that the platform is good.

### THE BUILDERS SHOW UP
For years the GX 460 lived in the shadow of the GX 470, partly because early aftermarket support was thin. That changed. IH8MUD's GX 460 build guide now lists purpose-built bumpers, sliders, skids and roof racks from Metal Tech 4x4, Southern Style Offroad, RCI, CBI, Dobinsons, Ironman and ARB. Front and gas-tank skids from the 5th-gen 4Runner can often be swapped across, and forum regulars report fitting 35-inch tires with a 2–2.5 in lift, new upper control arms, a body mount chop and some fender work.
Owners also discovered that the factory electronics can be unlocked. Crawl Control and Multi-Terrain Select can be retrofitted to any 2010–2019 truck with factory switches and a zero-point calibration. That's the GX 460 in a nutshell: more capability was always there, and Lexus mostly didn't mention it.

### HOW IT ENDED
The GX 460 never really faded. US sales peaked at 32,509 in 2021, and it still found 31,910 buyers in its final year, 2023. It was replaced by the boxy GX 550, which moves to the GA-F platform shared with the 250 Series Land Cruiser and swaps the V8 for a twin-turbo V6.
That leaves the 460 as the last V8 GX, and for some buyers that's the whole point. Its known weak spots are expensive leaks rather than catastrophic failures: water pumps, a coolant passage under the intake manifold called the coolant valley, timing covers, plus the secondary air pump on early trucks. None of them is a mystery, and all of them are documented step by step by owners who'd rather keep the V8 than trade for a newer engine.

### Data plate
- Chassis: J150 (URJ150)
- Years: 2010–2023 MY
- Engine: 1UR-FE 4.6 L V8, timing chain
- Output: 301 hp / 329 lb-ft (US)
- Transmission: 6-speed automatic
- 4Wd: Full-time, low range, Torsen locking center diff
- Suspension: KDSS standard; rear air (RAHC) on upper trims
- Towing: 6,500 lb
- Stock Tire: P265/60R18
- Curb Weight: 5,128–5,199 lb
- Turning Circle: 38.1 ft (some spec sheets list 41.4 ft for '14+)
- Us Sales Peak: 32,509 (2021)

### Engineering
The GX 460 is a J150 Prado underneath, the same platform family as the 5th-gen 4Runner and the FJ Cruiser. A ladder frame carries independent front suspension and a solid rear axle. Full-time 4WD runs through an electronically shifted two-speed transfer case and a Torsen center differential that can be locked. Axle diffs stay open, with A-TRAC brake-based traction control filling in. KDSS, which hydraulically frees up the anti-roll bars for articulation, is standard. Higher trims add rear air springs with height control and adaptive dampers.
- Chassis: Ladder frame, J150 (Shared with the Prado 150 and the 5th-gen 4Runner.)
- Engine: 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 (301 hp and 329 lb-ft in US trim. Timing chain, not a belt.)
- Driveline: Full-time 4WD (Torsen center diff with a lock. Normally 40:60 front to rear, and up to 50:50 when the rear slips.)
- Suspension: KDSS standard (Hydraulically linked anti-roll bars. Get KDSS-specific front skids.)
- Rear: Solid axle (Rear air springs with height control (RAHC) and AVS dampers on '10–'13 Premium and '14-on Luxury.)
- Traction: A-TRAC, DAC, HAC (Crawl Control on some trims and retrofittable to others. No factory axle lockers.)

### Versions
- 2010–2013 · URJ150 · 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 · 301 hp / 329 lb-ft · Launch. Base and Premium trims, with KDSS standard. 'Don't Buy' and VSC recall in spring 2010. Secondary air pump failures common.
- 2012–2017 (China) · J150 · 1GR-FE 4.0 V6 · 271 hp / 281 lb-ft · GX 400, sold in China only.
- 2014–2019 · URJ150 · 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 · 301 hp / 329 lb-ft · Spindle grille and LED headlights. Base, Premium and Luxury trims.
- 2020–2021 · URJ150 · 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 · 301 hp / 329 lb-ft · Second facelift. Off-Road package with Crawl Control, MTS, a transmission cooler and a fuel-tank protector. Safety System+ standard.
- 2022–2023 · URJ150 · 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 · 301 hp / 329 lb-ft · New infotainment with CarPlay and Android Auto, plus a redesigned dash. 2022 Black Line edition.

### Year-by-year
- 2010: Launch with the 1UR-FE 4.6 V8 (301 hp), six-speed automatic and standard KDSS. In April 2010, Consumer Reports' 'Don't Buy' label led to a VSC software recall, and the label was lifted on May 7.
- 2010–2013: Secondary air-injection pump and valve failures are common; ClubLexus moderators call it a known 2010–13 problem. Confirm the parts were replaced under program ZLH. [avoid]
- 2014: First facelift: spindle grille, LED headlamps and LED DRLs, with a US price cut of $4,750. ClubLexus moderators say air-pump trouble is far less common from 2014 on. [buy]
- 2017: Second-row captain's chairs with the Luxury package.
- 2020: Second facelift. New Off-Road package with Crawl Control, Multi-Terrain Select, a transmission cooler, a fuel-tank protector and Multi-Terrain Monitor. Safety System+ is standard.
- 2022: New infotainment with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto plus a redesigned dash. Black Line edition.
- 2023: Final year. Eminent White Pearl added.
